chapters.title: Chapter 601
paragraphs: Repairs were underway at Ares Guild headquarters.
Inside the conference room, the mood was grim.
Some thirty men and women sat around a massive round table, their somber eyes fixed on the man speaking.
“...And that is why I called this emergency meeting.”
Vice President Park Daewon had barely finished when objections erupted from all sides.
“Well, well. They must think very little of us. And it’s a brat who isn’t even thirty.”
“His intentions couldn’t be more obvious. He means to swallow Ares whole.”
“No, hyung. Why would you call an emergency meeting at the request of an outsider who has no authority? Even if you are the Vice President, this is going too far.”
As the complaints came at him, Park wiped his half-bald forehead with a handkerchief.
Nearing sixty, he found the whole situation bewildering.
How on earth did it come to this?

He had distinguished himself in battle, but political infighting had never been his strength. Fortunately, he was the sort of man who made no enemies, and that had allowed him to keep his largely ceremonial position as Vice President.
Then, ten days ago, while taking a vacation ahead of his retirement, he had heard news he could hardly believe.
Ares Guild headquarters had been crushed by a single person, and Go Jun, the Vice Guild Master, had been murdered.
That can’t be true.
For the first ten minutes, at least, that was what Park had thought.

But every bit of it had been true. The impregnable fortress they had spent some thirty years building had fallen, and its newly appointed City Lord had lost his head before he had even settled into office.
And the retainers who had narrowly escaped the prosecutors’ office were voicing their grievances in unison.
“This is absurd! We don’t have to listen to such nonsense.”
“We created the name Ares, and we were the ones who protected it. What right does some outsider—some bloody brat who still doesn’t know how the world works—have to interfere?”
“Vice President Park, this really isn’t right!”
Park Daewon silently took a long drink from his glass of water.

Everyone gathered here had spent at least ten years with Ares Guild; some had been with it for more than thirty. Most of those who held real power in the Guild had been summoned by the prosecutors’ office, but the executives in this room were far from powerless.
...But we can’t ignore him, either.
Park Daewon knew all about Choi Minwoo.

No, he couldn’t not know. Cheon Taemin’s private life and family relationships had been protected with the utmost care, but things were different for the few people classified as his close associates. Park, a founding member of the Guild, was one of them.
I first saw him at his doljabi. The funeral was the last time...wasn’t it?
The child who had slowly faded from his memory had grown up and returned to reclaim what he had lost long ago.

Park had spent his life going along with whatever happened around him, but this troubled him. He knew it was only a shallow sense of guilt for turning away from Choi Minwoo when the boy had been shut out of the Guild entirely.
What should I do?
While Park Daewon was lost in thought, a short, powerful voice rang through the noisy conference room.
“I was going to see how far you’d take this, but it’s getting more ridiculous by the minute. I can’t listen to any more.”
A chill silence fell over the conference room. Eyes widened, and every gaze turned toward the speaker.
“Managing Director Kim, what kind of outrageous statement was that?”
“Managing Director, my ass. Hey, Kim Gwangpil! What the hell are you talking about?”
The silence broke into angry shouts. Managing Director Kim shrugged his broad shoulders.
“Am I wrong? I called it ridiculous because it is. And Executive Director Baek, watch your language. I may be your junior, but I don’t care to be spoken to like that.”
“Just you wait, you traitorous bastard...”
Kim’s thick eyebrows twitched.
“What did you call me?”
“A traitor, you bastard! If it weren’t for traitors like you, we wouldn’t be in this goddamn mess!”
“Wasn’t it the people on Executive Director Baek’s side who acted like animals? We can figure that out simply by seeing who’s in the detention center right now.”
“What?”

“You seemed awfully bothered that a few executives and I joined Jin Taekyung. But in the end, what kind of shit was the Vice Guild Master—no, what was that man Go Jun—up to? Or did you have a hand in it too, Executive Director Baek?”
“You—you bastard...!”
“Hey, Managing Director Kim! Watch your mouth!”
“You’re the ones who need to watch your mouths!”
“Exactly!”
“How dare you!”
The room split into two factions, furious shouts flying back and forth. Then Park Daewon, who had remained silent, spoke up.
“Strictly speaking, he isn’t an outsider.”
The executives stopped short.
“What?”
“Vice President Park, what did you just...?”
“I’m talking about Choi Minwoo.”
Park slowly looked around at the thirty-odd executives.
“Isn’t he Guild Master Cheon Taemin’s only maternal grandson?”
He had touched on the one thing they had all been avoiding, and the room fell silent. Kim Gwangpil’s faction brightened at once. The faces of those who had spent the meeting complaining went ashen.
“B-but that’s only a rumor, isn’t it?”
“Th-that’s right, hyung. No one’s confirmed it.”
Word of Choi Minwoo’s identity had been spreading quietly since the Small Cataclysm. They weren’t so much ignorant as pretending to be.
Park, at least, had no need to pretend.
“No. I’m certain. Unless my memory fails me, he is that person’s maternal grandson. And...”
Before anyone could object, Park set his smartphone on the table.
“It seems he’s decided to tell the world himself.”
“What do you mean...?”
“Argue with each other all you like, but you should have checked what was happening outside. Especially since you barred the secretaries you brought from coming in. Wouldn’t you agree?”
Several executives seemed to realize what he meant. They hurriedly pulled out their phones.
Within a minute, startled gasps sounded around the room. A reporter’s urgent voice played from dozens of speakers.
“M-Mr. Choi Minwoo! Could you tell us your maternal grandfather’s full name once more?”
Another voice followed, filling the conference room.
“The Cheon character, the Tae character, and the Min character. Cheon Taemin. He is my maternal grandfather.”
The ceaseless camera flashes and the surrounding murmur vanished in an instant, both at the press conference shown in the video and inside the conference room.
Everyone had suspected it. But hearing that suspicion confirmed and announced to the world had an impact none of them had imagined.
All the more so when it concerned the only blood relative of Cheon Taemin, a man about whom everything was shrouded in mystery.
At the same moment, everyone in the room understood.
He’s finally drawn his sword.

After more than twenty years in what had amounted to exile, the royal grandson had returned. At the perfect moment, he had drawn the sharpest blade he possessed to reclaim what he had lost by his own strength.
The question was where he would swing it—and at whom.
Gulp.
No one could bring themselves to speak easily. As time passed in an atmosphere where an invisible thread of tension had been pulled taut, the room filled with faint whispers.
Then—
Beep.
Every head turned at the faint electronic sound. It had come from the clock on the conference room wall.
The current time shone in red LEDs, like a warning.
Six o’clock.
The time they had gathered for. The time someone was due to arrive.
Step. Step.
Everyone heard shoes crossing the hallway outside the door, and without realizing it, they reflexively rose from their seats.
And then...
Click.
The door opened smoothly, revealing two people.
“You’re all here early.”
“Oh, they fixed this place already. I think I broke it last time.”
The occupying force had arrived: one polite, one rude, and neither to be avoided.
When I was little, my father used to tell me, “Son, once a man draws his sword, he has to cut at least a radish.”
By that measure, Team Leader Choi was a man among men. He had come to cut up Ares Guild, not a radish.
Come to think of it, I had already cut it down once myself. But still.
“Nice to meet you. I’m Choi Minwoo.”
Team Leader Choi gave a polite bow, and the Ares Guild executives standing around the table awkwardly returned it.

Some looked as if the world would end in three seconds. Others wore broad smiles. I recognized them: they were the executives from Song Cheonwoo’s faction who had sided with me when I attacked headquarters.
One person was harder to read.
The elderly middle-aged man seated at the head of the table was Vice President Park Daewon.
“Welcome, Team Leader Choi Minwoo.”
Team Leader Choi studied his conflicted expression, then nodded.
“I hope I’m not late. The press conference ran longer than I expected. I apologize for keeping you waiting.”
Judging by their faces, they’d all watched the live broadcast. About half of them didn’t seem to think they’d got their money’s worth from the license fee.
“Not at all. Before we begin, please have a seat...”
“That won’t be necessary.”
Team Leader Choi gently stopped Park from offering him a place.
“This won’t take long. And since the others still think of me as an outsider, I wouldn’t want to make them uncomfortable by drawing it out.”
“...Ahem.”
Awkward coughs came from around the table. Team Leader Choi paid them no mind as he looked over the room.
“I see five empty seats. Where are the three advisers and the directors of the United States and France branches?”
A middle-aged man with a prickly appearance answered with an uncomfortable expression.
“You seem very interested in our people.”
“I have a good memory, Executive Director Baek.”
Baek fell silent. One of the executives who had sided with me ten days ago answered promptly.
“They didn’t come.”
“Something unavoidable must have kept them away. Is that right?”
“The three advisers cited illness. As I understand it, the two branch directors refused to attend.”
“I specifically told them to attend. It seems my wishes weren’t conveyed properly.”
Team Leader Choi muttered this calmly, and Executive Director Baek spoke again.
“This isn’t an official meeting. We gathered at an outsider’s request. No one was obliged to attend, even if that outsider...”
After hesitating for a moment, he continued in a distinctly quieter voice.
“...is that person’s maternal grandson.”
“You’re right.”
Team Leader Choi nodded in agreement, then took a small note from inside his clothes and handed it over.
“What’s this?”
“A prescription for the advisers who are ill. Ah, the other two branch directors will receive something other than a prescription.”
I had a feeling the advisers who’d used illness as an excuse would recover the moment they saw that note. It listed the crimes they’d committed that hadn’t come to light yet.
Baek read it and swallowed hard.
“Th-this...”
“You don’t look well yourself, Executive Director Baek. Would you like a prescription too?”
“N-no! What are you talking about? I’m fine!”
I stood with my arms crossed, watching the situation, and muttered.
“Wasn’t that ‘I’m fine’ a bit too casual?”
“I—I’m quite well.”
One Hundred and One Ways to Kill Without a Sound, by Jin Taekyung.
“I—I’m perfectly fine, sir.”
Hmm. The man could take a hint. I glanced at him as he stood there swallowing nervously, then turned to Team Leader Choi.
“Can’t we sit down and talk? My legs hurt.”
“Well, there isn’t really a suitable seat...”
I helpfully pointed toward the head of the table before he could finish.
“There. That one’s empty.”
“Oh, I see. But would it be all right for me to sit there?”
“Let’s put it to a vote. Majority rules. Anyone opposed? Hands?”
No one raised a hand.

chapters.title: Chapter 602
paragraphs: A whip could be an effective way to make someone do what you wanted. It could also make them resent you. Team Leader Choi knew exactly how to use the one in his hand.
“Director Hong.”
From his seat at the head of the table, Team Leader Choi called on one of the youngest executives. Hong answered, his face tense.
“Yes, yes.”
“I’ve heard a great deal about you, Director Hong. They say you’re exceptionally capable.”
“Oh, no. I’ve just been lucky...”
“Luck alone doesn’t make someone an Ares Guild executive. Especially not at your age. Wouldn’t you agree?”

Team Leader Choi’s tone and voice were gentle, but an unmistakable anxiety appeared on Director Hong’s face. And there was bound to be a reason why Team Leader Choi had singled out one person from among dozens of executives.
“I grew up overseas, so it was hard to fit in at first. But people live there too, after all. One by one, I made friends.”
Exiled or not, he was still the royal grandson. Team Leader Choi had lived a life worlds apart from that of an ordinary guy like me. His connections went further than I could imagine.
“Some of those friends get in touch now and then with news. I’ve heard some interesting things about you too, Director Hong.”
“...Have you?”
“Yes. Nothing but praise. The same goes for the rest of you, of course.”
Each time Team Leader Choi’s calm gaze moved, the executive who met it flinched as if burned. None of them was stupid enough to take his words at face value.
Leave water standing long enough and it rots.
Ares Guild was one of the largest organizations in the world. An executive position there came with astronomical wealth and prestige.

How many people at this table were clean as fresh water? They hadn’t avoided a summons from the prosecutors’ office because they were spotless. They were just clean enough to pass for third-grade water.
The sewage, and those with filth floating in them, were already having a reunion in the detention center.
“Are you feeling unwell? You’re breaking out in a cold sweat.”
Director Hong wiped his forehead. “Oh, no. It’s just a little hot.”
“There must be a problem with the temperature-control Magic. You should have it fixed.”

Magic kept the conference room at a comfortable temperature, but half the executives were breathing as if they’d stepped into a steam room. They had all seen the whip tucked up Team Leader Choi’s sleeve. He didn’t have to swing it. A glimpse was enough to put pressure on them.
There was, of course, an exception.
“I can’t listen to any more of this.”
The speaker was a middle-aged man with irritable eyes and a sparse white beard. He tapped thick knuckles on the round table.
“Are you seriously threatening us?”
“You’re Director Kim, in charge of the Asian region.”
Team Leader Choi rubbed his chin. “Is that how it feels?”
“What if it did?”
“I won’t deny it. It’s true.”
“What?”
“I said it’s true. I’m threatening you, and I intend to make Ares Guild mine.”
He added gently, “With everyone’s consent, of course. Legally.”
“A lizard thinks it can swallow a dinosaur.”
Director Kim looked between Team Leader Choi and me and gave a short laugh.
“You two are young, and it shows. Do you think Ares Guild is a joke?”
I nodded, looking interested. “Hmm. A little?”
That seemed to leave him at a loss. After a brief silence, he went on.
“Headquarters fell. That doesn’t mean the whole of Ares Guild is helpless. No matter how strong you are, do you think you can take on all of us?”
He had a point. Ares Guild had branches all over the world, and the forces at headquarters were only a fraction of its strength. Even I couldn’t subdue them all on my own.
But...
“So what?”
At my question, bewilderment flashed across Director Kim’s face.
“What?”
“What, asshole?”
“Asshole?”
“You fucking bastard, I ought to—”
What the hell is this guy doing? His face said it all.
I raised my fist. Director Kim instinctively edged his chair back and blinked.
“What... what is this?”
“What does it look like? I’m about to fuck you up.”
“You’re going to use force? Now? Here?”
“Should I use my brains instead? It’s depressing enough how little I’ve got to work with.”
“But... that would be illegal.”
“Was it legal when I took Go Jun’s head off ten days ago?”
“Something will work out. I’ve already sent a few people to the grave. Who’s going to complain if I add one more? Right?”
Team Leader Choi smacked his lips. “This is a different matter. Someone might complain.”
“Things have been going pretty well for me lately, but even I couldn’t stay out of prison, could I?”
“That’s right. But given how favorable the public image and public opinion surrounding Mr. Jin Taekyung are at present, if things go well, you might be able to settle for a few years.”
“Right. What if I was drunk?”
“Are you a genius? That would cut the sentence considerably.”
“Come to think of it, I’ve been through so much lately that I might have diminished mental capacity.”
“Oh, you could even aim for a suspended sentence.”
What a wonderful country. Get drunk, claim diminished mental capacity, and they’d throw in a generous sentence reduction.
The man listening to our hopeful discussion had gone ashen.
“You... you lunatics.”
“I thought you knew. You didn’t know I was a lunatic?”
“Then watch yourself. We’re trying to do this the nice way. Why are you the only one making trouble?”
It was only talk, of course.

What mattered was how it sounded to him. I was the madman who had gone berserk, smashed up Ares Guild headquarters, and killed people without a thought for the consequences. Right now, even a joke from me would sound like a threat.
If the whip doesn’t work, you need one hell of a strong whip.
The one man who had come close to openly dissenting pressed his lips together. Vice President Park Daewon, who had been watching quietly, spoke up.
“I understand what the two of you want. As for Team Leader Choi Minwoo returning to Ares Guild... I support it in my capacity as Vice President.”
“V-Vice President.”
“Why? Is there a problem?”
“Well, that...”
Startled voices came from around the table. But the tide had turned, and Team Leader Choi offered them the carrot he had prepared.
“If the rest of you accept Vice President Park Daewon’s opinion, Ares Guild will stabilize quickly. The vacancies created by this incident will soon be filled as well.”
“...What are you saying?”
“Whatever has happened up to now, I have no intention of discounting your abilities. Once things settle down, there will be major personnel changes.”
I could practically see the rabbits’ ears perk up as they recognized the carrot.
If Ares Guild changed hands, its existing executives had the most to lose. Take away that worry and promise them promotions instead, and things looked very different.
No reason to refuse.
Besides, Team Leader Choi had nothing to disqualify him. Quite the opposite. He was more than qualified, which was why he could speak with such quiet confidence.
“I’ll put everything that has happened until now behind me. I’ll quickly stabilize the Guild, restore its tarnished image, and use this incident as a stepping stone to make it grow even larger.”
No one questioned him now. It wasn’t only the carrot. They knew what Team Leader Choi could do.

In barely half a year, he had brought Peace Guild to where it stood today. I’d played a key role in that, sure. But without his eye for people, his ability to run an organization, and his political skill, there would be no Peace Guild as it was now.
And there was something else.
He’s Cheon Taemin’s only blood descendant.
Dynasties had vanished from this country long ago, but Cheon Taemin’s name belonged to the realm of the divine.
The bloodline of the man who saved humanity carried its own power and nobility. No chaebol group, however wealthy, and no dynasty that had ever existed could claim to stand above Team Leader Choi.
And a title like that was bound to carry tremendous influence, especially within Ares Guild.
“Hmm.”

Low groans rose from various parts of the conference room. They knew it too. Lee Jungryong and Go Jun had been nothing more than usurpers, while Team Leader Choi—with undeniable legitimacy and ability—was the one suited to become the new City Lord.
Scrape.

The sound of chairs broke the silence. More than ten executives stood. They had been in the same boat since ten days ago, and they bowed respectfully to Team Leader Choi without hesitation, as though they had been waiting for this moment.
The tide was with us now. The others had seen the whip and the carrot. It was time to choose.
One by one, the watching executives rose.
Scrape. Scrape.
Amid the sounds of shifting chairs, I sent a Sound Transmission to the last two holdouts.
—Oh, for fuck’s sake...
Executive Director Baek and Director Kim shuddered as though they’d been electrocuted. Then they got to their feet on trembling legs and bowed.
Only one executive remained seated.
Vice President Park Daewon.
Under the gazes of Team Leader Choi and me, he finally rose quietly from his seat. An aged voice slipped through his dry lips.
“Do you know I’ll be retiring soon?”
Team Leader Choi calmly nodded, and Vice President Park Daewon muttered softly.
“Then this will be my last task.”
“If you wish, I can arrange for you to stay longer.”
“No. I’m sorry I failed to look after you all these years... and thank you for coming back.”
Of everyone in the room, Park had been with Ares Guild the longest. That also meant he had turned away from Team Leader Choi the longest.
He looked at Team Leader Choi, conflicting emotions plain on his face, then bowed respectfully. His next words brought it all to an end.
“I’ll convene an official board meeting, Young Master.”
A glint passed through Team Leader Choi’s eyes.
Surrounded by some thirty retainers, he was already the City Lord in all but name.

sentences.text: A whip could be an effective way to make someone do what you wanted.
It could also make them resent you.
Team Leader Choi knew exactly how to use the one in his hand.
“Director Hong.”
From his seat at the head of the table, Team Leader Choi called on one of the youngest executives.
Hong answered, his face tense.
“Yes, yes.”
“I’ve heard a great deal about you, Director Hong.
They say you’re exceptionally capable.”
“Oh, no.
I’ve just been lucky...”
“Luck alone doesn’t make someone an Ares Guild executive.
Especially not at your age.
Wouldn’t you agree?”
Team Leader Choi’s tone and voice were gentle, but an unmistakable anxiety appeared on Director Hong’s face.
And there was bound to be a reason why Team Leader Choi had singled out one person from among dozens of executives.
“I grew up overseas, so it was hard to fit in at first.
But people live there too, after all.
One by one, I made friends.”
Exiled or not, he was still the royal grandson.
Team Leader Choi had lived a life worlds apart from that of an ordinary guy like me.
His connections went further than I could imagine.
“Some of those friends get in touch now and then with news.
I’ve heard some interesting things about you too, Director Hong.”
“...Have you?”
“Yes.
Nothing but praise.
The same goes for the rest of you, of course.”
Each time Team Leader Choi’s calm gaze moved, the executive who met it flinched as if burned.
None of them was stupid enough to take his words at face value.
Leave water standing long enough and it rots.
Ares Guild was one of the largest organizations in the world.
An executive position there came with astronomical wealth and prestige.
How many people at this table were clean as fresh water?
They hadn’t avoided a summons from the prosecutors’ office because they were spotless.
They were just clean enough to pass for third-grade water.
The sewage, and those with filth floating in them, were already having a reunion in the detention center.
“Are you feeling unwell?
You’re breaking out in a cold sweat.”
Director Hong wiped his forehead.
“Oh, no.
It’s just a little hot.”
“There must be a problem with the temperature-control Magic.
You should have it fixed.”
Magic kept the conference room at a comfortable temperature, but half the executives were breathing as if they’d stepped into a steam room.
They had all seen the whip tucked up Team Leader Choi’s sleeve.
He didn’t have to swing it.
A glimpse was enough to put pressure on them.
There was, of course, an exception.
“I can’t listen to any more of this.”
The speaker was a middle-aged man with irritable eyes and a sparse white beard.
He tapped thick knuckles on the round table.
“Are you seriously threatening us?”
“You’re Director Kim, in charge of the Asian region.”
Team Leader Choi rubbed his chin.
“Is that how it feels?”
“What if it did?”
“I won’t deny it.
It’s true.”
“What?”
“I said it’s true.
I’m threatening you, and I intend to make Ares Guild mine.”
He added gently, “With everyone’s consent, of course.
Legally.”
“A lizard thinks it can swallow a dinosaur.”
Director Kim looked between Team Leader Choi and me and gave a short laugh.
“You two are young, and it shows.
Do you think Ares Guild is a joke?”
I nodded, looking interested.
“Hmm.
A little?”
That seemed to leave him at a loss.
After a brief silence, he went on.
“Headquarters fell.
That doesn’t mean the whole of Ares Guild is helpless.
No matter how strong you are, do you think you can take on all of us?”
He had a point.
Ares Guild had branches all over the world, and the forces at headquarters were only a fraction of its strength.
Even I couldn’t subdue them all on my own.
But...
“So what?”
At my question, bewilderment flashed across Director Kim’s face.
“What?”
“What, asshole?”
“Asshole?”
“You fucking bastard, I ought to—”
What the hell is this guy doing?
His face said it all.
I raised my fist.
Director Kim instinctively edged his chair back and blinked.
“What... what is this?”
“What does it look like?
I’m about to fuck you up.”
“You’re going to use force?
Now?
Here?”
“Should I use my brains instead?
It’s depressing enough how little I’ve got to work with.”
“But... that would be illegal.”
“Was it legal when I took Go Jun’s head off ten days ago?”
“Something will work out.
I’ve already sent a few people to the grave.
Who’s going to complain if I add one more?
Right?”
Team Leader Choi smacked his lips.
“This is a different matter.
Someone might complain.”
“Things have been going pretty well for me lately, but even I couldn’t stay out of prison, could I?”
“That’s right.
But given how favorable the public image and public opinion surrounding Mr.
Jin Taekyung are at present, if things go well, you might be able to settle for a few years.”
“Right.
What if I was drunk?”
“Are you a genius?
That would cut the sentence considerably.”
“Come to think of it, I’ve been through so much lately that I might have diminished mental capacity.”
“Oh, you could even aim for a suspended sentence.”
What a wonderful country.
Get drunk, claim diminished mental capacity, and they’d throw in a generous sentence reduction.
The man listening to our hopeful discussion had gone ashen.
“You... you lunatics.”
“I thought you knew.
You didn’t know I was a lunatic?”
“Then watch yourself.
We’re trying to do this the nice way.
Why are you the only one making trouble?”
It was only talk, of course.
What mattered was how it sounded to him.
I was the madman who had gone berserk, smashed up Ares Guild headquarters, and killed people without a thought for the consequences.
Right now, even a joke from me would sound like a threat.
If the whip doesn’t work, you need one hell of a strong whip.
The one man who had come close to openly dissenting pressed his lips together.
Vice President Park Daewon, who had been watching quietly, spoke up.
“I understand what the two of you want.
As for Team Leader Choi Minwoo returning to Ares Guild...
I support it in my capacity as Vice President.”
“V-Vice President.”
“Why?
Is there a problem?”
“Well, that...”
Startled voices came from around the table.
But the tide had turned, and Team Leader Choi offered them the carrot he had prepared.

The vacancies created by this incident will soon be filled as well.”

Once things settle down, there will be major personnel changes.”

If Ares Guild changed hands, its existing executives had the most to lose.

chapters.title: Chapter 603
paragraphs: It’s over.
Thud.
Baek Hanseong, the occupant of the Phoenix Chair, gave a bitter smile as he set down the report.

Submitted personally by the director of the NIS, it contained a complete account of Choi Minwoo’s movements the day before: the press conference held immediately after the national funeral, and the mood inside Ares Guild during its emergency meeting.
I didn’t expect him to move this quickly.
Baek had already known the secret of Choi Minwoo’s birth. He simply hadn’t expected Minwoo to reveal it to everyone at such a perfect moment.
No. More accurately, he hadn’t expected Ares Guild’s executives to accept a new City Lord so easily.
That’s how much Cheon Taemin’s bloodline means to them.

Cheon Taemin was a hero who symbolized humanity itself. No matter how much filth the recent incidents had smeared across Ares Guild, the power of his name remained undiminished. No media outlet or celebrity dared touch a man they regarded as sacrosanct.
But that wasn’t the only reason Choi Minwoo had been able to build Peace Guild into what it was today and secure the support of Ares Guild’s executives.
Jin Taekyung.
Fearless, approachable, devoted. A young hero drawing closer, step by step, to Cheon Taemin’s once-unrivaled reputation.
As long as he stood beside Choi Minwoo, nothing could stop the two of them. Not even if the country’s most powerful politicians, chaebol corporations, and major Guilds joined forces.
“Mr. President.”
Baek looked up at his chief secretary’s voice.
“What is it?”
“The Guild Association is asking to see you.”
Just what he least wanted to hear.

Representing the country’s ten largest Guilds, the association had been watching Ares Guild for an opening ever since the Go Jun incident. They had cooperated so readily with the government not out of any desire for justice or a cleaner society, but to pick through the fallen castle’s ruins for treasure.
And they would have, if not for Choi Minwoo.
Minwoo was young, capable, and had legitimacy on his side. If he became Vice Guild Master, Ares Guild would rebuild. His and Jin Taekyung’s good reputations could wash the filth from its name.
Opposition from the Guild Association was only to be expected. The problem was that they wanted Baek to reward their contributions and repay their favors.
Baek Hanseong muttered bitterly, “Not one of them knows how to behave.”
“Excuse me?”
“Nothing. Put the matter of the Guild Association on hold for now.”
“Mr. President, I’m sorry to say this, but their requests have been coming in without pause...”
“I said put it on hold.”
The chief secretary flinched at his quiet voice, bowed, and left.
Once the door closed, Baek rubbed his tired eyes. One problem after another had worn him down, body and mind. He even found himself craving the cigarettes he had given up after his election.
But nicotine and tar weren’t what he needed. He needed a solution—a way to untangle the problems knotted together like the Gordian knot of myth.
And the quickest, surest place to find one wasn’t the Blue House.
Is this really the only way?
With a heavy heart, Baek pressed the button beneath his chair. Barely ten seconds later, the security officers waiting in the next room hurried in and bowed.
“I was thinking of getting some fresh air. Would that be all right?”
The head of the Presidential Security Service answered calmly. “Of course, Mr. President. Do you have a destination in mind?”
A destination.
Baek looked out the window.
“Peace Guild. Let’s go to Peace Guild.”
I’d been wondering why the Guild was so quiet today. The moment I left the training room at Team Leader Choi’s summons and stepped inside, I found out.
“You’re here, Hunter Jin Taekyung.”
“...Why are you here again?”
Baek Hanseong gave my heartfelt question a weary smile.
“I’ve been asking myself the same thing. Still, it’s good to see you again after so long.”
“Sure.”
I wasn’t sure fifteen days counted as so long, but I pulled out a chair and sat down. Baek was turning a cigarette over in his fingers, so I added, “This is a no-smoking area.”
“I know. I quit a year ago.”
He rubbed at the dark circles beneath his eyes. “But lately... I’ve been wondering whether I should start again.”
He must have had a rough time. He looked ten years older than when I’d last seen him.
I gave him a sympathetic look and patted his shoulder.
“I get that, but I’m telling you, this is a no-smoking area.”
“So what brings you here?”

The question was a formality. The middle-aged man in front of me was the President. He wasn’t the guy from the neighborhood bakery, free to drop by whenever he liked. There weren’t many reasons for him to come in person, especially now.
Sure enough, Baek gave a humorless little laugh.
“I think you both already know.”
Team Leader Choi spoke calmly. “The Guild Association’s opposition must be fierce.”
“It isn’t only the Guild Association. But the politicians and business leaders have chosen to stand back for now.”
“They’ll move once they see which way the scales tip.”
“Exactly. The Guild industry has the most at stake here.” Baek sighed. “As you know, they’re afraid of another Ares Guild.”

Ares Guild was an undisputed predator. In Korea especially, it had wielded overwhelming influence since its founding. Saying it held more power than the Blue House would hardly have been an exaggeration.

“The Guild Association won’t back down easily,” Baek continued. “An opportunity like this may never come again. They want to weaken Ares Guild through this incident and take some of its interests as their reward.”
“But then Team Leader Choi held a press conference and met with Ares Guild’s leadership...”
“That must put you in a difficult position.”
“Frankly, yes. They’ve been hounding me.”
I’d been listening in silence, but I cut in. “You can be more honest than that.”
“What do you mean?”
“You’re worried too, aren’t you, Mr. President? About a second Ares Guild. No—about a second Lee Jungryong.”
“Our Peace Guild is growing at a terrifying pace even as we speak. And now Ares Guild is going to bow before Team Leader Choi as well? If that happens, the game is completely over.”

A corporation’s strength came from its size and capital. A Guild’s came from its Hunters. By that measure, Peace Guild already had standing and fighting strength far beyond the country’s ten largest Guilds.
It had me and my overwhelming power. It had Team Leader Choi, Cheon Taemin’s only blood descendant.
And if we add Ares Guild to that?
Team Leader Choi would wield enormous power. He’d go from the only challenger capable of bringing Ares Guild down to a power no one could touch.
“Hmm.”
Baek let out a low hum. I snapped my fingers.
Tap. Fwoosh.
A flame of Samadhi True Fire flickered into being. Baek stared at it in surprise. When I nodded, he understood and put the cigarette between his lips.
Sizzle. Hoo.

White smoke poured out with his breath. Perhaps because it had been so long since he had smoked, he leaned back against the sofa and closed his eyes before suddenly removing the cigarette from his lips.
“Hunter Jin Taekyung is right. I’m more worried about a second Lee Jungryong than a second Ares Guild.”
Team Leader Choi brushed the smoke aside with one hand.
“That’s disappointing. I didn’t know you thought of me that way, Mr. President.”
“Anyone can change. Politics taught me that.”
“But you came here yourself today. You even postponed your meeting with the Guild Association.”
“Why?”
After a moment’s silence, Baek answered with difficulty.
“Because I wanted to believe the two of you were different.”
His subdued gaze rested on Team Leader Choi and me.
“What matters most isn’t how strong or sharp a weapon is. It’s who holds it.”
He had a point. A cheap box cutter from a stationery store was a weapon in a criminal’s hand. A magnificent sword made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron was a kitchen knife in a master chef’s.
And the Team Leader Choi I knew was capable and wise. He wasn’t the sort of man to swing a weapon carelessly just because it was in his hand.
“Then I can put your worries to rest,” Team Leader Choi said quietly.
Baek’s eyes lit up. “You mean...?”
“Trust me. I’ll use my influence and power fairly and justly, and I’ll hand over a share of the interests—enough to satisfy the Guild Association. If you like, I’ll put it in writing.”
“But now that I’ve given you the answer you wanted, I’d like a promise from you in return.”
Baek blinked at the unexpected offer, then leaned forward. “What is it?”
“I don’t want any more noise surrounding my actions from now on. Resolve the problem with the Guild Association, and stop the ongoing field investigation at Ares Guild headquarters.”
It was an alliance founded on trust, but it was a deal too. Baek was a seasoned politician. He nodded without much hesitation.
“If you keep your word, that won’t be difficult.”
“Then it’s settled. Nice and clean.”
As though they had planned it in advance, the two men rose from their seats at the same time and extended their hands.
Just as they were about to shake, Baek turned to me.
“Hunter Jin Taekyung. May I ask one last question?”
“Me? Sure.”
“Your request to stop the investigation at Ares Guild headquarters... Is it connected to the visit at the special detention center the other day?”
“Ah.”
I’d figured a report would reach him. Sure enough.
My eyes met Team Leader Choi’s. I read his assent there and shrugged.
“Yes.”
“Huh. The investigators must have missed something.”
“Why? Going to send them back in?”
“I am curious what Go Se-won was hiding, but... if I were that stupid, I would never have made it this far.”
With that politician’s answer, Baek smiled and took Team Leader Choi’s hand.
“I hope we continue to get along.”
“I look forward to working with you, Mr. President.”
The newly formed super-Guild and the government had forged a firm partnership.
And the last obstacle between us and Ares Guild was gone.
“C-could you say that again?”
“Cheon. Tae as in Crown Prince, and Min. Cheon Taemin. That’s my maternal grandfather’s name.”
On the day of the joint national funeral for the victims, the reporters were wrapping up their coverage when a bombshell dropped on them.
They could hardly process it. Neither could anyone else, apart from the handful of people who had known in advance.
Cheon Taemin. The immortal hero shrouded in mystery for more than twenty years.
His only blood descendant, who had remained out of sight even as turmoil engulfed Ares Guild, had appeared before the cameras.
Naturally, media outlets in Korea and around the world erupted at once.
[Peace Guild Team Leader Choi Minwoo: “My Maternal Grandfather Is Cheon Taemin.”]
[Press Conference Stunned. Ten Seconds of Silence.]
[Foreign Media in Uproar: Who Is Choi, Descendant of a Living Legend?]
[Truth or Lie? Debate Erupts over Choi Minwoo’s Shocking Statement.]
[Peace Guild Spokesperson: “Choi Minwoo Confirmed as Peace Guild’s New Guild Master.”]
[Ares Guild Official: “Board Meeting Called Regarding Choi Minwoo. Appointment as New Vice Guild Master Likely.”]
[Peace Guild’s New Captain—and Ares Guild Comes Calling?]
[KakaoPage Web-Novel Reader Ttolseu Comments on Chapter 599 of a Certain Novel: “Choi Minwoo’s a diehard Baek fan. I’ll go read the fun Gigant Rider instead.” Author’s Response: “?”]
All four of Korea’s major morning papers gave Choi Minwoo extensive coverage, as did the foreign press. Nonsense had even reached web-fiction platforms. That alone showed the scale of the uproar.
For a short while, people argued over whether his claim was true. Then Go Se-won, who knew Ares Guild’s inner workings better than anyone, and Magic Johnson spoke up.
[Former Head of Security Go Se-won: “Choi Minwoo’s Statement Is True. He Lost His Parents as a Child and Was Shut Out of Ares Guild for More Than Twenty Years.”]

[American Grand Mage Magic Johnson: “He Is Definitely Cheon Taemin’s Maternal Grandson. He Is Also a Very Capable and Charming Man Who Built Peace Guild into What It Is Today. By the Way, Where Is Kanghee Lee? Is He in the Shower?”]
[Former U.S. President Joseph Biden: “I Think So, If I Remember Right. Actually, I’m Not Sure.”]
[Prince Felix of the United Kingdom, on Hearing the News: “What The Fuk...” Royal Household Requests Interview Be Stopped.]
The finishing touch was the Blue House’s announcement confirming Choi Minwoo’s identity and declaring its support, followed by the results of Ares Guild’s official board meeting the next day.
[Ares Guild Elects Choi Minwoo, Current Peace Guild Master, as New Vice Guild Master. “Board Vote Unanimous.”]
[Choi Minwoo: Young Power Broker Now at the Helm of Two Major Guilds.]
[Guild Association Offers “Sincere Congratulations,” Contrary to Experts’ Predictions of Opposition.]
[Immortal Hero Still Nowhere to Be Seen.]
[Overseas Reaction: “Where Is Slayer?”]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung?”
At the voice in my ear, I looked up from my phone. The face I’d seen in countless article photos was right in front of me.
Now Ares Guild’s new captain, welcomed with applause and cheers, Team Leader Choi regarded me calmly.
“What are you looking at?”
“Articles about you. Should I still call you Team Leader Choi? Or Guild Master now? Maybe Vice Guild Master? You’ve got a foot in each Guild. It’s confusing.”
“Whatever you’re comfortable with.”
“Hmm. How about Minwoo?”
“Ah... Guild Master Choi Minwoo would be fine.”
“That feels awkward. I’ll stick with Team Leader.”
Given his position and the people watching, Guild Master would have been the proper title. But he couldn’t refuse my suggestion. It was a hundred times better than Minwoo.
“...All right.”
Still looking uneasy, Team Leader Choi surveyed our surroundings.
The vast, devastated space had deliberately been left unrepaired for the investigation. We were in Area A, inside Ares Guild headquarters.
Though “formerly hidden” would be more accurate now.
I crossed the familiar hallway. I’d fought the mutated Go Jun here, and wreckage littered everywhere I looked and stepped.
Damn, it’s huge.
This wasn’t an orchard, but by my rough estimate, the place covered well over a thousand pyeong—more than thirty-five thousand square feet.
And Team Leader Choi and I had to comb through it.
Well, not just the two of us. Our third member wasn’t human.
“Come out, you bastard.”
Swoosh.
A human-shaped creature that wasn’t human emerged from my Inventory.
“Are my eyes playing tricks on me? I could’ve sworn you said you’d take me to a club. You promised drinking games with beautiful women.”
The Skeleton King looked aggrieved. I answered with complete confidence.
“We’re playing treasure hunt here.”
“Find it fast and I’ll really take you to a club. I swear on Hyuk Mujin’s balls.”
“You despicable human. I’ll trust you one last time. But who is Hyuk Mujin, and why do you keep wagering his balls?”
I casually ignored the Skeleton King’s question and gestured toward Team Leader Choi.
“You take that side. I’ll take this one. Bones can handle way over there.”
“The area you’ve assigned me seems rather large.”
“Team Leader, you’re hurting my feelings. If you don’t like it, quit. Is he our grandfather? He’s your grandfather.”
“That settles it. Understood.”
With the work divided, we got moving.
Three hours later, we met up again, all wearing grim expressions.
“Fuuuck... I can’t do this shit.”
“For some reason, the mana detector isn’t working. And it’s the genuine luxury model I bought at a Sotheby’s auction.”
“Human. Treasure hunt is boring as hell.”
Knowing how meticulous Lee Jungryong was, I’d expected the secret area to be hard to find. I hadn’t expected this.
No wonder the government investigators had come away empty-handed.
There isn’t even a reaction in the office. Could the information have been wrong?
But Go Se-won knew more about Ares Guild’s secrets than anyone left alive. With Lee Jungryong, Song Cheonwoo, and Go Jun dead, trusting him was our only...
“Huh?”
A thought flashed through my mind, and my eyes widened.
Team Leader Choi stopped thumping the mana detector with his fist. He and the Skeleton King both looked at me.
“What is it?”
“Oh. Did you remember a club with a great crowd?”
“No, wait. I think I know where to look.”
I quickly traced my memories of Area A: the fight with Go Jun, my first victory, and then...
When I came back, he was running away.
By then Go Jun had changed into a horrible mixture of human and monster. He’d definitely been fleeing.
The question was where he’d been going.
That’s the place. There’s something there I didn’t find.
Tap—whoosh!
I launched myself forward without another thought. Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King hurried after me as I shot ahead like the wind.
We’d searched the place several times already, but this time was different.
Swoosh.
A dead-end hallway. Several rooms.
I slowed and leaned close against the wall, heightening my Qi Sense. A System chime sounded, and a blue circle spread outward from me.
It swept the hallway and every room, but no notification appeared to tell me I’d found anything.
Fwoooooosh.
The System determined the range of my Qi Sense. I could perceive only what lay within it.
But was that really all?
Farther. Wider.
I steadied my breathing. The sounds around me receded, and internal energy rose from my dantian, lending strength to my Qi Sense.
And then, at the moment my Middle Dantian finally responded—
Fwoooooosh!
The blue circle, which had stopped expanding, surged outward. Beyond the space I could see, toward another space hidden from sight.
At the edge of its reach came the notification I’d been waiting for.
Ding.

sentences.text: It’s over.
Thud.
Baek Hanseong, the occupant of the Phoenix Chair, gave a bitter smile as he set down the report.

Submitted personally by the director of the NIS, it contained a complete account of Choi Minwoo’s movements the day before: the press conference held immediately after the national funeral, and the mood inside Ares Guild during its emergency meeting.
I didn’t expect him to move this quickly.
Baek had already known the secret of Choi Minwoo’s birth.
He simply hadn’t expected Minwoo to reveal it to everyone at such a perfect moment.
No.
More accurately, he hadn’t expected Ares Guild’s executives to accept a new City Lord so easily.
That’s how much Cheon Taemin’s bloodline means to them.
Cheon Taemin was a hero who symbolized humanity itself.
No matter how much filth the recent incidents had smeared across Ares Guild, the power of his name remained undiminished.
No media outlet or celebrity dared touch a man they regarded as sacrosanct.
But that wasn’t the only reason Choi Minwoo had been able to build Peace Guild into what it was today and secure the support of Ares Guild’s executives.
Jin Taekyung.
Fearless, approachable, devoted.
A young hero drawing closer, step by step, to Cheon Taemin’s once-unrivaled reputation.
As long as he stood beside Choi Minwoo, nothing could stop the two of them.
Not even if the country’s most powerful politicians, chaebol corporations, and major Guilds joined forces.
“Mr.
President.”
Baek looked up at his chief secretary’s voice.
“What is it?”
“The Guild Association is asking to see you.”
Just what he least wanted to hear.
Representing the country’s ten largest Guilds, the association had been watching Ares Guild for an opening ever since the Go Jun incident.
They had cooperated so readily with the government not out of any desire for justice or a cleaner society, but to pick through the fallen castle’s ruins for treasure.
And they would have, if not for Choi Minwoo.
Minwoo was young, capable, and had legitimacy on his side.
If he became Vice Guild Master, Ares Guild would rebuild.
His and Jin Taekyung’s good reputations could wash the filth from its name.
Opposition from the Guild Association was only to be expected.
The problem was that they wanted Baek to reward their contributions and repay their favors.
Baek Hanseong muttered bitterly, “Not one of them knows how to behave.”
“Excuse me?”
“Nothing.
Put the matter of the Guild Association on hold for now.”
“Mr.
President, I’m sorry to say this, but their requests have been coming in without pause...”
“I said put it on hold.”
The chief secretary flinched at his quiet voice, bowed, and left.
Once the door closed, Baek rubbed his tired eyes.
One problem after another had worn him down, body and mind.
He even found himself craving the cigarettes he had given up after his election.
But nicotine and tar weren’t what he needed.
He needed a solution—a way to untangle the problems knotted together like the Gordian knot of myth.
And the quickest, surest place to find one wasn’t the Blue House.
Is this really the only way?
With a heavy heart, Baek pressed the button beneath his chair.
Barely ten seconds later, the security officers waiting in the next room hurried in and bowed.
“I was thinking of getting some fresh air.
Would that be all right?”
The head of the Presidential Security Service answered calmly.
“Of course, Mr.
President.
Do you have a destination in mind?”
A destination.
Baek looked out the window.
“Peace Guild.
Let’s go to Peace Guild.”
I’d been wondering why the Guild was so quiet today.
The moment I left the training room at Team Leader Choi’s summons and stepped inside, I found out.
“You’re here, Hunter Jin Taekyung.”
“...Why are you here again?”
Baek Hanseong gave my heartfelt question a weary smile.
“I’ve been asking myself the same thing.
Still, it’s good to see you again after so long.”
“Sure.”
I wasn’t sure fifteen days counted as so long, but I pulled out a chair and sat down.
Baek was turning a cigarette over in his fingers, so I added, “This is a no-smoking area.”
“I know.
I quit a year ago.”
He rubbed at the dark circles beneath his eyes.
“But lately...
I’ve been wondering whether I should start again.”
He must have had a rough time.
He looked ten years older than when I’d last seen him.
I gave him a sympathetic look and patted his shoulder.
“I get that, but I’m telling you, this is a no-smoking area.”
“So what brings you here?”
The question was a formality.
The middle-aged man in front of me was the President.
He wasn’t the guy from the neighborhood bakery, free to drop by whenever he liked.
There weren’t many reasons for him to come in person, especially now.
Sure enough, Baek gave a humorless little laugh.
“I think you both already know.”
Team Leader Choi spoke calmly.
“The Guild Association’s opposition must be fierce.”
“It isn’t only the Guild Association.
But the politicians and business leaders have chosen to stand back for now.”
“They’ll move once they see which way the scales tip.”
“Exactly.
The Guild industry has the most at stake here.” Baek sighed.
“As you know, they’re afraid of another Ares Guild.”
Ares Guild was an undisputed predator.
In Korea especially, it had wielded overwhelming influence since its founding.
Saying it held more power than the Blue House would hardly have been an exaggeration.
“The Guild Association won’t back down easily,” Baek continued.
“An opportunity like this may never come again.
They want to weaken Ares Guild through this incident and take some of its interests as their reward.”
“But then Team Leader Choi held a press conference and met with Ares Guild’s leadership...”
“That must put you in a difficult position.”
“Frankly, yes.
They’ve been hounding me.”
I’d been listening in silence, but I cut in.
“You can be more honest than that.”
“What do you mean?”
“You’re worried too, aren’t you, Mr.
President?
About a second Ares Guild.
No—about a second Lee Jungryong.”
“Our Peace Guild is growing at a terrifying pace even as we speak.
And now Ares Guild is going to bow before Team Leader Choi as well?
If that happens, the game is completely over.”
A corporation’s strength came from its size and capital.
A Guild’s came from its Hunters.
By that measure, Peace Guild already had standing and fighting strength far beyond the country’s ten largest Guilds.
It had me and my overwhelming power.
It had Team Leader Choi, Cheon Taemin’s only blood descendant.
And if we add Ares Guild to that?
Team Leader Choi would wield enormous power.
He’d go from the only challenger capable of bringing Ares Guild down to a power no one could touch.
“Hmm.”
Baek let out a low hum.
I snapped my fingers.
Tap.
Fwoosh.
A flame of Samadhi True Fire flickered into being.
Baek stared at it in surprise.
When I nodded, he understood and put the cigarette between his lips.
Sizzle.
Hoo.
White smoke poured out with his breath.
Perhaps because it had been so long since he had smoked, he leaned back against the sofa and closed his eyes before suddenly removing the cigarette from his lips.
“Hunter Jin Taekyung is right.
I’m more worried about a second Lee Jungryong than a second Ares Guild.”
Team Leader Choi brushed the smoke aside with one hand.
“That’s disappointing.
I didn’t know you thought of me that way, Mr.
President.”
“Anyone can change.
Politics taught me that.”
“But you came here yourself today.
You even postponed your meeting with the Guild Association.”
“Why?”
After a moment’s silence, Baek answered with difficulty.
“Because I wanted to believe the two of you were different.”
His subdued gaze rested on Team Leader Choi and me.
“What matters most isn’t how strong or sharp a weapon is.
It’s who holds it.”
He had a point.
A cheap box cutter from a stationery store was a weapon in a criminal’s hand.
A magnificent sword made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron was a kitchen knife in a master chef’s.
And the Team Leader Choi I knew was capable and wise.
He wasn’t the sort of man to swing a weapon carelessly just because it was in his hand.
“Then I can put your worries to rest,” Team Leader Choi said quietly.
Baek’s eyes lit up.
“You mean...?”
“Trust me.
I’ll use my influence and power fairly and justly, and I’ll hand over a share of the interests—enough to satisfy the Guild Association.
If you like, I’ll put it in writing.”
“But now that I’ve given you the answer you wanted, I’d like a promise from you in return.”
Baek blinked at the unexpected offer, then leaned forward.
“What is it?”
“I don’t want any more noise surrounding my actions from now on.
Resolve the problem with the Guild Association, and stop the ongoing field investigation at Ares Guild headquarters.”
It was an alliance founded on trust, but it was a deal too.
Baek was a seasoned politician.
He nodded without much hesitation.
“If you keep your word, that won’t be difficult.”
“Then it’s settled.
Nice and clean.”
As though they had planned it in advance, the two men rose from their seats at the same time and extended their hands.
Just as they were about to shake, Baek turned to me.
“Hunter Jin Taekyung.
May I ask one last question?”
“Me?
Sure.”
“Your request to stop the investigation at Ares Guild headquarters...
Is it connected to the visit at the special detention center the other day?”
“Ah.”
I’d figured a report would reach him.
Sure enough.
My eyes met Team Leader Choi’s.
I read his assent there and shrugged.
“Yes.”
“Huh.
The investigators must have missed something.”
“Why?
Going to send them back in?”
“I am curious what Go Se-won was hiding, but... if I were that stupid, I would never have made it this far.”
With that politician’s answer, Baek smiled and took Team Leader Choi’s hand.
“I hope we continue to get along.”
“I look forward to working with you, Mr.
President.”
The newly formed super-Guild and the government had forged a firm partnership.
And the last obstacle between us and Ares Guild was gone.
“C-could you say that again?”
“Cheon.
Tae as in Crown Prince, and Min.
Cheon Taemin.
That’s my maternal grandfather’s name.”
On the day of the joint national funeral for the victims, the reporters were wrapping up their coverage when a bombshell dropped on them.
They could hardly process it.
Neither could anyone else, apart from the handful of people who had known in advance.
Cheon Taemin.
The immortal hero shrouded in mystery for more than twenty years.
His only blood descendant, who had remained out of sight even as turmoil engulfed Ares Guild, had appeared before the cameras.
Naturally, media outlets in Korea and around the world erupted at once.
[Peace Guild Team Leader Choi Minwoo: “My Maternal Grandfather Is Cheon Taemin.”]
[Press Conference Stunned.
Ten Seconds of Silence.]
[Foreign Media in Uproar: Who Is Choi, Descendant of a Living Legend?]
[Truth or Lie?
Debate Erupts over Choi Minwoo’s Shocking Statement.]
[Peace Guild Spokesperson: “Choi Minwoo Confirmed as Peace Guild’s New Guild Master.”]
[Ares Guild Official: “Board Meeting Called Regarding Choi Minwoo.
Appointment as New Vice Guild Master Likely.”]
[Peace Guild’s New Captain—and Ares Guild Comes Calling?]
[KakaoPage Web-Novel Reader Ttolseu Comments on Chapter 599 of a Certain Novel: “Choi Minwoo’s a diehard Baek fan.
I’ll go read the fun Gigant Rider instead.” Author’s Response: “?”]
All four of Korea’s major morning papers gave Choi Minwoo extensive coverage, as did the foreign press.
Nonsense had even reached web-fiction platforms.
That alone showed the scale of the uproar.
For a short while, people argued over whether his claim was true.
Then Go Se-won, who knew Ares Guild’s inner workings better than anyone, and Magic Johnson spoke up.
[Former Head of Security Go Se-won: “Choi Minwoo’s Statement Is True.
He Lost His Parents as a Child and Was Shut Out of Ares Guild for More Than Twenty Years.”]
[American Grand Mage Magic Johnson: “He Is Definitely Cheon Taemin’s Maternal Grandson.
He Is Also a Very Capable and Charming Man Who Built Peace Guild into What It Is Today.
By the Way, Where Is Kanghee Lee?
Is He in the Shower?”]
[Former U.S.
President Joseph Biden: “I Think So, If I Remember Right.
Actually, I’m Not Sure.”]
[Prince Felix of the United Kingdom, on Hearing the News: “What The Fuk...” Royal Household Requests Interview Be Stopped.]
The finishing touch was the Blue House’s announcement confirming Choi Minwoo’s identity and declaring its support, followed by the results of Ares Guild’s official board meeting the next day.
[Ares Guild Elects Choi Minwoo, Current Peace Guild Master, as New Vice Guild Master.
“Board Vote Unanimous.”]
[Choi Minwoo: Young Power Broker Now at the Helm of Two Major Guilds.]
[Guild Association Offers “Sincere Congratulations,” Contrary to Experts’ Predictions of Opposition.]
[Immortal Hero Still Nowhere to Be Seen.]
[Overseas Reaction: “Where Is Slayer?”]
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung?”
At the voice in my ear, I looked up from my phone.
The face I’d seen in countless article photos was right in front of me.
Now Ares Guild’s new captain, welcomed with applause and cheers, Team Leader Choi regarded me calmly.
“What are you looking at?”
“Articles about you.
Should I still call you Team Leader Choi?
Or Guild Master now?
Maybe Vice Guild Master?
You’ve got a foot in each Guild.
It’s confusing.”
“Whatever you’re comfortable with.”
“Hmm.
How about Minwoo?”
Guild Master Choi Minwoo would be fine.”
“That feels awkward.
I’ll stick with Team Leader.”
Given his position and the people watching, Guild Master would have been the proper title.
But he couldn’t refuse my suggestion.
It was a hundred times better than Minwoo.
“...All right.”
Still looking uneasy, Team Leader Choi surveyed our surroundings.
The vast, devastated space had deliberately been left unrepaired for the investigation.
We were in Area A, inside Ares Guild headquarters.
Though “formerly hidden” would be more accurate now.
I crossed the familiar hallway.
I’d fought the mutated Go Jun here, and wreckage littered everywhere I looked and stepped.
Damn, it’s huge.
This wasn’t an orchard, but by my rough estimate, the place covered well over a thousand pyeong—more than thirty-five thousand square feet.
And Team Leader Choi and I had to comb through it.
Well, not just the two of us.
Our third member wasn’t human.
“Come out, you bastard.”
Swoosh.
A human-shaped creature that wasn’t human emerged from my Inventory.
“Are my eyes playing tricks on me?
I could’ve sworn you said you’d take me to a club.
You promised drinking games with beautiful women.”
The Skeleton King looked aggrieved.
I answered with complete confidence.
“We’re playing treasure hunt here.”
“Find it fast and I’ll really take you to a club.
I swear on Hyuk Mujin’s balls.”
“You despicable human.
I’ll trust you one last time.
But who is Hyuk Mujin, and why do you keep wagering his balls?”
I casually ignored the Skeleton King’s question and gestured toward Team Leader Choi.
“You take that side.
I’ll take this one.
Bones can handle way over there.”
“The area you’ve assigned me seems rather large.”
“Team Leader, you’re hurting my feelings.
If you don’t like it, quit.
Is he our grandfather?
He’s your grandfather.”
“That settles it.
Understood.”
With the work divided, we got moving.
Three hours later, we met up again, all wearing grim expressions.
“Fuuuck...
I can’t do this shit.”
“For some reason, the mana detector isn’t working.
And it’s the genuine luxury model I bought at a Sotheby’s auction.”
“Human.
Treasure hunt is boring as hell.”
Knowing how meticulous Lee Jungryong was, I’d expected the secret area to be hard to find.
I hadn’t expected this.
No wonder the government investigators had come away empty-handed.
There isn’t even a reaction in the office.
Could the information have been wrong?
But Go Se-won knew more about Ares Guild’s secrets than anyone left alive.
With Lee Jungryong, Song Cheonwoo, and Go Jun dead, trusting him was our only...
“Huh?”
A thought flashed through my mind, and my eyes widened.
Team Leader Choi stopped thumping the mana detector with his fist.
He and the Skeleton King both looked at me.
“What is it?”
“Oh.
Did you remember a club with a great crowd?”
“No, wait.
I think I know where to look.”
I quickly traced my memories of Area A: the fight with Go Jun, my first victory, and then...
When I came back, he was running away.
By then Go Jun had changed into a horrible mixture of human and monster.
He’d definitely been fleeing.
The question was where he’d been going.
That’s the place.
There’s something there I didn’t find.
Tap—whoosh!
I launched myself forward without another thought.
Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King hurried after me as I shot ahead like the wind.
We’d searched the place several times already, but this time was different.
Swoosh.
A dead-end hallway.
Several rooms.
I slowed and leaned close against the wall, heightening my Qi Sense.
A System chime sounded, and a blue circle spread outward from me.
It swept the hallway and every room, but no notification appeared to tell me I’d found anything.
Fwoooooosh.
The System determined the range of my Qi Sense.
I could perceive only what lay within it.
But was that really all?
Farther.
Wider.
I steadied my breathing.
The sounds around me receded, and internal energy rose from my dantian, lending strength to my Qi Sense.
And then, at the moment my Middle Dantian finally responded—
Fwoooooosh!
The blue circle, which had stopped expanding, surged outward.
Beyond the space I could see, toward another space hidden from sight.
At the edge of its reach came the notification I’d been waiting for.
Ding.

chapters.title: Chapter 604
paragraphs: Ding.

System You have gained enlightenment regarding Middle Dantian! Middle Dantian is partially activated! Middle Dantian activation: 10% - The efficiency of all martial arts and internal energy has increased slightly, and you may occasionally exert strength beyond your limits! - You have achieved the rare Achievement Waaah, I’m a Baby Middle Dantian! - You have gained a large amount of EXP as an Achievement reward! - Level Up!
Activated?
I hadn’t expected that.
It had been more than a month since I opened my Middle Dantian, but I’d had no idea it could do this.
And then, following the System notification announcing an unexpected reward, the news I had been waiting for arrived.
Ding.
System The range of Qi Sense is expanding! - The target cannot be identified precisely! - An unidentified, strange power is being sensed!
I hadn’t identified the target, but this wasn’t a failure. It was a success.
Something existed beyond this wall. Certain of it, I punched the wall without hesitation.
Boom!
The solid wall burst apart, revealing empty space.
Area A, hidden on the top floor of Ares Guild headquarters, was held in place by barriers, invisibility magic, and gravity magic. The government investigators must have known that too.
The problem was that they’d missed the most important thing.
No. They couldn’t have helped missing it.
I reached through the broken wall and ran my hand through the air. I felt nothing. It was empty, just as it appeared to be. The mana detector in Team Leader Choi’s hand remained silent.
But I was certain something lay beyond it.
Fwoosh.
Three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi transformed into flame. I silently looked down at my hands, bluish-white flames flickering over them, then closed my eyes and reached out.
What you see isn’t everything.
It was a matter of perception. I had to see and feel with my instincts, my senses, my heart—not my eyes.
I focused every bit of my attention and poured out internal energy without restraint. My partially opened Middle Dantian responded.
The flickering flames gradually settled, completely enveloping my entire hand.
Compression. True Form.
And then...
Crack.
I gripped the flow of qi in my grasp and tore it apart with all my strength.
Shraaak!
The air split apart amid the bluish-white flames. Force dispelled spells I couldn’t begin to understand, revealing an opening into another space.
The Skeleton King and Team Leader Choi stared blankly at the scene unfolding before them and muttered.
“He... tore it.”
“How in the world did you...?”
“When your body’s no good, your head has to do the work. Let’s go.”
“...Isn’t it usually the other way around?”
“Usually, yes.”
But I’m not usual.
At my casual reply, Team Leader Choi tossed the mana detector behind him.
Hmm. Having a good body really was the best.
It was a good thing we’d cleared the top floor in case something happened. Otherwise, we might have broadcast our entry into an unidentified subspace live.
Swoosh.
I stepped through the tall, narrow opening into a completely different world.
What the hell is this?
The space was vast and high-ceilinged, filled with a kind of elegance and extravagance I wasn’t used to. Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King followed me in, too busy looking around to speak.
“That’s...”
Team Leader Choi walked across the soft carpet, his eyes trembling faintly. He studied a painting hanging in the wide corridor.
“Salvator Mundi.”
“Did you just call me Mundi?”
“No. That’s the painting’s title. Salvator Mundi. It’s a masterpiece by Leonardo da Vinci. Have you never heard of it?”
“I’ve heard it from my mom now and then. She’s from Gyeongsang-do.”
“What’s that look for? Are you looking down on Gyeongsang-do? Team Leader Choi, do you have regional prejudice?”
“What? Regional prejudice?”
That hadn’t come from Team Leader Choi. The Skeleton King, who’d been looking around, butted in with an offended expression.
“Regional prejudice must be eliminated. As one born in the Demon Realm, I, too, agree with the wicked human.”
“Look at this undead bastard trying to bone in on the conversation. Stay out of it.”
“What the hell? I’m helping you, and you’re giving me shit?”
“The Demon Realm’s a different dimension, you bastard. That’s dimensional prejudice. You make it sound like it’s right next to Mount Jiri.”
“The Gate where I operated was in Bucheon. Of course, I’m from Atlanta, Georgia, in the United States.”
“Are you actually insane?”
While I argued with the Skeleton King across dimensions and borders, Team Leader Choi had given up on our conversation and started opening doors along the corridor. He called out to us.
“Both of you, stop and come over here.”
The Skeleton King drew himself up like a scholar.
“This body is the lord of the undead. I do not listen to the words of a human steeped in regional prejudice.”
“Come along if you don’t want your ass kicked.”
I grabbed the idiot by the collar and hauled him over. One look through the open doorway told me why Team Leader Choi had called us.
“What is this...?”
Not a single light was on, yet the room was as bright as day. Magic Gems sat neatly arranged on display shelves.
Even the lowest-grade gems were A-grade. By my rough count, there were around five hundred of them.
How much money is all this worth?
I couldn’t even begin to guess. And the five S-grade Magic Gems shining brightest on the top shelf were treasures you’d struggle to obtain no matter how much money you had.
“So all of this...?”
My voice trailed off. Team Leader Choi gave a small nod.
“Lee Jungryong definitely stole them. From what I’ve seen so far, the other rooms are the same.”
“This is fucking insane...”
“Not only Magic Gems, but also gold bars, diamonds, bonds, and other valuable assets. There are even countless works of art believed to have disappeared after the Great Cataclysm.”
He was right. Every door we opened on either side of the corridor revealed treasures of immense value, or treasures you couldn’t put a price on at all.
The calculator in my head had broken down long ago.
I expected him to have plenty stashed away, but... he really took a hell of a lot.
After the Great Cataclysm, Gates and Magic Gems had become a second source of oil money—no, something greater. Major Guilds had gained enough wealth and influence to overshadow powerful corporations.
Everyone, myself included, had assumed Lee Jungryong was immensely wealthy. No one could have guessed he’d hidden away this much on top of what had already been uncovered.
Vault.
The word flashed through my mind.
Right. This was the private vault Lee Jungryong had built and passed on to Go Jun.
But we couldn’t forget that this place was a prison as well as a vault.
A prison meant to hide one person from the world.
Its only two guards were dead. Beside me, the new owner of this space was walking toward the final door.
Step. Step.
At the end of the long corridor, Team Leader Choi approached the firmly shut door. He couldn’t hide the tremor in his steps.
“Hoo.”
He took a quiet breath to steady himself. I stepped ahead of him and brought my hand down like a blade toward the door, where an enormous flow of mana gathered.
A streak of flame cut through the air.
Slice! Boom!
The spells fell away, and the alloy door split to either side. Darkness and bitter cold, as though they’d been crouching beyond it, swept over us.
Whoooosh.
An inexplicable chill ran through me. I had reached the realm of Unaffected by Cold and Heat, yet I shuddered. Even the Skeleton King, a being born of death and cold, trembled.
Only one of us did not.
Step.
Footsteps rang strangely loud in the darkness. Team Leader Choi walked on without a word, all trace of trembling and hesitation gone.
More than twenty years.

A child had become a boy, and a boy had become a young man. He’d lost his parents early and been separated from his maternal grandfather without knowing why. Now, at last, he had returned to his place and stood here.
To meet his only blood relative and learn the truth.
“I missed you. I always have.”
Step.
His footsteps continued forward until, at some point, they suddenly stopped.

Before him stood a large oval mechanical capsule connected to countless wires. It looked like something out of a science-fiction movie, a device made for hibernation. A coffin made for someone still alive.
Hoo.
Team Leader Choi’s breath fogged the dust-covered glass. His long fingers trembled as he wiped it clean.
“I wanted to see you.”
As the dust came away, a face emerged. It looked older and more worn than in the photographs online.
Yet the resemblance to Team Leader Choi was unmistakable. He spoke softly to the old man.
“Grandfather.”
Team Leader Choi kept everything strictly secret. For now, no one besides the Skeleton King and me could know, and I agreed wholeheartedly.
There was one minor complication.
“Keeping a secret is easy enough. But I have two conditions.”
With the resolve of an independence activist, the Skeleton King laid them out.
“First, take me to a club. Second, give me one of the S-grade Magic Gems in there.”
Team Leader Choi readily agreed to the first. The second gave him pause, so I offered him a simple alternative.
“There’s a better way.”
“What is it?”
“How many S-grade Magic Gems do we have right now?”
“There are still five left.”
“Then let’s beat that bastard up and make it six. We can keep the secret and secure an additional S-grade Magic Gem.”

The Skeleton King, who had demanded his terms with the spirit of an independence activist, became a pro-Japanese collaborator and cooperated, and we reached a dramatic compromise by agreeing to take him to a club.
But for the most important matter—what to do with Cheon Taemin—we had no choice but to ask someone for help.
“We can’t keep my maternal grandfather here forever. We need to move him somewhere else.”
“The problem is moving him without anyone noticing...”
Neither a pocket enchanted with spatial expansion magic nor my Inventory could do it. The Immortal Hero, Cheon Taemin, was very much alive.
After thinking it over, only one answer remained.
“We have to move him using teleportation magic.”
What mattered was who performed it.
Someone we could trust completely. Someone who wouldn’t tell a soul even after learning the truth. Someone sympathetic to the unconscious Cheon Taemin and to us, who could continue helping us...
“Only one person comes to mind.”
“I imagine we’re thinking of the same person, Mr. Jin.”
So I made a call.
“Can you come to Korea for a bit?”
—Hey, Jin. I’m busy too. There’s a mutated Gate right now—
“Team Leader Choi wants to see you. A kiss is totally possible.”
—I’ll come right now.
