Boom!
The solid wall burst apart, revealing empty space.
Area A, hidden on the top floor of Ares Guild headquarters, was held in place by barriers, invisibility magic, and gravity magic.
The government investigators must have known that too.
The problem was that they’d missed the most important thing.
No.
They couldn’t have helped missing it.
I reached through the broken wall and ran my hand through the air.
I felt nothing.
It was empty, just as it appeared to be.
The mana detector in Team Leader Choi’s hand remained silent.
But I was certain something lay beyond it.
Fwoosh.
Three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi transformed into flame.
I silently looked down at my hands, bluish-white flames flickering over them, then closed my eyes and reached out.
What you see isn’t everything.
It was a matter of perception.
I had to see and feel with my instincts, my senses, my heart—not my eyes.
I focused every bit of my attention and poured out internal energy without restraint.
My partially opened Middle Dantian responded.
The flickering flames gradually settled, completely enveloping my entire hand.
Compression.
True Form.
And then...
Crack.
I gripped the flow of qi in my grasp and tore it apart with all my strength.
Shraaak!
The air split apart amid the bluish-white flames.
Force dispelled spells I couldn’t begin to understand, revealing an opening into another space.
The Skeleton King and Team Leader Choi stared blankly at the scene unfolding before them and muttered.
“He... tore it.”
“How in the world did you...?”
“When your body’s no good, your head has to do the work.
Let’s go.”
“...Isn’t it usually the other way around?”
“Usually, yes.”
But I’m not usual.
At my casual reply, Team Leader Choi tossed the mana detector behind him.
Hmm.
Having a good body really was the best.
It was a good thing we’d cleared the top floor in case something happened.
Otherwise, we might have broadcast our entry into an unidentified subspace live.
Swoosh.
I stepped through the tall, narrow opening into a completely different world.
What the hell is this?
The space was vast and high-ceilinged, filled with a kind of elegance and extravagance I wasn’t used to.
Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King followed me in, too busy looking around to speak.
“That’s...”
Team Leader Choi walked across the soft carpet, his eyes trembling faintly.
He studied a painting hanging in the wide corridor.
“Salvator Mundi.”
“Did you just call me Mundi?”
“No.
That’s the painting’s title.
Salvator Mundi.
It’s a masterpiece by Leonardo da Vinci.
Have you never heard of it?”
“I’ve heard it from my mom now and then.
She’s from Gyeongsang-do.”
“What’s that look for?
Are you looking down on Gyeongsang-do?
Team Leader Choi, do you have regional prejudice?”
“What?
Regional prejudice?”
That hadn’t come from Team Leader Choi.
The Skeleton King, who’d been looking around, butted in with an offended expression.
“Regional prejudice must be eliminated.
As one born in the Demon Realm, I, too, agree with the wicked human.”
“Look at this undead bastard trying to bone in on the conversation.
Stay out of it.”
“What the hell?
I’m helping you, and you’re giving me shit?”
“The Demon Realm’s a different dimension, you bastard.
That’s dimensional prejudice.
You make it sound like it’s right next to Mount Jiri.”
“The Gate where I operated was in Bucheon.
Of course, I’m from Atlanta, Georgia, in the United States.”
“Are you actually insane?”
While I argued with the Skeleton King across dimensions and borders, Team Leader Choi had given up on our conversation and started opening doors along the corridor.
He called out to us.
“Both of you, stop and come over here.”
The Skeleton King drew himself up like a scholar.
“This body is the lord of the undead.
I do not listen to the words of a human steeped in regional prejudice.”
“Come along if you don’t want your ass kicked.”
I grabbed the idiot by the collar and hauled him over.
One look through the open doorway told me why Team Leader Choi had called us.
“What is this...?”
Not a single light was on, yet the room was as bright as day.
Magic Gems sat neatly arranged on display shelves.
Even the lowest-grade gems were A-grade.
By my rough count, there were around five hundred of them.
How much money is all this worth?
I couldn’t even begin to guess.
And the five S-grade Magic Gems shining brightest on the top shelf were treasures you’d struggle to obtain no matter how much money you had.
“So all of this...?”
My voice trailed off.
Team Leader Choi gave a small nod.
“Lee Jungryong definitely stole them.
From what I’ve seen so far, the other rooms are the same.”
“This is fucking insane...”
“Not only Magic Gems, but also gold bars, diamonds, bonds, and other valuable assets.
There are even countless works of art believed to have disappeared after the Great Cataclysm.”
He was right.
Every door we opened on either side of the corridor revealed treasures of immense value, or treasures you couldn’t put a price on at all.
The calculator in my head had broken down long ago.
I expected him to have plenty stashed away, but... he really took a hell of a lot.
After the Great Cataclysm, Gates and Magic Gems had become a second source of oil money—no, something greater.
Major Guilds had gained enough wealth and influence to overshadow powerful corporations.
Everyone, myself included, had assumed Lee Jungryong was immensely wealthy.
No one could have guessed he’d hidden away this much on top of what had already been uncovered.
Vault.
The word flashed through my mind.
Right.
This was the private vault Lee Jungryong had built and passed on to Go Jun.
But we couldn’t forget that this place was a prison as well as a vault.
A prison meant to hide one person from the world.
Its only two guards were dead.
Beside me, the new owner of this space was walking toward the final door.
Step.
Step.
At the end of the long corridor, Team Leader Choi approached the firmly shut door.
He couldn’t hide the tremor in his steps.
“Hoo.”
He took a quiet breath to steady himself.
I stepped ahead of him and brought my hand down like a blade toward the door, where an enormous flow of mana gathered.
A streak of flame cut through the air.
Slice!
Boom!
The spells fell away, and the alloy door split to either side.
Darkness and bitter cold, as though they’d been crouching beyond it, swept over us.
Whoooosh.
An inexplicable chill ran through me.
I had reached the realm of Unaffected by Cold and Heat, yet I shuddered.
Even the Skeleton King, a being born of death and cold, trembled.
Only one of us did not.
Step.
Footsteps rang strangely loud in the darkness.
Team Leader Choi walked on without a word, all trace of trembling and hesitation gone.
More than twenty years.
A child had become a boy, and a boy had become a young man.
He’d lost his parents early and been separated from his maternal grandfather without knowing why.
Now, at last, he had returned to his place and stood here.
To meet his only blood relative and learn the truth.
“I missed you.
I always have.”
Step.
His footsteps continued forward until, at some point, they suddenly stopped.
Before him stood a large oval mechanical capsule connected to countless wires.
It looked like something out of a science-fiction movie, a device made for hibernation.
A coffin made for someone still alive.
Hoo.
Team Leader Choi’s breath fogged the dust-covered glass.
His long fingers trembled as he wiped it clean.
“I wanted to see you.”
As the dust came away, a face emerged.
It looked older and more worn than in the photographs online.
Yet the resemblance to Team Leader Choi was unmistakable.
He spoke softly to the old man.
“Grandfather.”
Team Leader Choi kept everything strictly secret.
For now, no one besides the Skeleton King and me could know, and I agreed wholeheartedly.
There was one minor complication.
“Keeping a secret is easy enough.
But I have two conditions.”
With the resolve of an independence activist, the Skeleton King laid them out.
“First, take me to a club.
Second, give me one of the S-grade Magic Gems in there.”
Team Leader Choi readily agreed to the first.
The second gave him pause, so I offered him a simple alternative.
“There’s a better way.”
“What is it?”
“How many S-grade Magic Gems do we have right now?”
“There are still five left.”
“Then let’s beat that bastard up and make it six.
We can keep the secret and secure an additional S-grade Magic Gem.”

The Skeleton King, who had demanded his terms with the spirit of an independence activist, became a pro-Japanese collaborator and cooperated, and we reached a dramatic compromise by agreeing to take him to a club.
But for the most important matter—what to do with Cheon Taemin—we had no choice but to ask someone for help.
“We can’t keep my maternal grandfather here forever.
We need to move him somewhere else.”
“The problem is moving him without anyone noticing...”
Neither a pocket enchanted with spatial expansion magic nor my Inventory could do it.
The Immortal Hero, Cheon Taemin, was very much alive.
After thinking it over, only one answer remained.
“We have to move him using teleportation magic.”
What mattered was who performed it.
Someone we could trust completely.
Someone who wouldn’t tell a soul even after learning the truth.
Someone sympathetic to the unconscious Cheon Taemin and to us, who could continue helping us...
“Only one person comes to mind.”
“I imagine we’re thinking of the same person, Mr.
Jin.”
So I made a call.
“Can you come to Korea for a bit?”
—Hey, Jin.
I’m busy too.
There’s a mutated Gate right now—
“Team Leader Choi wants to see you.
A kiss is totally possible.”
—I’ll come right now.

chapters.title: Chapter 605
paragraphs: “Jacob, how are things over there? You’re not hurt, are you?”
On the holographic TV, an East Asian anchor with heavy eye makeup put the question to a broad-shouldered Black reporter at the scene. He winked at the camera.
“Thanks for worrying about me, Jenny. I’m fine, and so is everyone else.”
“It looks unbelievably peaceful for the site of a Mutated Gate.”
“It is. No one was hurt, and the whole thing was over in no time. Besides, this is Texas. Everyone here is tough, men and women alike.”
“Haha. That’s a relief. But where’s the hero who saved everyone?”
“Jenny, I owe you and our viewers an apology. Magic Johnson, the hero we hoped to have with us today, has already left. I did my best, but I couldn’t persuade him to stay.”
“Oh, dear.”
“He said something urgent had come up and turned down the interview. He looked so desperate to leave, I thought he was off to meet a secret lover.”
“I see. Now, Jacob, about the exact cause of this Mutated Gate...”
Hmm. A secret lover.
I leaned back on the sofa, watching the holographic TV, and found myself humming.
“When Dad goes to work, Ppoppo. Magic Johnson comes to Korea, Ppoppo.”
Whoosh! Crash!
I ducked at the sound of something cutting through the air. A crystal glass skimmed the back of my neck and smashed into the holographic TV.
Shards flew everywhere, and water pooled across the floor. My eyes met Team Leader Choi’s. He spoke calmly.
“Oh. You dodged it.”
“In case you’re wondering, that was deliberate.”
“...You’re not even going to pretend it was an accident?”
“Because it wasn’t an accident. Still, it’s a real shame. If that had been just a little faster, it would’ve smashed Mr. Jin Taekyung’s skull...”
“Hey, you don’t call a person’s head a ‘skull.’ A skull?”
“I can when you won’t stop running that damn mouth of yours. Frankly, even ‘head’ is too good a word for a blockhead like you.”
“Whoa. ‘Damn head’? ‘Damn mouth’?”
“Don’t fall asleep in front of me from now on. If you sleep with your mouth open, I’ll pour cyanide down it.”
What the hell was that punchline?
He must have been furious. He practically spat the words, and the venom in them left me speechless for a moment.
I considered taking out the Myriad-Poison Ring, then politely waved a hand.
“Team Leader Choi. Calm down. This was all my fault.”
“Do I look like I can calm down?”
“I’m telling you, I had no choice. You saw the news. He was busy with a Mutated Gate. What else could I do? I had to get him here first.”
“By offering up my lips without asking me?”
“But I couldn’t offer up my own lips, could I?”
Whoosh! Crash!
Whoa. That one was actually close.
I narrowly dodged again and shouted, “Stop! Team Leader, stop!”
Team Leader Choi picked up a third crystal glass.
“Shut your mouth and stick your head out. Right there.”
“I didn’t kiss him! I didn’t do it in the end!”
“You almost did!”
Team Leader Choi was just about to swing his arm with a roar that could rival a lion’s roar when—
Bang.
The door flew open without a knock. In the doorway stood the Skeleton King, brimming with anticipation, and Magic Johnson, looking dejected.
“The job’s done. Are we going to a club now?”
“Choi, I’m a romantic too.”
Team Leader Choi stared silently at the club-obsessed parrot and the pure-hearted Grand Mage. Then, with a sigh, he lowered his hand.
Before he was an outstanding War Mage, Magic Johnson was a Grand Mage capable of wielding most forms of magic.
He had come straight to Korea after our call, and we’d told him the truth as soon as he arrived.
“Mr. Johnson. There’s something we need to move...”
“Whatever the reason, I want my Ppoppo first. Ready, Choi?”
“I’m not ready, I won’t be ready, and I never will be.”
“Then we have a problem. I don’t know what you’re trying to move in such secrecy, but...”
“Actually, it isn’t a thing. It’s a person.”
“What do you mean, Jin? A person? Are you helping someone escape?”
“I don’t know if ‘escape’ is the right word, but it’s something like that.”
“Who is it? Some heinous criminal? A secret lover?”
“My maternal grandfather.”
“Oh, shit. Sorry, Choi. I didn’t mean to—wait. Who did you say?”
Magic Johnson had remained silent for a long time even after hearing the whole story. He didn’t speak again until he saw Cheon Taemin’s face for himself.
“Damn it. What the hell happened?”
“As you can see, it’s a shitty situation.”
“There was a reason you couldn’t explain everything over the phone. All right, let’s take care of the urgent matter first. Choi, where are we moving him from this prison-like place?”
After that, things moved quickly.
Magic Johnson cast Teleport to the coordinates Team Leader Choi gave him, and we all—no, one of us, trapped in a deep sleep he could hardly wake from—returned to the mansion where he had once lived.
To the home he had missed.
It was a return more than twenty long years in the making.
“Space distortion, barriers, defensive magic, of course. I’ve set up humidity and temperature controls too. And...”
Magic Johnson rattled off spell after spell like a wanderer riding a beat, then finished in a breathless rush.
“In short, I’ve done everything I can for now. There’s still more work to do, though.”
The Skeleton King, sulking because he hadn’t gotten to go to a club, muttered, “I get that it’s impressive. How impressive?”
“The place will hold unless a Grand Mage on my level—or two or three S-rank Hunters—sets out to smash it.”
“That’s some serious performance.”
I agreed with the Skeleton King. Magic Johnson really had done everything he could for now, making it impossible for even most S-rank Hunters to detect Cheon Taemin or find his location.
Combat and magic are different disciplines.
There was no end to martial arts training, and the same went for magic. If I hadn’t opened my Middle Dantian, I wouldn’t have found Cheon Taemin so easily either.
“By the way, does anyone know who created that secret space? The magic in Area A and the spells installed there weren’t beneath mine.”
“This body has no idea, human.”
I gave the Skeleton King’s shoulder a courteous pat.
“He asked if anyone knew. Not if a monster knew.”
“You really are a fucking bastard.”
Hmm. His vocabulary was improving by the day.
Smack!
As a reward for his Vocabulary Improvement Quest, I struck the back of his head, then turned to Magic Johnson.
“I’ve been wondering about that too. Do you have anyone in mind?”
“Hmm. When you think about it, it would have to be another Grand Mage. Especially with magic at that level.”
“Then maybe...”
“You mean the other two?”
I fell silent, uncertain. Magic Johnson shook his head, his expression unusually serious.
“Probably not. Though I do have someone in mind.”
“You do?”
“Hmm.”
Magic Johnson let out a low hum and seemed to sink into thought before continuing.
“I’d rather not say more yet. It’s too early to be sure. But I should visit the other Grand Mages, just in case. It’s been a while since I’ve seen them.”
“I’d appreciate that.”
It was welcome news. Magic Johnson had the insight of a Grand Mage, and he meant to find out for himself whether his suspicions were right.
There are currently only three Grand Mages in the world.
If one of them had accepted the job knowing full well what Lee Jungryong intended...
We couldn’t let that pass. Anyone who had helped imprison the hero who saved humanity from disaster as though he were a criminal would have to answer for it.
For the sake of one person, if nothing else.
“Team Leader Choi.”
He didn’t respond. Inside the cold, oval metal hibernation capsule, Team Leader Choi gazed endlessly at his grandfather, who lay in a deep sleep. Then, all at once, he spoke.
“I’ve waited for so long... but you still haven’t woken up.”
A clumsy attempt at comfort would have been worse than silence. We all knew it, and none of us spoke.
The Immortal Hero, Cheon Taemin, still hadn’t regained consciousness.
For more than twenty years.
We knew neither the cause nor the reason. Unfortunately, everything Team Leader Choi had heard from Song Cheonwoo had been true.

Lee Jungryong and Song Cheonwoo, those two ambitious men, had once tried every possible way to wake him, but in the end they’d failed. In this frustrating situation, there was only one thing we could say now.
“There has to be a way.”
“Jin’s right. An effect can’t exist without a cause. Neither can an illness.”
“Cheer up. He certainly isn’t dead yet. Even if he dies, I’ll find a way to bring him back as a Death Knight...”
Magic Johnson and I turned our killing intent on the Skeleton King. He stopped and stammered, “I-I was trying to comfort him.”
“You call that comfort, you fucking asshole?”
“Monster motherfucker...”
I was berating the Skeleton King in a voice no louder than a mosquito’s buzz so Team Leader Choi wouldn’t overhear when Choi spoke with a faint smile.
“It’s all right. We’ll find a way somehow. I’m grateful he’s alive.”
A smile didn’t mean someone was happy.
I could feel what Team Leader Choi was going through. So could Magic Johnson. Even the Skeleton King, who didn’t have a finger bone’s worth of tact, could feel it.
As though by agreement, we all fell silent. Team Leader Choi’s voice, sunk deep with emotion, pierced my ears.
“But... at least for today, I’d like to rest. Thank you all for your hard work. I truly appreciate it.”
He looked at us one by one, then bowed his head sincerely.
I understood the meaning of that gesture and was the first to walk toward the entrance.
This was a reunion that had come after more than twenty years. For a grandfather and grandson who could not even exchange a single greeting right now, it was time for us to leave them alone.
One of the most important things to Koreans was rice.
“Are you eating properly?” “Let’s get a meal sometime.” “What are you, jotbap?”
Okay, that last one was a little strange. But even our insults have bap in them. That’s Korean culture for you.
Which meant that when Koreans finished a job, they ate together. And the best meal was rice in hot soup.
“Gukbap? What’s this?”
Magic Johnson eyed Mom’s homemade blood sausage gukbap with suspicion and put down his spoon.
“Hey, Jin. Got any toast?”
“Come on. Just try it.”
“No, thanks. I’m not hungry.”
Grrrrr.
“...You really don’t have any toast?”
“Even if there were some, there isn’t. If you’re that reluctant, just try the broth. The broth alone.”
“Damn it. Is this Korean soup? Why does it look so weird?”
Grumbling, Magic Johnson picked up his spoon and clumsily scooped up some broth.
The moment he tasted it, the game was over.
“Kheeeee. Fuck yeah.”
He polished off two bowls of blood sausage gukbap, saying “Fuck yeah” over and over, then smiled contentedly.
“There were so many things going wrong today that I was busy all day. I feel like I can finally breathe.”
“I saw the news earlier, actually. You subdued the Mutated Gate and came straight here without even doing an interview.”
“A Mutated Gate? Didn’t you watch to the end?”
I couldn’t. Team Leader Choi smashed the TV with a crystal glass.
I shrugged. “Why?”
“Because you wouldn’t say that if you had.”
Magic Johnson picked up a toothpick.
“Strictly speaking, it wasn’t a Mutated Gate.”
“What?”
What the hell was he talking about now?

For more than twenty years.
We knew neither the cause nor the reason.
Unfortunately, everything Team Leader Choi had heard from Song Cheonwoo had been true.
Lee Jungryong and Song Cheonwoo, those two ambitious men, had once tried every possible way to wake him, but in the end they’d failed.
In this frustrating situation, there was only one thing we could say now.
“There has to be a way.”
“Jin’s right.
An effect can’t exist without a cause.
Neither can an illness.”
“Cheer up.
He certainly isn’t dead yet.
Even if he dies, I’ll find a way to bring him back as a Death Knight...”
Magic Johnson and I turned our killing intent on the Skeleton King.
He stopped and stammered, “I-I was trying to comfort him.”
“You call that comfort, you fucking asshole?”
“Monster motherfucker...”
I was berating the Skeleton King in a voice no louder than a mosquito’s buzz so Team Leader Choi wouldn’t overhear when Choi spoke with a faint smile.
“It’s all right.
We’ll find a way somehow.
I’m grateful he’s alive.”
A smile didn’t mean someone was happy.
I could feel what Team Leader Choi was going through.
So could Magic Johnson.
Even the Skeleton King, who didn’t have a finger bone’s worth of tact, could feel it.
As though by agreement, we all fell silent.
Team Leader Choi’s voice, sunk deep with emotion, pierced my ears.
“But... at least for today, I’d like to rest.
Thank you all for your hard work.
I truly appreciate it.”
He looked at us one by one, then bowed his head sincerely.
I understood the meaning of that gesture and was the first to walk toward the entrance.
This was a reunion that had come after more than twenty years.
For a grandfather and grandson who could not even exchange a single greeting right now, it was time for us to leave them alone.
One of the most important things to Koreans was rice.
“Are you eating properly?” “Let’s get a meal sometime.” “What are you, jotbap?”
Okay, that last one was a little strange.
But even our insults have bap in them.
That’s Korean culture for you.
Which meant that when Koreans finished a job, they ate together.
And the best meal was rice in hot soup.
“Gukbap?
What’s this?”
Magic Johnson eyed Mom’s homemade blood sausage gukbap with suspicion and put down his spoon.
“Hey, Jin.
Got any toast?”
“Come on.
Just try it.”
“No, thanks.
I’m not hungry.”
Grrrrr.
“...You really don’t have any toast?”
“Even if there were some, there isn’t.
If you’re that reluctant, just try the broth.
The broth alone.”
“Damn it.
Is this Korean soup?
Why does it look so weird?”
Grumbling, Magic Johnson picked up his spoon and clumsily scooped up some broth.
The moment he tasted it, the game was over.
“Kheeeee.
Fuck yeah.”
He polished off two bowls of blood sausage gukbap, saying “Fuck yeah” over and over, then smiled contentedly.
“There were so many things going wrong today that I was busy all day.
I feel like I can finally breathe.”
“I saw the news earlier, actually.
You subdued the Mutated Gate and came straight here without even doing an interview.”
“A Mutated Gate?
Didn’t you watch to the end?”
I couldn’t.
Team Leader Choi smashed the TV with a crystal glass.
I shrugged.
“Why?”
“Because you wouldn’t say that if you had.”
Magic Johnson picked up a toothpick.
“Strictly speaking, it wasn’t a Mutated Gate.”
“What?”
What the hell was he talking about now?

chapters.title: Chapter 606
paragraphs: It wasn’t a Mutated Gate? What the hell was that supposed to mean?
My confusion lasted only a moment. Then Magic Johnson dropped a single word, and my eyes widened.
“Terrorism?”

“Yeah, terrorism. An Arab man was caught trying to enter a Gate with a forged Hunter license. Turns out he was a B-rank Hunter with a terrorist group in the Middle East, and he was carrying an A-grade Magic Gem. One that hadn’t been purified, of course.”
“Wait. That sounds...”
“It must be a pretty familiar situation to you, Jin. Am I wrong?”
I pressed my lips together instead of answering. Recent memories flashed through my mind.
Go Jun. Song Cheonwoo. And two Monster Waves.
Something that should never have happened again kept happening.
“He was trying to cause a Monster Wave.”
“Probably. No, I’m sure of it.”
Damn it.
“What about the casualties?” I asked urgently. “Was anyone hurt? Did the news deliberately hide the damage because...”
I couldn’t bring myself to finish.

The recent incidents had been one disaster after another. The man might not have been comparable to Go Jun, but if a B-rank Hunter from a terrorist group had absorbed an unpurified A-grade Magic Gem, he could have done considerable damage on his own.
Magic Johnson answered calmly.
“Whoa. Easy, Jin. The news reports were true. Thank God, there wasn’t any significant damage.”
“Are you sure?”
“Why would I lie to you?”
“But how?”

“After what happened, the whole world’s on high alert. Identity checks and Magic Gem inspections have gotten several times stricter. That’s how they caught him. He tried to absorb the Magic Gem as a last resort. What do you think happened?”
Magic Johnson took a sip of the instant coffee in his paper cup.
“It’s simple. He couldn’t withstand the power contained in the Magic Gem. By the way, this coffee is pretty good.”
“Forget the coffee. If he couldn’t withstand it, shouldn’t he have mutated like Go Jun?”
Mana and magical power were like oil and water. They could never mix.
Go Jun was proof. Even as a certified S-rank Hunter trained in the modern Mana Cultivation Method, he had never managed to absorb magical power completely.
The real problem was the temporary surge of power—and the mutation waiting afterward.
So how was the result simple?
The lack of significant damage made even less sense now.
Magic Johnson’s answer took me completely by surprise.
“No. He exploded.”
“What?”
“I mean he blew apart. Into pieces. Boom!”
Bang, bang!
Magic Johnson tapped his spoon against the earthenware bowl and shrugged.
“And that was the end of everything. All I did at the scene was protect people from the blast’s aftermath.”
“In a way, you could certainly call it a suicide attack. But that was all it amounted to.”
At those words, I realized something and muttered inwardly.
It wasn’t that it was like what happened with Go Jun. It was that what happened with Go Jun had only been possible because it was Go Jun.
I’d had it backward from the start.
It came down to the size of the vessel. Not in terms of a person’s character or breadth of mind, but in terms of how much power they could contain without letting it overflow.
By that measure, Go Jun had been a large vessel. He could absorb some magical power and hold on to it, if only briefly.
And even he eventually mutated.
Go Jun had absorbed two S-grade Magic Gems at once. The balance of his vessel broke, and he finally mutated.
Even if I hadn’t intervened personally, there was a very good chance he would have died after holding out for only a little longer.
An ordinary Hunter wouldn’t stand a chance.
The terrorist in today’s news had been a B-rank Hunter, but the power had still blown him apart on the spot. He hadn’t been able to control any of the magical power in that Magic Gem.
“Hey, Jin. Looks like you’re getting it.”
Magic Johnson was grinning. I let out a short, disbelieving laugh.
“That’s a huge relief.”
“It is. Only a complete idiot would try the same thing after today.”
Magic Johnson had put his finger on what mattered. It was fortunate that the terrorist attack had caused no damage, but the greater relief was that it would deter similar incidents in the future.
“The terrorist group must have realized it, too. To put it coldly, this was a terrible trade from their perspective.”

A trained Hunter was a valuable asset, and a Magic Gem was an energy source of immense value. I didn’t know how the group had gotten hold of an unpurified A-grade Magic Gem, but today they’d failed spectacularly.
They had lost both a valuable operative and a Magic Gem easily worth several billion won.
“They’ll change tactics,” Magic Johnson said. “Probably go back to targeting defenseless civilians with that damn magic wand of Allah. But it’s too early to let our guard down.”
He sighed quietly.

“Terrorist organizations have been making some worrying moves lately. I hear they’ve been experimenting with Gates and Magic Gems, especially in Africa and the Middle East. The information came from the Pentagon, so it’s reliable.”
The Skeleton King, who had spent the entire conversation fiddling with his smartphone without participating, perked up his ears.
“The Pentagon? Are we going there right now? Is much rub-rub possible?”
“Just so you know, it’s not a club.”
“Damn it. I thought I was finally going to meet some hot girls.”
Don’t even dream about it, you bastard...
The Pentagon was the headquarters of the United States Department of Defense. If the Skeleton King’s identity came to light, its researchers would party all night.
In a heavily secured laboratory, of course, where they’d try all kinds of rub-rub with every experimental tool they had.
“Hmm. Everyone would certainly be happy if we took him to the Pentagon,” Magic Johnson said.
“Not so good for you or me, though.”
“True. We’d probably stand trial for violating international law. Though if a terrorist group caused trouble while the trial was going on, the whole thing might fizzle out.”
Life was hard. The moment one problem was solved, another popped up.
A terrorist group.
Once the series of incidents caused by Go Jun became known to the world, every country had been thrown into shock and heightened alertness.
But terrorist groups had gained another weapon.
If the information Magic Johnson had obtained from the Pentagon was true, they would find a way no matter what it took.
“...Of all times,” I muttered.
Magic Johnson looked puzzled.
“Of all times? What do you mean?”
“Hmm.”
I hesitated, then shook my head.
“It’s nothing. Don’t worry about it.”
“It sounds like something, and it’s bothering me a lot.”
“It’s just... there’s something I’ve been preparing to do. But after hearing that, I’m hesitating for now.”
“Something you’ve been preparing?”
I gave a small nod.
I hadn’t told anyone yet. It was one of the things I’d decided to do when I returned to the modern era this time.
For myself, and for everyone else, I had made a decision after a long period of hesitation and had been preparing for it...
But this changes things.
Humanity had regained peace after the Great Cataclysm. That didn’t mean the whole world was peaceful.
Mana had appeared, along with Awakened people. Those who survived and came out strong had remade the world by their own rules, and conflicts everyone thought had ended were still going on.
No. Some people would even say they’ve only gotten worse.

Magic Gems were more valuable and useful than oil. Gates were mines that kept spitting out those diamonds. Conflict over them was inevitable, whether the people involved called themselves entrepreneurs, Guilds, or rebels.
The terrorist groups in the Middle East were more dangerous still.

They called awakening a blessing from God and held it up as proof that God existed. You might ask what the hell they were talking about when even atheists could Awaken, but looking for logic in people like that was a mistake to begin with.
Warriors chosen by God! Advance!
God wills it!
I had no idea which god or doctrine had told them to do such idiotic things.
But singers sang, blacksmiths worked iron, and idiots kept doing idiotic things. They fought across the world, dying or ending up crippled.
And they were still at it right now.
Bastards.
The Skeleton King was a lot better than them. He might have started out as a monster, but by now he’d shown as much sacrifice and dedication as any Hunter.
Good lad.
At the warmth in my gaze, the Skeleton King glared at me ferociously.
“You just cursed this body in your thoughts.”
“...What the hell? That’s absurd.”
“Tell me the truth. I’ll let it slide.”
“Johnson, can’t we just take this bastard to the Pentagon?”
Magic Johnson grinned.
“Shall we?”
“You hear that? You’re finished, you experimental-subject bastard.”
“Now that it’s come to this, going right away wouldn’t be bad.”
“Tell them to prepare a cauldron. We’ll make some bone broth out of this bastard.”
“I don’t know about a cauldron, but the laboratory will be ready whenever we are.”
For some reason, Magic Johnson and I were on exactly the same wavelength today.
He played along without missing a beat, then drew a staff from inside his clothes.
“Well, now that we’ve eaten, shall we get going?”
“Sounds good... Wait.”
I’d answered on reflex. Then I felt mana circulating through his staff and gave him an uneasy look.
“Uh, there’s no need to go that far.”
“Don’t you have a traditional Korean proverb? Once a gay draws his magic wand, he must pierce even a radish.”
That sounded like a strange and impressive twist on a proverb I’d never heard in my life. I swallowed.
“Wait. Seriously?”
“Yeah. Seriously.”
“You’re not joking?”
“The Pentagon sent an official request two days ago. They want your advice and your help, Jin. As soon as possible.”
“What?”
I blinked, then let out a hollow laugh.
“Oh, I get it. This is an American joke.”
Magic Johnson fixed me with the profound gaze of a gay man.
“How did you know? I don’t remember showing you that memory.”
What the fuck is he talking about?
I stood there blankly for a moment before hurriedly waving my hands.
“...No, I got the pronunciation mixed up. Joke. Joke. A gag.”
“I know. That was a joke, too.”
He flashed a white-toothed grin.
“But the part about the Pentagon wasn’t.”
“Let’s go. It looks like someone else is already ready. Isn’t that right?”
I followed his gaze and turned my head. I sensed a familiar presence, and a figure came into view.
Team Leader Choi answered in a subdued voice.
“Of course, Mr. Johnson.”

chapters.title: Chapter 607
paragraphs: The Pentagon.
The massive pentagon-shaped building was practically impregnable.

A security force of some thousand guards, every one of them a high-ranking Hunter. Immense flows of mana surrounded the building inside and out. That alone told you what kind of place the Pentagon was.
“Impressive, isn’t it?”
Magic Johnson had just finished the authentication process. Seeing Team Leader Choi and me looking around wide-eyed, he gave us a knowing grin.
“Since it was first built during World War II, the Pentagon has only been attacked twice. Once on 9/11, and once during the Great Cataclysm. You both know how those turned out.”
Team Leader Choi nodded.
“Even the Demon King Asmodeus and his monster army’s all-out assault couldn’t bring it down.”
“That’s right. It was the second fiercest battle of my life. The first was the Day of Victory, of course. Both times, one person helped me escape with my life.”
Any person on Earth, not just an American, knew that fact.
During the Great Cataclysm and afterward, only one person had been able to stop the demon who descended upon this world: the Demon King Asmodeus.
“Cheon Taemin. If your maternal grandfather—the man Americans call Sky—hadn’t been there, neither I nor this Pentagon would exist today.”
Magic Johnson was gazing at Team Leader Choi with distant eyes, as though remembering something, when a voice came out of nowhere.
“I was thinking the same thing, Johnson.”
It wasn’t Team Leader Choi or me. Naturally, it wasn’t the Skeleton King hiding in my Inventory, either.
Clomp. Clomp.
Heavy footsteps. Wrinkled jeans and a shirt. White hair tangled into a complete mess.
An elderly white man with one side of his face badly distorted strode up to us and thrust out both hands.
“I don’t know which of you two I should shake hands with first, so I’ll do both at once. I’m Chuck Hagel. You can just call me Chuck.”
He didn’t just give off the air of a tough Texan. It practically poured out of him.
His face looked familiar. I stared at it as I took his hand.
“I’m Jin Taekyung. But are you, by any chance...?”
“That Chuck Hagel? Yep. I’m not as famous as you, but I cut down my fair share of monsters back in the day.”
“Oh. Ooooh.”
I’d suspected it when I saw him, but the old man really was the previous generation’s S-rank Hunter known as Uncle Chuck.
I had never imagined I would meet one of the war heroes from the Great Cataclysm whom I had admired as a child. With a cry of delight, I vigorously shook his hand up and down.
“I’m a fan. A real fan. I even collected your Hunter cards in elementary school.”
“Hunter cards? They sold those in South Korea?”
“They probably sold them in North Korea, too. I bought them every time I got my allowance.”
“Huh. So here’s another dumb little kid who handed me a fortune in royalties. Of course, I spent the lot on alimony from five divorces.”
Chuck Hagel smiled contentedly, having demolished a childhood memory in a single sentence.
“If you still have any of my cards, bring them by sometime. I’ll sign them if you want.”
“Ah, I traded them all away.”
“What?”
“I collected ten and traded them for a Cheon Taemin card my friend had. Honestly, Uncle Chuck cards weren’t that rare.”
The smile vanished from Chuck Hagel’s face. He sighed.
“Damn it. And of all people, it had to be Mr. Sky. Can’t argue with that.”
“There’s no comparing their rarity or value. My friend wanted twenty cards at first, but I kept haggling until...”
“...I get it. I get it. You can stop now.”
Chuck Hagel shook his head repeatedly, then shook hands with Team Leader Choi.
“You’re the spitting image of your maternal grandfather. Good to meet you, Choi.”
“It’s a pleasure, Mr. Hagel.”
“I told you to call me Chuck. If you were one of those other idiots with nothing but shit in their heads, that would be different. But you and the traitor beside you have earned the right.”
Look at him calling me a traitor just because I traded some cards.
As I grumbled to myself, Team Leader Choi replied calmly.
“Please understand, Mr. Hagel. I wouldn’t feel comfortable calling the man in charge of the Pentagon—and the United States Secretary of Defense—by his first name.”
“Hm. Is that so? Come to think of it, I suppose you do have to worry about what people think. You’re in charge of two massive Guilds now, after all.”
I blinked.
“The man in charge of the Pentagon? The Secretary of Defense?”
“Hm? You didn’t know?”
“Obviously not.”
“Really? Everyone else seemed to know. I assumed Johnson had at least told you.”
Under the Secretary of Defense’s gaze, the Grand Mage—widely expected to become the next Secretary of Gukbap—scratched his chin.
“I figured you knew, too. Jin, you really didn’t?”
At this point, I felt like I had somehow become an idiot. I replied with some reluctance.
“I really didn’t. Were you appointed a few days ago? Ah, that must be why I hadn’t heard.”
Chuck Hagel’s answer was short and blunt.
“This is my eighth year.”
“Well, you had no particular reason to know. It’s hardly important compared to what we’re about to discuss. Come on, everyone. Follow me.”
Chuck Hagel pulled a cigar from the breast pocket of his dress uniform and put it in his mouth as naturally as could be. He led the way, and we followed.
Each time he puffed on the cigar, acrid smoke rose to the ceiling. An alarm sounded, and a red light began to flash.
Wee-oo! Wee-oo!
Fire hazard! Fire hazard!
Bang!
Chuck Hagel smashed the warning light without a moment’s hesitation.
“Fucking siren.”
Forget tough guy. Forget petty bastard. This man was insane.
The Skeleton King, who had made it through the security checkpoint hidden in my Inventory, whispered,
“Is he human? Are you sure he isn’t a monster?”
I had my doubts, too. But he matched the description on the Hunter cards I’d collected as a kid.
Born in Texas. Dreamed of becoming a cowboy. Supposedly tamed a Minotaur with his fists and rode it around. And that was just the beginning.
Clomp. Clomp.
No one was brave enough to stand in Chuck Hagel’s way as he marched forward without hesitation.

Researchers, Hunters, and employees who appeared to belong to the Pentagon split to either side as if facing a disaster. Moses, who had a cigar in his mouth instead of a staff, crossed between them while spewing smoke like a chimney.
He didn’t forget to talk trash along the way.
“When the hell are they going to widen this damn hallway? Every time I see it, I want to smash it to pieces.”

“Hey, Smith. Put that electronic cigarette away while I’m asking nicely. If you waft that shitty strawberry scent in front of me one more time, I’ll put you on the list of people who died in the line of duty. Cigars are fine, though.”
“Gordon. There’s a smashed warning light in Section Three. Go fix it. Who broke it? Listen carefully: your fucking direct superior.”
No one could stop Chuck Hagel as he rampaged through the Pentagon like an enraged bull.

In the roughly five minutes it took us to reach our destination, poor Smith was forced to change his e-cigarette liquid, innocent Gordon ran off at full speed to repair the warning light, and seven more lights warning of a fire hazard met the same fate beneath the clouds of cigar smoke.
Gordon would probably have to fix those, too.
This guy really was out of his mind.
I was wondering who’d had the insane idea of making him Secretary of Defense when Magic Johnson leaned over and whispered,
“Hey, guys. Chuck’s been touchy lately because of the terrorist problem. He’s a good guy at heart. Cut him some slack.”
The moment he finished speaking, Chuck Hagel slammed his fist into the wall.
“This goddamn hallway! Hallway! Hallway! Didn’t I tell you to make the hallway wider?”
Bang! Bang! Kraaang!
Team Leader Choi watched the hallway widen, then asked with complete sincerity,
“Is he really a good person?”
“...Probably. Whatever he looks like right now, he’s outstanding as Secretary of Defense. Capable, and he gets things done.”
Of course he got things done. Get even slightly on Chuck Hagel’s nerves, and your life would be over.
As Magic Johnson’s answer trailed off with noticeably less confidence, Chuck Hagel passed through a mana-recognition device and pointed to a tightly shut door.
“We’re here already. Everyone, this is Building Five.”
“Building Five?”
“Also called the E-Ring. And for what it’s worth, as far as I know, no foreigner has set foot in here for twenty-five years.”
Chuck Hagel looked at Team Leader Choi and grinned.
“Only one outsider on Earth was ever free to come and go as he pleased. Mr. Sky. He was treated the same as the President of the United States.”
Even without the rest, the fact that Chuck Hagel unfailingly called him “Mr. Sky” said plenty about Cheon Taemin’s standing.
“And now his maternal grandson and a young hero have taken up the baton. Both of you... welcome to Building Five.”
The instant Chuck Hagel finished speaking, brilliant light poured from the entire door.
Whoosh!
No. It wasn’t light. It was magic.
I let the flow of mana sweep over my whole body without resisting it. Dazzling brightness filled my vision, and the space around us warped.
This is...
The moment I realized that this familiar sensation was Teleport, I blinked and found myself in a completely unfamiliar new space.
As my vision rapidly returned, I saw people seated around a pentagonal table.
“Then the forces being deployed to the Middle East front will be... Oh. It seems our guests have finally arrived.”
Beep.
With a mechanical chime, the hologram illuminating the dark conference room disappeared. A neat-looking middle-aged man at the head of the table stopped speaking and rose.
I knew his face at once.
He was a man whose position kept him constantly exposed in every form of media. He looked older than he had on television and radiated even more charisma than he had in the newspapers.
“You’re later than I expected, Secretary Hagel. I hope you haven’t smashed another innocent warning device.”
At the man’s amused remark, Chuck Hagel snapped the glowing tip off his cigar with his fingers.
“Take it out of my salary.”
“The Treasury Secretary asked me to pass on a message. Your entire salary for this month has already gone toward repairing the damage you’ve done to the Pentagon.”
“Damn it. Again? At this rate, I’ll be too afraid of alimony to get divorced.”
Chuck Hagel let out a sighing mutter, then turned toward us.
“No need for introductions, I assume?”
At least this time, there was no need.
Team Leader Choi knew who the man was. So did I. Even the Skeleton King knew.
“Wicked human. Is that old human perhaps...?”
That was right. I gave a small nod as the middle-aged man approached with measured steps, and murmured his name to myself.
Donald Doramp Jr.
His title was better known than his name: President of the United States.

sentences.text: The Pentagon.
The massive pentagon-shaped building was practically impregnable.
A security force of some thousand guards, every one of them a high-ranking Hunter.
Immense flows of mana surrounded the building inside and out.

“Impressive, isn’t it?”
Magic Johnson had just finished the authentication process.
Seeing Team Leader Choi and me looking around wide-eyed, he gave us a knowing grin.
“Since it was first built during World War II, the Pentagon has only been attacked twice.
Once on 9/11, and once during the Great Cataclysm.
You both know how those turned out.”
Team Leader Choi nodded.
“Even the Demon King Asmodeus and his monster army’s all-out assault couldn’t bring it down.”
“That’s right.
It was the second fiercest battle of my life.
The first was the Day of Victory, of course.
Both times, one person helped me escape with my life.”
Any person on Earth, not just an American, knew that fact.
During the Great Cataclysm and afterward, only one person had been able to stop the demon who descended upon this world: the Demon King Asmodeus.
“Cheon Taemin.
If your maternal grandfather—the man Americans call Sky—hadn’t been there, neither I nor this Pentagon would exist today.”
Magic Johnson was gazing at Team Leader Choi with distant eyes, as though remembering something, when a voice came out of nowhere.
“I was thinking the same thing, Johnson.”

Naturally, it wasn’t the Skeleton King hiding in my Inventory, either.
Clomp.

Heavy footsteps.
Wrinkled jeans and a shirt.
White hair tangled into a complete mess.
An elderly white man with one side of his face badly distorted strode up to us and thrust out both hands.
“I don’t know which of you two I should shake hands with first, so I’ll do both at once.
I’m Chuck Hagel.
You can just call me Chuck.”
He didn’t just give off the air of a tough Texan.
It practically poured out of him.
His face looked familiar.
I stared at it as I took his hand.
“I’m Jin Taekyung.
But are you, by any chance...?”
“That Chuck Hagel?
Yep.
I’m not as famous as you, but I cut down my fair share of monsters back in the day.”
“Oh.
Ooooh.”
I’d suspected it when I saw him, but the old man really was the previous generation’s S-rank Hunter known as Uncle Chuck.
I had never imagined I would meet one of the war heroes from the Great Cataclysm whom I had admired as a child.
With a cry of delight, I vigorously shook his hand up and down.
“I’m a fan.
A real fan.
I even collected your Hunter cards in elementary school.”
“Hunter cards?
They sold those in South Korea?”
“They probably sold them in North Korea, too.
I bought them every time I got my allowance.”
“Huh.
So here’s another dumb little kid who handed me a fortune in royalties.
Of course, I spent the lot on alimony from five divorces.”
Chuck Hagel smiled contentedly, having demolished a childhood memory in a single sentence.
“If you still have any of my cards, bring them by sometime.
I’ll sign them if you want.”
“Ah, I traded them all away.”
“What?”
“I collected ten and traded them for a Cheon Taemin card my friend had.
Honestly, Uncle Chuck cards weren’t that rare.”
The smile vanished from Chuck Hagel’s face.
He sighed.
“Damn it.
And of all people, it had to be Mr.
Sky.
Can’t argue with that.”
“There’s no comparing their rarity or value.
My friend wanted twenty cards at first, but I kept haggling until...”
“...I get it.
I get it.
You can stop now.”
Chuck Hagel shook his head repeatedly, then shook hands with Team Leader Choi.
“You’re the spitting image of your maternal grandfather.
Good to meet you, Choi.”
“It’s a pleasure, Mr.
Hagel.”
“I told you to call me Chuck.
If you were one of those other idiots with nothing but shit in their heads, that would be different.
But you and the traitor beside you have earned the right.”
Look at him calling me a traitor just because I traded some cards.
As I grumbled to myself, Team Leader Choi replied calmly.
“Please understand, Mr.
Hagel.
I wouldn’t feel comfortable calling the man in charge of the Pentagon—and the United States Secretary of Defense—by his first name.”
“Hm.
Is that so?
Come to think of it, I suppose you do have to worry about what people think.
You’re in charge of two massive Guilds now, after all.”
I blinked.
“The man in charge of the Pentagon?
The Secretary of Defense?”
“Hm?
You didn’t know?”
“Obviously not.”
“Really?
Everyone else seemed to know.
I assumed Johnson had at least told you.”
Under the Secretary of Defense’s gaze, the Grand Mage—widely expected to become the next Secretary of Gukbap—scratched his chin.
“I figured you knew, too.
Jin, you really didn’t?”
At this point, I felt like I had somehow become an idiot.
I replied with some reluctance.
“I really didn’t.
Were you appointed a few days ago?
Ah, that must be why I hadn’t heard.”
Chuck Hagel’s answer was short and blunt.
“This is my eighth year.”

It’s hardly important compared to what we’re about to discuss.
Come on, everyone.
Follow me.”

chapters.title: Chapter 608
paragraphs: I stared at the middle-aged man before me.
Donald Doramp Jr.

A tycoon with a business empire and a fortune worth trillions of won, he had followed his father, a former U.S. president, into office. They were the third father-and-son pair to hold the presidency in United States history.
Neat as a British gentleman, he looked twenty years younger than he was. His smile as he greeted us was genuine.
“Welcome, both of you.”
Unlike his father, President Doramp wore his hair neatly combed back. We shook his hand.
I’d seen the President of the United States on television and in online articles, but I’d never imagined meeting him. Even with him standing right in front of me, I could hardly believe it.
“Haha, there’s no need to look at me like that. If anything, I’m the one who’s amazed. After hearing so much about you both, I finally get to meet you.”
Team Leader Choi answered in fluent English.
“Thank you for welcoming us, Mr. President.”

“I know a joint national funeral was held in Korea. My condolences to the victims who lost their lives so tragically, and to Mr. Kim, the former Guild Master of the Peace Guild. May they rest in peace.”
President Doramp was a gentleman in manner as well as appearance.
He had already done the proper thing by sending the U.S. ambassador to Korea and the Secretary of State to the funeral. Yet he had remembered to offer his condolences in person, too.
“Come to think of it, you’ve already met the Secretary of State, haven’t you? Isn’t that right, Jesse?”
At his call, the middle-aged woman seated at the pentagonal table smiled and greeted us with a glance.
Only then did it hit me: the people in this room were the ones holding up the superpower that was the United States.
The top brass of the U.S. military and government.
Only a few wore suits. The Secretary of State, whom I’d met briefly at the funeral, was among them. The others were probably cabinet members or held positions just as high.
As for the military...
There are a shitload of them.
It was a feast of stars, literally.
Middle-aged and elderly generals, their hair either going gray or already white, watched us with curiosity. Insignia and stars gleamed on their dress uniforms.
“Ah, I’m late with the introductions.”
President Doramp noticed where I was looking and continued.
“Everyone, this is Mr. Choi, who leads the Peace Guild and Ares Guild. And this is Mr. Jin, whom you all know. As for the people here...”
Jack. Philip. Joey. Liam. Isabella.
Names and titles I’d heard in Hollywood war movies flew past me.
Team Leader Choi seemed to know every face and name, as usual. I just stared and nodded.
How many departments and titles are there?
The only people who stuck in my mind were the directors of the CIA and FBI. Probably because those organizations showed up in movies so often.
“Now that we’ve made the introductions, I should tell you why we brought you here so suddenly.”
Snap. Fwoosh!
The instant President Doramp snapped his fingers, the holograms that had briefly disappeared filled the room in every direction.
This is...
A map. Not of the whole Earth, but a detailed map of one region.
Coordinates hovered over countless buildings and stretches of terrain. Markers whose meaning I couldn’t guess glittered here and there like stars.
Oh.
The place names. The deserts scattered across the map. And what President Doramp had been saying when we arrived.
I put it together and muttered, “The Middle East?”
“It’s a tactical map showing the locations of the terrorist groups. The sparkling markers are probably Gates or their bases.”
Team Leader Choi had spoken almost at the same time as me. President Doramp nodded to us both.
“You’re both right, though Mr. Choi’s answer is more detailed and closer to the mark. The lights indicate suspected terrorist bases. Hologram, zoom out.”
Whoosh.
The enlarged map shrank into a globe. It turned slowly at President Doramp’s gesture, lights large and small scattered across its surface.
“All of those are terrorist groups?”
“When my late father was president, there were already more than a hundred Islamic terrorist organizations alone. After the Great Cataclysm, of course, they multiplied at a frightening rate.”
That was news to me.
More than a hundred Islamic terrorist organizations before the Great Cataclysm. Who knew how many there were now?
Sure, some were probably little groups that operated on the scale of clubs. The problem was, they weren’t meeting to talk about comics. They carried out attacks to kill people.
Seriously, why are there so many?
I knew the world had plenty of lunatics. I’d never imagined there were this many.
Team Leader Choi watched the hologram, his gaze dark.
“Does that exclude the rebel forces scattered across Africa?”
“A good question, Mr. Choi. Fortunately, the rebels are included.”
“Just as you said, Mr. President, that truly is fortunate. And I think I understand why you went out of your way to invite us.”
His voice dropped.
“You’re planning to launch an operation to wipe out the terrorist groups, aren’t you?”
“That’s right.”
President Doramp gave a grave nod.

“As both of you know, the United States is still the world’s greatest power, but that also means we face an equal amount of opposition. Therefore, we have no choice but to act cautiously, both militarily and diplomatically.”

The United States might have a long history as the world’s bully, but even it couldn’t push around every country on Earth. That was especially true after it had suffered the worst losses in the Great Cataclysm.
“But the terrorist groups and rebels operating around the world must be eliminated as soon as possible. I’m sure you both know why.”
Of course I did.
As Magic Johnson had told us, the terrorist groups and African rebels had begun experimenting with Gates and Magic Gems.
I didn’t know what those experiments would produce, or whether they would succeed. But the experiments alone were dangerous enough.
Like nuclear tests.
The whole world paid attention whenever North Korea tested a missile.
Koreans, of course, just thought, Those bastards are at it again, and got on with their day. But that was because we knew they weren’t going to fire at us.
Terrorist groups were as crazy as North Korea. Crazier, even.

“You must have heard from Mr. Johnson. Today alone, terrorist groups carried out the same kind of attack simultaneously in California, Arizona, and Texas. And this isn’t happening only in the United States.”
President Doramp swept a hand through the hologram.
The globe vanished. Dozens of small windows took its place.
“Surrender! Put down your weapons now, and...!” “God is great!” “R-run!” “BOOM!”
Dozens of languages, translated for me by the System, mingled in a deafening clamor.
People of different appearances and skin colors fled explosions or screamed as human bone and flesh sprayed over them.

“There have been thirty-two attempted attacks around the world today alone. Fortunately, as with the incident in Texas that made the news, the damage so far has been minor. But if the terrorist groups complete their experiments with the Gates and Magic Gems in their possession...”
Chuck Hagel, fiddling with his cigar, cut in.
“Fuck. Everything goes to shit. Monster Waves will break out at any time, anywhere, just like what happened in South Korea.”
Magic Johnson spoke with a sigh.

“And the rebels won’t stay quiet, either. They’re just as dangerous as the terrorist groups. They kidnap even children, brainwash them, and use them as soldiers. If it meant taking over a country, they wouldn’t bat an eye even if tens or hundreds of thousands of people died.”
Why did that remind me of the saying that human beings were capable of both the greatest good and the greatest evil?
The bodies of the people who had died before my eyes only weeks ago came back to me. So did their screams. A weight settled in my chest.
“Hmm.”
I glanced sideways at Team Leader Choi with a low hum.
His gaze was deeply sunken as he remembered someone who had left his side not long ago.
That can’t happen again.
I didn’t know how cruel people could become, or how many had to die or be hurt before this insane wheel stopped turning.
But at the same time, I felt relieved. I possessed enough power to stop that endlessly turning wheel, even if only for a moment.
And if I couldn’t stop it...
I’ll break it.
Having already made up my mind, I looked at President Doramp and suddenly spoke.
“When will the operation to wipe them out begin?”
He understood what I meant. A smile spread across his face, and at his signal, someone at the pentagonal table stood.
“Assuming the entire UN Security Council agrees, we estimate that it will take two months at the earliest to complete all preparations. At the longest, it may take more than six months.”
“Two months at the earliest?”
Slow. Far slower than I’d expected.
I frowned.
“Considering how dangerous you’ve said the situation is, doesn’t that seem like an awfully long time?”
“International law leaves us little choice. Deploying troops to countries in the Middle East and Africa without their consent would be a clear violation of their sovereignty.”
“Funny. My modern history textbooks made it look like you fought in the Middle East just fine. I watched a documentary criticizing the oil money involved, too.”
The key government official who had been listening suddenly lost his ability to speak and cleared his throat.
“Ahem... That was because of the 9/11 attacks. Under the new international agreements made after the Great Cataclysm—”
“Never mind. Two months really is the absolute earliest?”
“Ahem. Yes.”
I thought for a moment, then leaned close to President Doramp and whispered.
“Can I ask you something?”
“Anything.”
“Suppose someone nobody could identify—some mysterious stranger, for example—wiped out the African rebels or the terrorist groups in the Middle East. Would that break international law?”
“Pardon?”
“Batman. Spider-Man. Someone like that. And lower your voice before you answer.”
President Doramp stared blankly at me. When he finally caught on, he struggled to get the words out.
“So you’re saying that Mr. Jin would hide his identity and launch an operation against the terrorist groups...?”
“Me? Why would I?”
“But what you just said—”
“I never said that. It was an example.”
“W-wait, Mr. Jin.”
“This man is going to cause a disaster. Why would I do something like that alone? Unless I were some lunatic who stormed into Ares Guild headquarters by himself.”
A suffocating silence filled the room.
President Doramp stared at me as if I were insane. At last, he spoke.
“It seems I misunderstood. What an absurd thought.”
“Right?”
“Yes. In that case, we’ll end today’s meeting here. I’m going to leave the holographic tactical map behind by accident.”
“Ah. An accident.”

“Yes. It’s top-secret—more secret than any other classified information—so it must never be leaked outside. Especially since it contains the precise locations of rebel forces in the Middle East and Africa.”
“Anything else?”
“Everything necessary is in the materials. Not that you’ll have any opportunity to obtain them, Mr. Jin. You’ll be heading straight back to Korea, won’t you, Mr. Johnson?”
Magic Johnson had caught on. He nodded.
“Of course, Mr. President. Though Jin likes to travel. I wonder if it would be all right for me to take a few days off and spend some time with him.”
“Is that so? Is there anywhere you particularly like to—”
“Africa and the Middle East,” I said without drawing breath. “I go crazy for deserts. My dream is to pee in an oasis and give the Sphinx some Churu.”
Team Leader Choi added calmly, “I was born in summer, so I like hot places.”
“Well. What a coincidence.”
“Ready, Choi?”
“Of course, Johnson... No, that sounds a little strange.”
The conversation was bewildering, yet somehow going remarkably smoothly. Chuck Hagel clamped his cigar between his teeth and put an end to it.
“A lunatic is going to kill lunatics.”
He was right. Lunatics ought to die at the hands of a lunatic.
It was an ordinary day.
Muhammad Saladir ad-Din, leader of an armed Islamic terrorist group, had interrogated a foreign prisoner and killed a subordinate who’d gotten mouthy. Then he returned to his bedroom.
Before he could take off his outer clothes, he found an uninvited guest waiting for him.
“Stand up straight, Hassan.”
