“Where is the place with the biggest crowd right now?
I was supposed to meet someone, but that bastard isn’t showing up anywhere, so I’m going to look for him myself.”
“Try over there.” He pointed with his cane.
“I caught a glimpse of it on my way here.
No idea what’s going on, but it was awfully noisy.
Probably something to do with the festival in a few days.”
Then he paused and studied my face with his cloudy eyes.
“By the way, which tribe are you from?”
“What?”
“You don’t look Yao, like me.
Yet you speak our language so well.
How strange...”
“Oh, I can see it over there.
Please be careful on your way.”
“Hey.
Wait.”
I left the old man behind and walked away quickly.
No matter how naturally I blended in, anyone who had enough time to study my face would notice.
The differences between the Han Chinese and Nanman’s other peoples weren’t so pronounced that I’d stand out at a glance, but they were there.
Fortunately, there was a solution.
My hands were very fast.

And as luck would have it, the market was packed with non-Han people, while the merchant selling traditional animal masks was too busy dealing with customers pouring in from every direction to pay attention to anything else.
In short, slipping one mask away was no trouble at all.
Open Inventory.
Store.
Ding.
System You have acquired Crudely Made Tiger Mask!
The hand wasn’t faster than the eye.
The System was.
I put the mask in my Inventory.
By the time I’d passed a couple of people, the tiger mask, painted with crude dye, was on my face.
This should do.
It won’t stand out around here.
Maybe it was because of the festival the old man had mentioned.
Two or three out of every ten people I saw were wearing similar masks.
I headed in the direction he’d pointed and listened to the voices around me.
“Did you hear?
The great chieftains of the Yi and Yao peoples are back.”
“Really?
I heard they went to subdue man-eating beasts about fifteen days ago.”
“They mobilized around five hundred warriors, so they must have finished quickly.
Unlike the Yao people, it seems the great chieftain of the Yi people didn’t achieve any noteworthy results, though.”
“Just what I expected.
Not that I expected much.”
I didn’t miss the familiar information exchanged in their conversation.
The Yi and Yao peoples.

Together with the Miao and Bai peoples—led respectively by the Beast Miao King, lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, and Baeksang, whom I had briefly encountered earlier—the Yi and Yao peoples made up Nanman’s four most powerful tribes.
I remembered what Namho had told me on our way to the Nanman Beast Palace.
Nanman’s four great tribes are the Miao, Bai, Yi, and Yao peoples.
The Miao are the strongest, followed by the Bai.
What about the Yi and Yao?
Twenty or thirty years ago, the Yi would have been ahead.
Sounds like they aren’t anymore.
Times have changed.
Many say the Yi great chieftain, who inherited the position from his late father, lacks resolve.
The Yao, on the other hand, have grown considerably.
They gained an exceptional leader.
I doubt any man they put in her place could have done as much.
Wait.
Are you saying...?
You’ve guessed right.
The Yao great chieftain is a woman.
Extremely intelligent, and extraordinarily beautiful.
My thoughts broke off.
Not because I chose to stop thinking, but because a clear note from a distant instrument reached my ears.
Fwoooosh.
A gentle melody rode Nanman’s hot, humid wind across the open space.
The noisy market fell silent in an instant, and a short exclamation escaped someone’s lips.
It was impossible to hold back.
The melody was that pure, and the procession revealed as people hurriedly stepped aside was splendid and beautiful.
Thump.
Thump.
Thump.
Hundreds of men and women marched to the low beat of drums.
The Yi men wore black tops trimmed with floral cloth and wide, pleated trousers.
The Yao women, in conical hats, walked slowly in two lines.
“Wow.”
“The Yi and Yao have arrived!”
Cheers rose all around me.
But while everyone else admired their beauty and finery, I watched the weapons strapped to their waists and shoulders.
Every one of them is a warrior.
A warrior of Nanman was equivalent to a Murim practitioner in the Central Plains.
Since these people belonged to their respective tribes, it would be more accurate to call them members of a martial sect.
And if the Yi and Yao great chieftains are back from subduing those beasts...
This was more than a procession.
It was a victory parade, and a victory parade needed the generals who had led the battle.
In this case, those generals were the two great chieftains.
“Oh!”
“Th-there...!”
Cries rang out almost as soon as the thought occurred to me.
Gazes and voices turned in one direction, and then the whole crowd erupted into cheers.
“Waaaaah!”
Amid the roar that seemed capable of shaking all of Nanman beyond the Outer Hall, two people finally appeared at the center of the procession and waved their hands.
A man riding an enormous black bear—presumably the Yi great chieftain.
And...
“Yohi!
Great Chieftain Yohi!”
A woman smiling brightly as the crowd lavished her with far more attention and affection than they had the man.
Even without hearing them call her name, I would have known she was the Yao great chieftain.
The Yao great chieftain is a woman.
Extremely intelligent, and extraordinarily beautiful.
Namho had been right.
Yohi was beautiful—almost bewitchingly so.
Whenever her deep gaze swept over the crowd, people gasped in admiration.
That was probably why I stood out.
Amid all those cheers and admiring faces, I was standing there like a block of wood.
Yohi’s eyes lit up when she spotted me.

chapters.title: Chapter 630
paragraphs: I’d let my guard down the moment I covered my face with the mask. That was my mistake.
Should I have stamped my feet and clapped like everyone else?
The thought came too late. Yohi was still looking straight at me.
Still, it shouldn’t be a problem. All I’d done was stand there awkwardly without joining in.
The chances of the Yao people’s great chieftain—the star of this splendid victory parade—showing any further interest in me were close to zero.
“You there.”
I said close to zero. Not zero.
Damn it. She really is calling me.
Yohi was looking straight at me, so I cautiously turned around, just in case.
“Yes. You who just turned around.”
Fortunately, I wasn’t the only one who had turned. Yohi’s sudden call had the whole marketplace murmuring and swiveling their heads like meerkats.
“The person in the tiger mask.”
I swept my eyes over the crowd. There were a dozen or so people in cool-looking tiger masks, including me. Those were reassuring odds.
Good thing I’d bought a tiger mask. Not that I’d paid for it.
“The man standing seven cheok tall, wearing a tiger mask, who just made eye contact with me. That’s enough. Come forward.”
The tiger-mask stock crashed as soon as she added gender and height to the description. My odds of winning had shot up so fast I could feel sweat gathering on my forehead.
I ducked my head to avoid Yohi’s gaze and swiftly, discreetly crossed my legs. Then I tucked my Black Anaconda neatly between them and looked up.
Yohi’s gaze had gone flat.
The procession had stopped. The cheers were gone.
In the suffocating silence, with Yohi and countless others staring at me, I straightened my tightly pressed legs and spoke with all the gravity I could muster.
“Um. Did you call me?”
No one answered. They just looked from my masked face to my lower body and back again.
Shit. I should’ve just stepped forward when she first called me.
A leader needed many qualities. A keen eye was one of them.
“I had a strange feeling the moment I saw you.”
Once the procession celebrating the beast subjugation had ended, Yohi had sent an attendant to summon me privately. Now she went on in a languid voice.
“What should I call it? Out of all those people, you were the only one who seemed out of place.”
Beside her, the great chieftain of the Yi people, who had been popping fruit into his mouth nonstop, grinned broadly and chimed in.
“She’s right. Standing there like a block of wood all by yourself, you were hard to miss.”
He was a plump, middle-aged man who hardly looked like a warrior. He waved a hand wet with fruit juice in greeting.
“And you’re still wearing that mask. Rude fellow. I don’t know who you are, but I expect you already know me. I’m Heugung, leader of the Yi people.”
Heugung. The name meant Black Bear.
That explained the bear he’d ridden in the procession. Apparently, keeping a pet beast named after yourself was the thing to do around here.
What am I supposed to say?
Now that it had come to this, I’d planned to remove my mask and reveal who I was. That was why I hadn’t slipped away earlier. But Yohi was far more perceptive than I’d expected.
“You can leave it on, Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“Hmm?”
“What?”
I was surprised twice over: first that Yohi, who had only just arrived, knew exactly who I was, and then that Heugung, a fellow great chieftain, was even more shocked than I was.
At the sight of Heugung and me both freezing for a moment, Yohi let out a quiet laugh.
“Why are you so surprised? I already heard the Palace Lord let a group of Han Chinese from the Murim Alliance into the Inner Palace.”
Heugung tilted his head.
“Han Chinese from the Murim Alliance? Really? I hadn’t heard.”
“That’s because you’re a foolish bear. Of course, I find that charming about you.”
Even the Skeleton King could have spotted the lip service in that last remark. Heugung grinned happily.
“Do you mean that?”
“Of course. Don’t forget that I’ve always been in love with you.”
Her voice and gaze were alluring. Her pale, flawless fingers—so white and unblemished it was hard to believe she was from Nanman—stroked his pockmarked cheek. Bliss spread across Heugung’s face.
“Ahh. My dear.”
If someone asked me to describe the sight in three words, I’d have an answer ready.
Ugh. Fucking hell...
A potbellied man in his fifties was melting like butter under the touch of a beautiful woman in her twenties.
People said love knew no age or borders. Watching this, I thought we ought to invent some.
Not that this was real love.
Now I could see why the Yi people’s power was falling like a stock headed for delisting—and how the Yao people had grown so strong.
Still... they’re different, but there’s a resemblance.
I was thinking of someone in particular when Yohi glanced at me and stroked Heugung’s shoulder.
“But, oppa...”
“O-oppa?”
I’d heard that line a few times in the daily dramas my mother liked to watch.
Don’t call me Manager. Call me Oppa.
Yohi knew exactly what a troublesome middle-aged man wanted to hear. As Heugung looked ready to die of happiness, she continued gently.
“Would you step outside for a moment? There’s something important I want to ask this Han Chinese man.”
“Hmm? Of course. Of course I will! Anything you want!”
“Thank you, oppa. I’ll see you later.”
“Ooh. Oooooh!”
Heugung left the tent red-faced and snorting with excitement. Yohi gave a quiet laugh, leaned back against the silk bedding, and muttered, “Moron.”
I’d expected something like that, but not quite this much. I scratched my chin, and she lifted one corner of her mouth.
“What? Too obvious?”
When someone was this direct, it made things easier. After a moment’s thought, I answered honestly.
“Well, you’re not wrong.”
“You don’t seem surprised. I suppose you’d already figured it out. I thought you were only good at martial arts, but you’re quicker to catch on than I expected.”
“People like you are rare, but not unheard of. Murim has plenty who aren’t the same inside as they appear on the outside.”
“Really? I suppose the Central Plains must be very large. A bitch like me is rare in Nanman. Oh, is that girl who came with you the same sort? I think I heard her name was... Ju Hwaran?”
I stared at Yohi instead of answering. Her smile deepened.
“All right. I take it back. From your expression, I’d say I shouldn’t have said that.”
I didn’t know what expression I’d made. Probably not a friendly one. I could just feel it.
An odd feeling stirred in me. I made myself speak evenly.
“Watch what you say next time. She’s a member of the Fire Dragon Pavilion who trusted me enough to follow me all the way to Nanman.”
“Oh? Just a subordinate you care about?”
“I don’t really divide people into superiors and subordinates... but think what you want.”
“I appreciate you putting it that way. I happen to have quite a vivid imagination.”
Yohi let out an enigmatic laugh, apparently imagining something, then continued.
“You were staring at me earlier, so I got the wrong idea. I thought you might have fallen for me at first sight.”
“As if. I don’t go falling for just anyone.”
“Then why were you looking at me like that? Did Heugung, that fucking moron, look pathetic to you?”
“No. You reminded me of someone I’d seen before.”
Interest lit her eyes.
“Who? A woman?”
“A woman, yes. You wouldn’t know her even if I told you.”
In truth, she was closer to a monster than a woman. The person Yohi had reminded me of was the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
The people of Dark Heaven were monsters for whom distinctions between men and women meant nothing. Fanatics who worshipped the Lord of Heaven.
“Hmm. A woman... Do we look that much alike?”
“A little. But you’re fundamentally different.”
“How can you be sure? I could be her.”
She looked mischievous, but I’d already checked with Qi Sense just in case. There was no mistaking one for the other.
Like I said, the two of them were fundamentally different.
Yohi’s looks and manner were bewitching. The Southern Heaven Demon Empress possessed a magical power that could beguile people—and I didn’t just mean her looks.
It was the way she carried herself.

There was something distinctive about her: beautiful, yet so natural you never thought to question it. Even I hadn’t sensed the danger in her beauty or her manner until after she’d fooled me completely in Hubei Province.
“Either way, you’re different.”
“Hmm. That’s no fun. Whoever she is, she must be important.”
“She is. And even more dangerous.”
“Dark Heaven. It’s Dark Heaven, isn’t it?”
Yohi was quick. She already knew why I’d come tens of thousands of li from the Central Plains to Nanman, and what I was here to do.
“I’m sorry to tell you, but none of the four great chieftains want to join the alliance. No one except the Palace Lord.”
“What about you?”
“Me? I don’t care either way. Whatever losses the Nanman Beast Palace suffers, I want the Yao people to bring the four great tribes under us.”
“That’s what you want. The other tribal chiefs...”

“Some of them want something else, of course. But most want their own tribes to grow stronger. On that much, I’m certain. If their people shed blood for nothing in the Central Plains, their power here in Nanman will naturally shrink.”

I remembered what the Beast Miao King had told me in the Inner Palace. He was the Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, and one of the Ten Kings recognized even in the Central Plains. In the end, though, he was also the Miao great chieftain.
If the chiefs who held sway over Nanman’s many parts thought like Yohi, then Yayul Mok was right. The Nanman Beast Palace joining the Murim Alliance was all but impossible.
Fuck, these negotiations are a nightmare.
I hadn’t come to Nanman as a diplomat, but this situation was still as good as a failure before it had even begun.
Yohi looked amused by my reaction.

“I’m sorry, but that’s reality. Ah, of course, there’s at least one person you might have a chance of persuading. He leads a tribe large enough to rank among the four great tribes, and he’s so stupid that it’s hard to believe.”
I knew who she meant. I let out a sigh.
“Heugung?”
Yohi burst out laughing.
“Yes, that fucking moron. He can’t do a thing with me and that old man Baeksang keeping him firmly under our thumbs anyway.”
He was still the great chieftain of a huge tribe that raised plenty of bears. Did she really have to treat him like that? Just thinking about him made my heart sink.
And if I actually had a chance of persuading him, she wouldn’t be telling me so helpfully.
Heugung was a puppet, grinning away without realizing Baeksang and Yohi were pulling his strings.
Is she messing with me?
I frowned at Yohi. Outside the tent, people began moving about, and a voice reached us.
“Yohi. Are you in there?”
Cold and dry. It was Baeksang.

chapters.title: Chapter 631
paragraphs: Sometimes you can tell just by meeting someone’s eyes that they dislike you. That no matter how hard you try, you’ll never get along.
My second meeting with Baeksang, great chieftain of the Bai people, felt like that.
Baeksang recognized me at once, even though my face was hidden behind a mask. Given his martial prowess, that wasn’t surprising.
At least early Supreme Peak.

That was my estimate. A Supreme Peak master was hard to find even in the Central Plains. It would have been stranger if a crude tiger mask had fooled him. Once martial artists reached a certain realm, they could recognize someone by their bearing.
The important part wasn’t that Baeksang knew who I was. It was that he wasn’t the least bit pleased to see me.
“So we have an unwelcome guest.”
Unwelcome, was it? If he’d said that when we first met, he might have scratched my tender heart. After everything I’d heard about him, though, I took it fairly calmly.
I scratched the back of my head. “They say you should speak straight even if your mouth is crooked. So, to set the facts straight, I’m not an unwelcome guest. I was invited.”
“Invited?”
His gaze shifted to Yohi. She met his eyes with a sweet smile.
“It’s true. I invited him.”
A beautiful woman’s smile worked wonders in most situations. Baeksang, apparently, wasn’t most people.
“Do you intend to collude with the Han Chinese?”
His voice had grown colder. Yohi shrugged theatrically.
“Collude? I was only a little curious. It’s not as if we were alone from the start.”
“But only you two and the heavens know what you discussed after sending Heugung away.”
“Set your worries aside. I haven’t forgotten the promise we made that day.”
I had no idea what they’d promised each other, but it sounded suspicious enough. Baeksang’s gaze darkened.
“You’re saying pointless things in front of a Han Chinese man, Yohi.”
Fwoosh!
An invisible wave of qi rolled off Baeksang and swept through the tent.
The air grew heavy. Pressure from a Supreme Peak master bore down from every direction, and for the first time, Yohi’s smile began to fade.
That was when I spoke up.
“Hey, the Han Chinese bastard is standing right here and can hear you. How about we stop with the ‘bastard’?”
Whoosh.
The pressure building around us suddenly broke. Baeksang’s eyebrows twitched as my words scattered the waves of qi.
“You bastard.”

“Young Hero Jin. Pavilion Head Jin. Blazing Flame Divine Dragon. Or just ‘you.’ Pick whichever one you like. At this point, I can’t tell whether I’m from the Jin Family of Taiyuan or the Bastard Family of Taiyuan.”

“Good with words, aren’t I? I know. But I trust you realize I didn’t become a Murim Alliance Pavilion Head by running my mouth. Otherwise, my sobriquet wouldn’t be Blazing Flame Divine Dragon. It’d be something like Wind Style: Mouth Dragon.”

That should have made two things clear to Baeksang. First, my martial prowess was in no way beneath his. Second, I wasn’t merely some young Han Chinese. I held a senior position in the Murim Alliance, formed from the martial world of the Central Plains.
Either one was enough to make me someone he couldn’t simply dismiss.
Baeksang studied me in silence for a while.
“Now that I’ve had another look, you’re certainly the successor to the Fire Gate Clan. Speaking and acting without a thought for the consequences... You truly are the Fire King’s disciple.”
“Old Master—no. Have you met my master?”
“The Palace Lord and I were always together. Including the day we first met the Fire King, whom we’d only heard of until then.”
I had a sudden hunch. “Oh. Then were you...?”
“The Palace Lord went down before we could do a thing. I was next. I’d called him a crazy old man, you see.”
Baeksang lifted his white robe slightly, revealing a burn scar on his side.
What was he, a cut of beef with a grade stamped on it?
That’s practically a certification mark.
After showing me the mark left by the piping-hot Fire King hand pie he’d received decades ago, Baeksang continued coldly.
“It was a long time ago. But every time I see this scar, I remember it.”
Jeok Cheongang had once warned me to be careful of gratitude and grudges in Murim. Now the ones he’d incurred in the past were coming back to me like a boomerang.
Is this Murim-style gratitude-and-grudges payback?
For a moment, I had nothing to say. Baeksang stared at me, his gaze dark and steady.
“I don’t care whether you’re the Fire King’s disciple or a Murim Alliance Pavilion Head. Nanman has already shed enough blood for the Central Plains, and the Palace Lord’s judgment is wrong.”
“That is all I have to say. Get out of my sight before I deal with you myself.”
Baeksang’s manner was downright threatening. Rather than argue, I got to my feet.
Not because I was afraid of him, but because there was more to lose than to gain. This was a time to think calmly.
Step.
I was about to leave the tent when I stopped. There was something I wanted to tell Baeksang, and I didn’t know when I’d see him again.
“That blood wasn’t shed for the Central Plains.”
“What?”
“The blood your people shed wasn’t for the Central Plains. It was for the whole world.”
I added quietly, “The same goes for someone’s son.”
Whoosh!
A fierce wave of qi erupted into a gale. Yohi, who had watched our exchange without a word, went pale. The huge tent swayed like a leaf caught in a typhoon.
At the center of it all stood Baeksang, trembling with rage.
Fire blazed in his eyes. His voice seemed to boil. I held his gaze.
Faced with all that fury, I found myself remembering someone who had been buried deep in my memory.
This...
I didn’t know whether this suspicion was true or whether it would end as nothing more than a guess.
But before that, I had to show the proper respect for the reverse scale I had touched.
I bowed my head slightly to Baeksang and left the tent. All the way back to my quarters, I thought about a man who was unmistakably different from Baeksang, yet somehow resembled him.
...The Head Elder.
The Blade of Flowers, Jin Baekyang.
A hero of the Great Faction War born in Shanxi Province. A man who had nearly become Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan despite being the second son.
And a traitor who had spent decades under Dark Heaven’s shadow.
I didn’t know why he’d come to mind at that particular moment.
But perhaps... perhaps...
Damn it. I don’t know.
I let out a long sigh. Ahead, outside the quarters we’d been temporarily assigned in the Inner Palace, Hyuk Mujin was roasting a whole wild boar. I had no idea where he’d gotten it.
Look at him. What a thoughtful little punk.

I gave him a hard time whenever I got the chance, but we’d been through thick and thin together since our days with the Jin Family of Taiyuan. And as a former gate guard, he knew more about the Head Elder than anyone else in the Fire Dragon Pavilion traveling with me.
Maybe he can offer some decent advice.
Just as I was about to wave at him happily, Hyuk Mujin spotted me approaching and abruptly raised one hand, holding a red-hot iron skewer.
“Who goes there?”
Advice, my ass.
I took off the tiger mask. “Put your head to the ground.”
“Oh. Ha ha. I was joking.”
“Good. I’m not. Put your head to the ground.”
Clank.
The skewer slipped from Mujin’s limp hand.
Two days passed in the blink of an eye.

Despite telling us at our first meeting to wait because he would summon us soon, the Beast Miao King hadn’t sent for us once. Yayul Mok, on the other hand, had been visiting more often than I’d expected.
Thump.
White Tiger dropped the wild boar from his jaws and puffed out his chest proudly. I looked at Yayul Mok, who was stroking the tiger’s neck.
“Where’d you catch this one?”
“In the western grass.”
He answered without thinking, then hurried to correct himself.
“...I mean, I found it on the way here.”
“Why bring something you found here?”
“Hmm. It seemed a shame to throw it away?”
“Funny. For something you found, those bite marks on its neck look exactly like a tiger’s.”
“My boy is well trained. He doesn’t bite just anything, beast or human.”
What kind of bullshit was that?
Was this one of those ideas that there were no bad tigers in the world?
I studied White Tiger’s teeth, caked with blood and bits of flesh. “Looks like he’d chew up a beast or a person in one bite. You mean he’s not a picky eater?”
“Anyway, he didn’t do it. Must’ve been another tiger.”
“Then why’s there only one set of bite marks?”
“How should I know? I found it dead by the road and brought it here.”
“Ah, right. A big, healthy wild boar died of natural causes by the road, and White Tiger just went chomp to carry it here?”
“Exactly.”
There came a point when someone was so shameless I didn’t have the energy to answer. I stared at Yayul Mok, then sighed at the mountain-sized boar.
“Another wild boar, though?”
“It’s a wild boar. Is that a problem?”
“The boar again?”
“...Do Han Chinese have no conscience? Think of the trouble I went to catching it and bringing it here. Shut up and eat.”
“Thought you found it.”
“Ah. I misspoke. I found it.”
This bastard was something else.
I only found out later that the meat Mujin had been roasting two days earlier had also come from Yayul Mok. No one had seen him bring it, of course, and he’d stubbornly denied being the one who had.
“Wild boar’s fine for a day or two, but it’s been days of nothing else. I’m sick of it. Sick of it.”
“Then I’ll take it back.”
“Mujin. Get the meat.”
“Yes, sir.”
Yayul Mok and White Tiger gave me identical flat looks. I’d been thick-skinned too long for that to bother me.
Yayul Mok clicked his tongue as Mujin bustled about getting ready to cook, then turned back to me.
“How is your work going?”
I shook my head.
“So you haven’t found anything.”
“Not yet.”
It wasn’t as though I had spent the past two days doing nothing. The Fire Dragon Pavilion members and I had been investigating both inside and outside the Nanman Beast Palace.
I had Ju Hwaran and Hyuk Mujin investigate what was happening in the Inner Palace, while I led the remaining members in scouting the surrounding area.
We might find traces of Dark Heaven.
But despite our efforts, we had nothing to show for it. If there were no traces of Dark Heaven near the Nanman Beast Palace, that was good news. If we simply hadn’t found them, it was another matter.
“For now, we’ll keep looking. At least until the Tribal Grand Council.”
The council, which would bring together all of Nanman’s tribes, was tomorrow. Yayul Mok nodded, then lowered his voice.
“You’d better put it off today.”
“Put it off? Why?”
“The Inner Palace has summoned you.”

chapters.title: Chapter 632
paragraphs: The Inner Palace.
Our quarters were technically part of the Inner Palace too, but I knew at once that wasn’t what Yayul Mok meant.
“Great Hero Yayul is summoning us?”
“Yes. To be precise, he told me to bring only you and that old man.”
Good news. After all this time without a word, the Beast Miao King had finally agreed to my request for a private audience.
But why call for Namho and me alone, rather than the whole Fire Dragon Pavilion?
A thought struck me.
“Do we need to keep out of sight?”
Yayul Mok stared at me in surprise, then gave a small nod.
“You’re quicker on the uptake than I expected. Try not to draw attention on the way.”
“Because the Tribal Grand Council is tomorrow?”
“No. Because most of the tribal chiefs hate you people.”
“It’s true.”
Was he a guillotine in a past life? He’d cut me off before I even got the words out.
I couldn’t deny it, though. I smacked my lips bitterly.
“I get the picture. Great Hero Yayul’s getting pressure from all sides, isn’t he?”
Yayul Mok’s lips moved as if he meant to answer, but his expression hardened and he closed his mouth.
Just as I couldn’t deny what he’d said, he couldn’t deny what I’d said.

Some things had to be acknowledged. Nanman wasn’t the barbaric land people in the Central Plains imagined, and the Beast Miao King wasn’t truly a king. He was one of the great chieftains who represented its people.
If I know that much, there’s no way Mok doesn’t.
Yayul Mok was a decent enough guy, but he was also young and hadn’t entirely outgrown his immaturity.
Then, still looking wounded in his pride, he muttered, “You’re right. Even my father can’t handle all of them alone.”
“What’s that look for?”
“I’m surprised, that’s all. Didn’t think you’d admit it so readily. Have you grown up a little?”
Did our talk two days ago get through to him?
He still snapped at me like a middle schooler going through puberty, but he was much friendlier than when we’d first met. He even went out of his way to catch wild boar for us.
That’s good. The problem is, in this whole enormous land, we’ve got about a millet grain’s worth of people on our side.
I opened my mouth a moment before Yayul Mok could glare at me.
“When and where?”
“Insi. I’ll come get you then.”
“Good. Oh, and while you’re coming...”
“While I’m coming, what?”
“Catch a deer or a roe deer for us. Not another wild boar.”
A day in Murim was divided into twelve shichen, each about two hours long. Insi was the period from three to five in the morning.
Yayul Mok kept his word. While everyone slept, a White Tiger covered head to tail in snow-white fur cut through the darkness and landed outside our quarters.
Thump.
Alongside it lay a dead animal that looked all too familiar.
“Fuck, another wild boar. You’re doing this on purpose, aren’t you?”
“Found it on the way.”
“You keep finding them. What, do you have a wild-boar farm somewhere? Do you water them, let them grow nice and big, then sneak over and seori them?”
Namho looked puzzled. “What is seori? I’ve never heard that word before.”
“It’s a thing. And don’t worry, Old Man Namho. You won’t hear it a second time in this lifetime.”
“So that’s how you Han Chinese talk...”
“Please stop hating Han Chinese people.”
Having politely asked Namho to stop grumbling, I saw Yayul Mok jerk his chin toward the space behind him.
“Get on.”
“The tiger?”
“...Would you rather ride on my shoulders?”
“He looks bad-tempered.”
“That’s prejudice. I’ve been with him since he was a cub. He’s as gentle as can be. Test him if you don’t believe me.”
“Oh. Really?”
I reached out to stroke the White Tiger’s chin—and snatched my hand back like lightning.
Clack!
Its large, sharp teeth snapped shut through empty air. I looked to Yayul Mok for an explanation, and he smacked his lips.
“What a shame.”
“You bastard.”
“I told you to test him if you didn’t believe me. I never said he wouldn’t bite.”
Having spouted nonsense not even a dog would believe, Yayul Mok gently scratched the White Tiger between the eyes.
“Yaho. Yaho, don’t be angry.”
For a moment, I thought he was doing an impression of a hiker on Bukhansan. Then it hit me.
“Wait. Is that his name?”
Yayul Mok nodded proudly.
“Muyaho. Tiger of the mighty wilds.”
“A magnificent name, isn’t it?”
Grrr. Prrr.
Apparently determined to prove it belonged to the cat family, the White Tiger purred. Yayul Mok gazed at it as if he might die from how adorable it was.
“That means he’s in a good mood. You can get on now.”
“...Uh. Sure.”
“Why the look? Is something wrong?”
There is. A little problem only I know about. But I can’t say it here.
I swallowed the words on the tip of my tongue and climbed quietly onto the White Tiger’s back. Namho followed, his face slightly flushed with excitement.
“To think I’d ride a tiger at my age! They say only warriors are allowed to ride them—and this one’s a sacred White Tiger!”
Nothing makes a parent happier than hearing someone praise their child. Yayul Mok, proud mother of Yaho, nodded.
“You know your tigers, old man. Do you like White Tigers?”
“Of course. I’ve always liked them very much.”
No. Stop there. Any further and you’re pushing it.

Just as I waited for the next line with equal parts anticipation and dread, the White Tiger stretched leisurely, seemingly unaffected by carrying three people, then kicked off the ground and raced away.
Papat!
Under the bright moon, the three of us rode the tiger through the dark jungle like a streak of light. We stopped before an old shrine that was falling to pieces.
The air inside the shrine was hot and humid as a steam sauna.
Dust coated the floor. Insects had eaten into the pillars. An oil lamp wavered as though it might go out at any moment, casting a dim light through the room.
At the center of it all, someone was waiting for us.
“I hadn’t been back in so long, I found the place a mess. Then again, it wasn’t in very good shape back then either.”
The Beast Miao King, Yayul Cheok, turned toward us. Unlike when we’d first met, his expression was as faint as the lamplight, though the weariness in it was plain to see.
Perhaps that was why none of us asked why he’d chosen to meet us in an old shrine rather than the Inner Palace’s main hall. Instead, I took up the thread of his wandering thoughts.
“When was that?”
“When I was young. No, younger than young. We were children. Whenever we caused a disaster too big to put right, we hid here from the adults.”
“We?”
“You’ve met him. I imagine you’ve already guessed.”
“Baeksang. Great chieftain of the Bai people.”
The Beast Miao King nodded. “That’s right. Him.”
“I know you’ve been together a long time.”
“Even ‘a long time’ isn’t enough to describe it. We spent our entire lives together. In the grasslands, the swamps, the mountains and fields, and even on the battlefield—we were always together.”
He gazed silently at the wavering lamp for a moment, as though looking back on those days, then gave a small nod.
“Yes. We did.”
“I heard you were inseparable childhood friends and sworn brothers.”
His eyes moved to me. I met his gaze and went on.
“Are you still?”
“Hmm.”
“...Jin Taekyung. Watch your mouth.”
Grrrr.
The crouching White Tiger let out a low growl. The Beast Miao King waved a hand at his son, who had stepped forward to warn me, and studied my face.
“You think we aren’t?”
“It occurred to me that Great Chieftain Baeksang might not see things the way you do, Palace Lord.”
“I don’t know how much you’ve heard, but all sorts of things are happening in the Central Plains. It started in Shanxi Province, where the Jin Family of Taiyuan is.”
I remembered it vividly.

The Shaolin Bloodshed and the Sichuan Blood Tragedy had since overshadowed it, but Dark Heaven had first made its appearance in the Central Plains in Shanxi Province. They manipulated the Mount Heng Sword Sect and its Head Elder into starting a war, and some thousand people lost their lives.
If the Hidden Shadow Pavilion has been keeping him informed, he has to know.
As though he’d read my mind, the Beast Miao King nodded.
“I’ve heard. I’d met the Blade of Flowers, Jin Baekyang, myself.”
“No one saw it coming. It might have been different if he’d been an outsider with no ties to the family. But the Head Elder was our blood kin, one of the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s most senior members.”
That was why Jin Wikyung had trusted the Head Elder to the end despite his suspicions. The Beast Miao King was sharp enough to understand what I was getting at.
“Baeksang... No. It can’t be. He’s not like the Blade of Flowers.”
“No one knows that.”
Namho, who had been watching in silence, spoke up.

“Long ago, I had a subordinate I cherished like family. He was the last descendant of a fallen martial family. The Demonic Cult had killed his parents. Later, when a hundred thousand followers of the Demonic Path rose like wildfire in the west, he joined the Murim Alliance. He never feared death on a mission, and the information he brought back won us more than ten small victories.”
I’d never heard of this Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent. Neither had the rest of the world.
Namho’s face darkened, and so did the story.

“Even after it happened, I couldn’t believe he was a traitor. One day, he sacrificed an arm to bring us information. That information sent more than five thousand Alliance members into the jaws of death.”

“When everything was revealed, he fled. And several days later, I saw the head of a man brought back by the assassination squad. He was grinning from ear to ear, as though something had made him terribly happy.”
His voice faded into silence. Namho sighed deeply before he spoke again.

“This old man isn’t saying the Bai great chieftain serves Dark Heaven. But this is Murim. We can’t see an inch ahead of us. Baeksang. Yohi. Heugung. Or one of the thirty-two tribal chiefs gathering here tomorrow. I wouldn’t be surprised if any one of them turned out to be a traitor.”
For a long time, the Beast Miao King said nothing. He watched the oil lamp sway and right itself, over and over, before turning back to me.
“Are you certain?”
“Of one thing, at least.”
“What?”
“The Southern Heaven Demon Empress. That fucking bitch won’t leave Nanman alone.”
The Beast Miao King let out a low groan before opening his mouth.
“Nanman is no easy target.”
“Were the Sichuan Tang Clan, Shaolin Temple, Emei Sect, and Qingcheng Sect easy fucking pushovers, then?”
“Oh, sorry. I went too far.”
The Beast Miao King let out a hollow laugh at my sudden outburst before answering.
“You really are Old Master Jeok’s disciple.”
“He’d be offended if he heard you say that.”
“He’d secretly love it.”
Okay. He knows Old Man Jeok.
I was giving him a mental thumbs-up when a sudden rush of movement came from outside the shrine.
Whoosh, hiss!
A voice followed, held as low as its owner could manage.
“P-Palace Lord!”
At the same moment, a red warning light went off in my head.
And a System alert sounded.
System Ding.

sentences.text: The Inner Palace.
Our quarters were technically part of the Inner Palace too, but I knew at once that wasn’t what Yayul Mok meant.
“Great Hero Yayul is summoning us?”
“Yes.
To be precise, he told me to bring only you and that old man.”
Good news.
After all this time without a word, the Beast Miao King had finally agreed to my request for a private audience.
But why call for Namho and me alone, rather than the whole Fire Dragon Pavilion?
A thought struck me.
“Do we need to keep out of sight?”
Yayul Mok stared at me in surprise, then gave a small nod.
“You’re quicker on the uptake than I expected.
Try not to draw attention on the way.”
“Because the Tribal Grand Council is tomorrow?”
“No.
Because most of the tribal chiefs hate you people.”
“It’s true.”
Was he a guillotine in a past life?
He’d cut me off before I even got the words out.
I couldn’t deny it, though.
I smacked my lips bitterly.
“I get the picture.
Great Hero Yayul’s getting pressure from all sides, isn’t he?”
Yayul Mok’s lips moved as if he meant to answer, but his expression hardened and he closed his mouth.
Just as I couldn’t deny what he’d said, he couldn’t deny what I’d said.
Some things had to be acknowledged.
Nanman wasn’t the barbaric land people in the Central Plains imagined, and the Beast Miao King wasn’t truly a king.
He was one of the great chieftains who represented its people.
If I know that much, there’s no way Mok doesn’t.
Yayul Mok was a decent enough guy, but he was also young and hadn’t entirely outgrown his immaturity.
Then, still looking wounded in his pride, he muttered, “You’re right.
Even my father can’t handle all of them alone.”
“What’s that look for?”
“I’m surprised, that’s all.
Didn’t think you’d admit it so readily.
Have you grown up a little?”
Did our talk two days ago get through to him?
He still snapped at me like a middle schooler going through puberty, but he was much friendlier than when we’d first met.
He even went out of his way to catch wild boar for us.
That’s good.
The problem is, in this whole enormous land, we’ve got about a millet grain’s worth of people on our side.
I opened my mouth a moment before Yayul Mok could glare at me.
“When and where?”
“Insi.
I’ll come get you then.”
“Good.
Oh, and while you’re coming...”
“While I’m coming, what?”
“Catch a deer or a roe deer for us.
Not another wild boar.”
A day in Murim was divided into twelve shichen, each about two hours long.
Insi was the period from three to five in the morning.
Yayul Mok kept his word.
While everyone slept, a White Tiger covered head to tail in snow-white fur cut through the darkness and landed outside our quarters.
Thump.
Alongside it lay a dead animal that looked all too familiar.
“Fuck, another wild boar.
You’re doing this on purpose, aren’t you?”
“Found it on the way.”
“You keep finding them.
What, do you have a wild-boar farm somewhere?
Do you water them, let them grow nice and big, then sneak over and seori them?”
Namho looked puzzled.
“What is seori?
I’ve never heard that word before.”
“It’s a thing.
And don’t worry, Old Man Namho.
You won’t hear it a second time in this lifetime.”
“So that’s how you Han Chinese talk...”
“Please stop hating Han Chinese people.”
Having politely asked Namho to stop grumbling, I saw Yayul Mok jerk his chin toward the space behind him.
“Get on.”
“The tiger?”
“...Would you rather ride on my shoulders?”
“He looks bad-tempered.”
“That’s prejudice.
I’ve been with him since he was a cub.
He’s as gentle as can be.
Test him if you don’t believe me.”
“Oh.
Really?”
I reached out to stroke the White Tiger’s chin—and snatched my hand back like lightning.
Clack!
Its large, sharp teeth snapped shut through empty air.
I looked to Yayul Mok for an explanation, and he smacked his lips.
“What a shame.”
“You bastard.”
“I told you to test him if you didn’t believe me.
I never said he wouldn’t bite.”
Having spouted nonsense not even a dog would believe, Yayul Mok gently scratched the White Tiger between the eyes.
“Yaho.
Yaho, don’t be angry.”
For a moment, I thought he was doing an impression of a hiker on Bukhansan.
Then it hit me.
“Wait.
Is that his name?”
Yayul Mok nodded proudly.
“Muyaho.
Tiger of the mighty wilds.”
“A magnificent name, isn’t it?”
Grrr.
Prrr.
Apparently determined to prove it belonged to the cat family, the White Tiger purred.
Yayul Mok gazed at it as if he might die from how adorable it was.
“That means he’s in a good mood.
You can get on now.”
Sure.”
“Why the look?
Is something wrong?”
There is.
A little problem only I know about.
But I can’t say it here.
I swallowed the words on the tip of my tongue and climbed quietly onto the White Tiger’s back.
Namho followed, his face slightly flushed with excitement.
“To think I’d ride a tiger at my age!
They say only warriors are allowed to ride them—and this one’s a sacred White Tiger!”
Nothing makes a parent happier than hearing someone praise their child.
Yayul Mok, proud mother of Yaho, nodded.
“You know your tigers, old man.
Do you like White Tigers?”
“Of course.
I’ve always liked them very much.”
No.
Stop there.
Any further and you’re pushing it.

Just as I waited for the next line with equal parts anticipation and dread, the White Tiger stretched leisurely, seemingly unaffected by carrying three people, then kicked off the ground and raced away.
Papat!
Under the bright moon, the three of us rode the tiger through the dark jungle like a streak of light.
We stopped before an old shrine that was falling to pieces.
The air inside the shrine was hot and humid as a steam sauna.
Dust coated the floor.
Insects had eaten into the pillars.
An oil lamp wavered as though it might go out at any moment, casting a dim light through the room.
At the center of it all, someone was waiting for us.
“I hadn’t been back in so long, I found the place a mess.
Then again, it wasn’t in very good shape back then either.”
The Beast Miao King, Yayul Cheok, turned toward us.
Unlike when we’d first met, his expression was as faint as the lamplight, though the weariness in it was plain to see.
Perhaps that was why none of us asked why he’d chosen to meet us in an old shrine rather than the Inner Palace’s main hall.
Instead, I took up the thread of his wandering thoughts.
“When was that?”
“When I was young.
No, younger than young.
We were children.
Whenever we caused a disaster too big to put right, we hid here from the adults.”
“We?”
“You’ve met him.
I imagine you’ve already guessed.”
“Baeksang.
Great chieftain of the Bai people.”
The Beast Miao King nodded.
“That’s right.
Him.”
“I know you’ve been together a long time.”
“Even ‘a long time’ isn’t enough to describe it.
We spent our entire lives together.
In the grasslands, the swamps, the mountains and fields, and even on the battlefield—we were always together.”
He gazed silently at the wavering lamp for a moment, as though looking back on those days, then gave a small nod.

We did.”
“I heard you were inseparable childhood friends and sworn brothers.”
His eyes moved to me.
I met his gaze and went on.
“Are you still?”
“Hmm.”
“...Jin Taekyung.
Watch your mouth.”
Grrrr.
The crouching White Tiger let out a low growl.

“I don’t know how much you’ve heard, but all sorts of things are happening in the Central Plains.

I remembered it vividly.

They manipulated the Mount Heng Sword Sect and its Head Elder into starting a war, and some thousand people lost their lives.
If the Hidden Shadow Pavilion has been keeping him informed, he has to know.

But the Head Elder was our blood kin, one of the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s most senior members.”
That was why Jin Wikyung had trusted the Head Elder to the end despite his suspicions.

No.

“P-Palace Lord!”
The Beast Miao King and Yayul Mok snapped their heads up at the call, which seemed to come from one of the guards.
“Something’s happened at Ailao Mountain...!”
Boom!

Ding.

The frozen time began to move again. Before even a moment had passed, we set out through the predawn darkness for Ailao Mountain.
The warriors of the Nanman Beast Palace were said to grow up alongside fierce beasts.

From childhood, warrior and beast formed a bond. Once a warrior completed the coming-of-age ceremony and was recognized as a full-fledged warrior, they officially became the beast’s owner and companion.
But even a centuries-old tradition had its exceptions.
Whoosh! Rustle!
The Beast Miao King, Yayul Cheok, had no need of a beast’s help. He probably never had, even as a child.
He was the greatest warrior Nanman had ever produced—and a beast in his own right.
Leading us through the dark, overgrown jungle, the Beast Miao King let out a mighty roar.
Gwaaaar!
It was a beast’s roar in every sense: rougher, more savage, and far more primal than Shaolin Temple’s lion’s roar, a supreme technique with the power to subdue demons.
His roar tore through the darkness, carrying the warning farther and faster.
Hundreds of torches flared to life here and there below a distant ridge. Looking down at them, the Beast Miao King shouted to the guards running around him.
“Gisan. Dogok. Go to the Outer Palace. Find the tribal chiefs staying there, reassure the people, and mobilize the warriors to prepare for a possible foreign invasion!”
“Yes, sir!”
“Wonhu. Manjeok. You’re going to the Inner Palace. Mobilize the Miao warriors and guard the palace!”
“At your command!”
“The remaining three of you, find the other great chieftains and inform them of the situation. Tell each of them to mobilize one hundred elite warriors and head for Ailao Mountain!”
He delivered his orders without missing a beat to the Seven Miao Tigers, his personal guard of the Miao people’s finest warriors. Then his gaze moved to his late-born son, running hard behind him.
“Mok.”
“...Yes, Father.”
The darkness around us wasn’t why Yayul Mok looked so grim. He answered faintly, as though he already knew what was coming.
“Go with them,” the Beast Miao King said firmly. “Gather the warriors under the Miao people and raise a force in case of trouble.”
“Have you forgotten? You’re the Miao people’s Young Chieftain and the Nanman Beast Palace’s Young Palace Lord.”
It was a reminder of why this man ruled the Nanman Beast Palace. When we’d first met, he’d seemed as easygoing as a well-fed lion. Now he was a beast with prey right in front of him.
And Yayul Mok wasn’t childish enough to defy his father’s orders at a time like this.
“...I obey, Palace Lord.”
Yet he didn’t leave us at once. He drew close to me as I ran beside the Beast Miao King and made an unexpected offer.
“Take this one with you.”
“Huh?”
Grrr?
He meant White Tiger, which made the offer all the more surprising. Nanman’s warriors considered the beasts at their sides their dearest comrades—and family.
Whoosh!
I ducked a branch rushing toward my face and asked cautiously, “Are you giving him away? Putting him up for adoption?”
“Don’t be ridiculous!”
Grrrr!
“Whoa. Why are you getting so angry? If it’s not, just say no.”
“No! If you save even a little strength, you’ll be more help to Father!”
Gwaaaar!
So much for man and beast understanding each other without words. They were both throwing the same fucking fit.
Still...
It would definitely be much better to ride him.
My reserves of internal energy were considerable even by Central Plains standards, but they weren’t an inexhaustible spring.
If I ended up facing Dark Heaven under the command of the Southern Heaven Demon Empress at Ailao Mountain, then, as Yayul Mok had said, it would be best to conserve as much strength as possible.
Good kid.
I hadn’t been in Nanman long, but I knew what it meant for a warrior to lend someone his beast. I gave Yayul Mok an approving look and decided to offer him a gift in return.
“Here. Don’t turn it down because you feel bad. Give and take, right?”
Rustle!
For a moment, there was only the wind and the sound of branches brushing past us. Namho, whom I was carrying in both arms like a piece of luggage, spoke with a grave expression.
“Am I an object?”
“If you were, I could at least throw you at someone. I can’t even do that with you, Old Man Namho.”
“What an insolent thug. You dare suggest attacking an old man...”
“Quit complaining and go. Your retirement plans are looking bright, so don’t get dragged into this for no reason. And our kids can’t just sit around doing nothing either.”

I wasn’t dismissing him. I was looking out for him. Namho might be a Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent who’d been through every kind of hardship, but he was still an old man who hadn’t learned a single move of martial arts.
He knew it better than anyone. He sighed, his face full of worry.
“I’ll tell the Fire Dragon Pavilion that the Pavilion Master is looking for them.”
“That’s enough. I trust you’ll tell them what to watch out for, too.”
The fuse that was Nanman had finally been lit. The question was who had lit it: an enemy from outside or one within.
Namho’s body had aged, but his mind hadn’t dulled in the slightest. He gave a small nod.
“Pavilion Master, one last thing.”
“Yes?”
“Don’t get hurt.”
“Ah.”
“And dying is even more out of the question.”
I gave him a small smile instead of an answer. Yayul Mok took Namho from me, then, with a glance, kicked off White Tiger’s back and sprang away.
Tap. Whoosh!

A shadow swept through the hazy moonlight. Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers left our group and disappeared into the darkness. The Beast Miao King, racing on all fours like a gigantic brown bear, picked up his pace.
Crack-crack-crack! Smash!
Thick branches snapped, and dense undergrowth was trampled.
I climbed onto White Tiger’s back, which Yayul Mok had left behind, and heard the Beast Miao King’s voice through the wind rushing violently past my ears.
“Do you think Dark Heaven is behind this?”
“We’ll have to get there to know for sure, but the possibility is high. At the very least, it’ll be connected somehow.”
His face had gone rigid. I spoke again.
“What exactly is Ailao Mountain?”
“Forbidden land. No one enters without permission.”
I already knew that much. Namho had told me on the way here, and the System had just said the same thing. The answer didn’t tell me what I wanted to know.
“Isn’t the Nanman Beast Palace the same way? Actually, that seems true of most of Nanman.”
“It’s different. Entirely different. The finest warriors of each tribe go in to keep watch over that place.”
“Why would they need to...?”

“This began more than three hundred years ago, when my ancestors’ ancestors lived in Nanman. For generations, over a hundred tribes had fought and killed one another across this land. Dozens vanished. The descendants who barely survived founded a sect of their own in Nanman’s deepest reaches—and began working with something more dangerous than any blade or beast.”

A conversation I’d had with Jeok Cheongang in Henan several months earlier flashed through my mind. We’d spoken of the Nanman Beast Palace’s history and its connection to the former Sect Leaders of the Fire Gate Clan. That history was also one reason the palace had joined the Great Faction War.
In that case...
There was only one answer.
“Poison,” I murmured. “It was poison.”
“Yes. That was the beginning of the Five Poisons Sect, which would terrorize Nanman for the next hundred years.”
We crossed a towering peak, leaped from a hill, and raced across the tops of the dense trees. The Beast Miao King swept his clawed hand into a thick tree and sent it flying as he continued.

“Countless people died, they say. Dead fish filled the riverbanks. Beasts ate fish that had washed downstream and died too. Poison spread through the wells, and an unknown epidemic broke out. After thousands—tens of thousands—had died, the divided tribes finally gathered beneath one banner and began a new war.”
That was how the Nanman Beast Palace was born.

But death bred death, and vengeance brought more vengeance. While the Nanman Beast Palace and the Five Poisons Sect fought their bitter war, trapped in that unending cycle, a stranger arrived from the distant Central Plains.

“He called himself the Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan. My ancestors had probably never heard the name, but I doubt that mattered to them. The moment he entered Nanman, he burned to death the hundred Five Poisons Sect warriors who attacked him.”
The Sect Leader of that era hadn’t appreciated the Five Poisons Sect’s unexpectedly grand welcome. Like most martial artists, he hated poison, too.
So he planted his ass on the scales of power, crushed the balance, and led the Nanman Beast Palace in reducing the Five Poisons Sect to ashes.
“The problem came after he left.”
The sect’s disciples were reduced to bones, but the venomous beasts and fierce animals they released in their final moments multiplied deep in the mountains where their headquarters had stood.
Slowly. Secretly.
And that former headquarters of the Five Poisons Sect was none other than...
“Right there. Ailao Mountain.”
I looked up, following the Beast Miao King’s pointing finger.
Far in the distance, a black mountain rose into view, its many peaks shrouded in clouds and mist.

I hadn’t been in Nanman long, but I knew what it meant for a warrior to lend someone his beast.
I gave Yayul Mok an approving look and decided to offer him a gift in return.
“Here.
Don’t turn it down because you feel bad.
Give and take, right?”
Rustle!
For a moment, there was only the wind and the sound of branches brushing past us.
Namho, whom I was carrying in both arms like a piece of luggage, spoke with a grave expression.
“Am I an object?”
“If you were, I could at least throw you at someone.
I can’t even do that with you, Old Man Namho.”
“What an insolent thug.
You dare suggest attacking an old man...”
“Quit complaining and go.
Your retirement plans are looking bright, so don’t get dragged into this for no reason.
And our kids can’t just sit around doing nothing either.”
I wasn’t dismissing him.
I was looking out for him.
Namho might be a Hidden Shadow Pavilion agent who’d been through every kind of hardship, but he was still an old man who hadn’t learned a single move of martial arts.
He knew it better than anyone.
He sighed, his face full of worry.
“I’ll tell the Fire Dragon Pavilion that the Pavilion Master is looking for them.”
“That’s enough.
I trust you’ll tell them what to watch out for, too.”
The fuse that was Nanman had finally been lit.
The question was who had lit it: an enemy from outside or one within.
Namho’s body had aged, but his mind hadn’t dulled in the slightest.
He gave a small nod.
“Pavilion Master, one last thing.”
“Yes?”
“Don’t get hurt.”
“Ah.”
“And dying is even more out of the question.”
I gave him a small smile instead of an answer.
Yayul Mok took Namho from me, then, with a glance, kicked off White Tiger’s back and sprang away.
Tap.
Whoosh!
A shadow swept through the hazy moonlight.
Yayul Mok and the Seven Miao Tigers left our group and disappeared into the darkness.
The Beast Miao King, racing on all fours like a gigantic brown bear, picked up his pace.
Crack-crack-crack!
Smash!
Thick branches snapped, and dense undergrowth was trampled.
I climbed onto White Tiger’s back, which Yayul Mok had left behind, and heard the Beast Miao King’s voice through the wind rushing violently past my ears.
“Do you think Dark Heaven is behind this?”
“We’ll have to get there to know for sure, but the possibility is high.
At the very least, it’ll be connected somehow.”
His face had gone rigid.
I spoke again.
“What exactly is Ailao Mountain?”
“Forbidden land.
No one enters without permission.”
I already knew that much.
Namho had told me on the way here, and the System had just said the same thing.
The answer didn’t tell me what I wanted to know.
“Isn’t the Nanman Beast Palace the same way?
Actually, that seems true of most of Nanman.”
“It’s different.
Entirely different.
The finest warriors of each tribe go in to keep watch over that place.”
“Why would they need to...?”
“This began more than three hundred years ago, when my ancestors’ ancestors lived in Nanman.
For generations, over a hundred tribes had fought and killed one another across this land.
Dozens vanished.
The descendants who barely survived founded a sect of their own in Nanman’s deepest reaches—and began working with something more dangerous than any blade or beast.”
A conversation I’d had with Jeok Cheongang in Henan several months earlier flashed through my mind.
We’d spoken of the Nanman Beast Palace’s history and its connection to the former Sect Leaders of the Fire Gate Clan.
That history was also one reason the palace had joined the Great Faction War.
In that case...
There was only one answer.
“Poison,” I murmured.
“It was poison.”
“Yes.
That was the beginning of the Five Poisons Sect, which would terrorize Nanman for the next hundred years.”
We crossed a towering peak, leaped from a hill, and raced across the tops of the dense trees.
The Beast Miao King swept his clawed hand into a thick tree and sent it flying as he continued.
“Countless people died, they say.
Dead fish filled the riverbanks.
Beasts ate fish that had washed downstream and died too.
Poison spread through the wells, and an unknown epidemic broke out.
After thousands—tens of thousands—had died, the divided tribes finally gathered beneath one banner and began a new war.”
That was how the Nanman Beast Palace was born.
But death bred death, and vengeance brought more vengeance.
While the Nanman Beast Palace and the Five Poisons Sect fought their bitter war, trapped in that unending cycle, a stranger arrived from the distant Central Plains.
“He called himself the Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan.
My ancestors had probably never heard the name, but I doubt that mattered to them.
The moment he entered Nanman, he burned to death the hundred Five Poisons Sect warriors who attacked him.”
The Sect Leader of that era hadn’t appreciated the Five Poisons Sect’s unexpectedly grand welcome.
Like most martial artists, he hated poison, too.
So he planted his ass on the scales of power, crushed the balance, and led the Nanman Beast Palace in reducing the Five Poisons Sect to ashes.
“The problem came after he left.”
The sect’s disciples were reduced to bones, but the venomous beasts and fierce animals they released in their final moments multiplied deep in the mountains where their headquarters had stood.
Slowly.
Secretly.
And that former headquarters of the Five Poisons Sect was none other than...
“Right there.
Ailao Mountain.”
I looked up, following the Beast Miao King’s pointing finger.
Far in the distance, a black mountain rose into view, its many peaks shrouded in clouds and mist.

chapters.title: Chapter 634
paragraphs: Papat!
Neither the Beast Miao King nor White Tiger slowed. I narrowed my eyes against the chilly wind sweeping over me.
That’s Ailao Mountain.
Its rugged slopes and deep valleys were unmistakable even from a distance. Countless mist-shrouded peaks rose high enough to pierce the sky.

Perhaps it was the predawn darkness that had yet to lift. Or perhaps it was knowing this had once been the headquarters of the Five Poisons Sect, which had terrorized Nanman long ago. Whatever the reason, Ailao Mountain looked dark and ominous as it drew closer.
Maybe that was why the Beast Miao King’s voice was so low when he spoke.
“The Five Poisons Sect was destroyed by the Palace. But not everything they left behind disappeared.”
If people vanished and left things behind, you could simply burn those things. It was different when they had legs.
“No one knew that whatever the Five Poisons Sect had left behind was still living in the deepest reaches of Ailao Mountain.”
For more than a hundred years.
The Five Poisons Sect’s dark legacy lived on deep within the mountain. In a territory no one else could enter, they devoured one another, bred, and slowly grew in number.
“But our ancestors eventually found out. In a way no one would have wished for.”
Three hundred of Nanman’s elite warriors dissolved into a handful of bloody water. Two great chieftains and a dozen or so tribal chiefs were torn limb from limb.
It happened at a Tribal Grand Council held on Ailao Mountain, exactly one hundred years after the Nanman Beast Palace destroyed the Five Poisons Sect.
“According to the records, the Palace was attacked by venomous beasts and strange predators rarely seen in Nanman—or anywhere else in the world.”
There were deadly poisons with no known antidote, and hundreds of beasts with claws and teeth harder than steel.
The unexpected attack dealt the Nanman Beast Palace devastating losses. They were horrified to find a trace of the Five Poisons Sect, which they had believed was long gone.
“Once again, all of Nanman joined forces. We mobilized every warrior from every tribe, surrounded Ailao Mountain, and set out to kill them.”
But the campaign was only half a success.
They killed hundreds of beasts and burned the venomous creatures, but their own losses were too great. And in the process, divisions began to open among the tribes.
When you think about it, how could they not?
Even if you ordered a single pizza to share, someone would get an extra topping and someone else would get less.
The campaign on Ailao Mountain worked much the same way.

Sensing danger, the venomous creatures and fierce beasts popped up everywhere to attack, as though they’d been possessed by Hong Gil-dong. The tribal chiefs leading the warriors were afraid of how many of their own people they might lose.
They couldn’t exactly say, “Since it’s come to this, let’s have a few people from each tribe die and split it evenly.”
“The tribes grew more divided by the day. As a last resort, we tried fire. It spread beyond the mountain and caused even more damage, but it still wasn’t enough to burn all of Ailao Mountain.”
And so the Nanman Beast Palace had to withdraw. That did not mean they had nothing to show for their losses.

“The Palace suffered terribly, but we reduced the threat just as much. We hunted countless venomous beasts and fierce predators and burned at least part of the mountain. Perhaps the result was only natural.”
“What happened after that?”

“Ailao Mountain went quiet, as if nothing had happened. But this time, no one let down their guard. We declared the entire mountain forbidden land and permanently stationed three hundred elite warriors drawn from the tribes there. Every year, the four great chieftains took turns leading small-scale hunts. That is how we kept the peace for more than a hundred years.”
For the tribal chiefs of the Nanman Beast Palace, it was a reasonable compromise. They could guard against the threat on Ailao Mountain without suffering such terrible losses again.
The problem was...
“I think that peace ends today.”
My voice sank as I pointed ahead.
At the end of the dark, rugged valley, which looked like the entrance to hell, a lone figure sat against a tree.
Whoosh!
The Beast Miao King shot upward like a beam of light, crossed the air, and landed at the mouth of the valley.
I followed close behind. By the time I climbed down from White Tiger’s back, the Beast Miao King was standing before the figure, his face set like stone.
“...We’re too late. He’s already dead.”
I nodded quietly. I would have known even if he hadn’t said it. An indescribable stench had struck my nose before we got within a few steps.
And there was only one cause of death that could produce a smell like that.
Poison. It’s poison.
An incredibly potent poison. The figure slumped against the tree—no, the corpse—gave off a stench, and the ground and grass soaked with the bloody fluid seeping from it had turned black and died.

Unless a martial artist had cultivated Scorching Yang Qi, rooted in the fire qi that countered poison, even an early Peak master would have trouble withstanding the poisonous qi within three zhang of the body.
Grrr.
I soothed White Tiger, whose brow was deeply furrowed, and spoke.
“Do you recognize him?”
“He looks familiar, though I can’t place him. He must be one of the warriors stationed on Ailao Mountain.”
“Do you usually post a guard at the entrance?”
“Of course not. We need every warrior on the mountain in case something happens. It covers such a vast area that there are three or four villages nearby, but the villagers know all this well enough.”
In other words, the area had been strictly controlled for so long that there was no need for another sentry.
Which meant...
He came down from the mountain. He was running from something.
I looked around.
Beyond the thick darkness, faint but unmistakable footprints remained. They were clearly human. I could see no tracks left by a beast or any venomous creature.
There was something else, too.
“There’s a wound. Look at his side.”
As the Beast Miao King said, the clothing at the corpse’s side was torn as though something had clawed it, and the skin beneath was black.
“It wasn’t a weapon. Looks like something rough and powerful barely grazed him, but...”
“That is what makes poison frightening. A small wound can kill in moments.”
He had only been scratched, and it had done this much damage. Was it anything like the Formless Ultimate Poison that had once afflicted Jeok Cheongang?
I took my eyes off the corpse and stared into the dark valley. I had not seen what happened, but I could almost picture it.
Until a short while ago, the nameless warrior must have been running through that rugged valley. Poisoned, stumbling and staggering, he had fled in a panic before dying beneath the tree.
It was tragic. But right now, I needed to know what had killed him.
Was it Dark Heaven? One of Ailao Mountain’s venomous beasts? Or...
A venomous beast from Ailao Mountain controlled by Dark Heaven.
With that question unanswered, I turned to the Beast Miao King.
“In the end, it seems there’s only one answer.”
“Yes.”
His voice was the growl of an enraged beast.
“I’ll see for myself which bastard did this.”
Ding.

It should have been growing light by now, but Ailao Mountain remained steeped in darkness.
And darkness was not the only thing there.
The scent of blood.

The smell had become familiar to me at some point. Now it served as an invisible guide. Following the dead warrior’s footprints through the mountain, the Beast Miao King and I caught the scent on the damp wind and changed course without hesitation.
At last, we found them.
Countless bodies lay scattered across the ridges. The stench of deadly poison overwhelmed even the thick smell of blood.
How many were there? A hundred? More?
The grim possibility that had occurred to me when we found the body in the valley was now before my eyes.
At the horrific sight, the Beast Miao King’s eyes blazed.
“What bastard dares...? I’ll tear him limb from limb!”

For the ruler of the Nanman Beast Palace, it was only natural to be furious. But instead of joining him, I kept as calm as I could. I drew up my internal energy, formed a qi curtain to keep any sound from escaping, and examined the bodies.
Broken bones. Bruises. Severed limbs. Poisoning.

Unlike the first warrior, these people had died in different ways. Some had been killed with their limbs crushed. More than a few had parts of their bodies—their necks, among other things—torn away by some unknown, tremendous force.
Anyone chosen to guard Ailao Mountain must have been skilled.
Yet they had been slaughtered like this.

From what I had seen, the Beast Miao King, Baeksang, and a handful of others stood out, while most Nanman warriors were less skilled than those of the Central Plains. Even so, these elite warriors would have been First Rate at minimum, with some at Supreme First Rate and perhaps a rare Peak master among them.
And Nanman warriors don’t fight alone. With the beasts that accompany them, they should be a match for a major sect of the Central Plains...
I broke off as something felt wrong. Then I saw White Tiger watching our surroundings with a low growl and realized what it was.
The beasts. Where did they go?
The beasts that were always at their warriors’ sides, as inseparable as parts of their own bodies, were gone.
I looked around quickly. Among what had to be more than a hundred human corpses, I could see only three or four dead beasts.
“Why?”
The moment I voiced the question—
Hsssss.
A chilling presence rode the wind toward us, piercing me like an awl.
The Beast Miao King, who had barely managed to contain his rage, and I both turned our heads like lightning.
We saw it. Heard it.
Rustle.
Far away, grass stirred faintly. Darkness rippled as though it were alive. And then—
Grrr.
A low growl, deep as an abyss, came from something crouched in the dark grass.
Step.
In a world that seemed to slow, the darkness moved, trampling the grass beneath it.
Wrapped head to toe in black, it came toward us. It was larger than any beast I had ever seen, and its blue-white eyes held unmistakable anger and majesty.
Black Tiger.
The word flashed through my mind like lightning. At that exact moment, White Tiger’s body began to tremble.
Gwaaaaaaaaaang!
A roar tore through the darkness, shaking heaven and earth. At the same time, a familiar chime rang in my ears.
Ding.
System Ailao Mountain’s Wraith has appeared!

chapters.title: Chapter 635
paragraphs: Ding.
System Ailao Mountain’s Wraith has appeared!
Ailao Mountain’s Wraith.
A being and a name I had never seen or heard of before.
Before I could process the new information, the colossal Black Tiger the System had named Ailao Mountain’s Wraith let out a thunderous roar.
Gwaaaaaaaaaang!
The roar tore through the darkness and echoed across the entire mountain. The air around us rippled like water, and grass and branches shattered.
This was no ordinary beast’s cry.
It was something primal, drawing out the fear hidden deep in the heart and shaking the soul itself.
And I knew the nature of that power better than anyone else in this world.
Fear.
I had known instinctively from the moment I met its blue-white eyes: the enormous creature that had appeared before us could not be fully described as a mere beast.
I knew because, a few months ago in Hubei, I had encountered something like it.
The Water God Dragon.
The master of Dongting Lake, driven mad and stripped of its reason by Dark Heaven. A rare spiritual creature that had entered a new realm after hundreds of years.
I sensed qi like the Water God Dragon’s emanating from the Black Tiger towering like Taishan, and I was not the only one who felt it.
Whine...
By any ordinary standard, White Tiger deserved to be called a spiritual creature. But it was no match for that overwhelming Fear.
While White Tiger whimpered like a frightened puppy, someone else stepped forward without the slightest hesitation.
“Was this your doing?”
Boom!
With a furious shout, the Beast Miao King kicked off the ground. In the blink of an eye, he had covered more than ten zhang.
Radiant light burst from his tightly clenched fist.
Whoooosh!
His fist split the air with a heavy rush. Destructive Force coiled around it like thread, erasing everything in its path.
And at the end of that path...
Slash!
Nothing.
Only empty air.
It had dodged a punch from a Supreme Peak master counted among the Ten Kings.
It had happened in an instant. The Black Tiger moved through the darkness like mist, evading the Beast Miao King’s attack, then swung its enormous front paw, black as night.
Swish!
Unbelievably fast. And powerful.
Boom! Crack-crack-crack!
A deafening impact sent a tremendous shock wave in every direction. Driven back by the force of the blow, the Beast Miao King’s eyes widened.
“What the...?”
He had no time to recover from his shock. A hungry predator did not hesitate before its prey.
Gwaaaaaaaaaang!
Another roar shook Ailao Mountain.
In the modern world, Gates and monsters had become part of everyday life. But the martial artists of this world were not accustomed to Fear.
The Beast Miao King had been caught off guard all the more because he had never encountered a creature so far beyond anything he expected.
“Kh!”
He froze for the barest instant. That was probably the best the Beast Miao King could have managed, but a life-and-death duel between masters could be decided by just such an opening.
That held true even when the opponent was a beast rather than a martial artist.
Whoosh!
In a world that seemed to slow, the Black Tiger’s hooked claws tore through the air.
At that moment, a spear left my hand and streaked across the space between us in a flash of light.
Shreeeek! Boom!
A roar split the heavens. Everything within a radius of more than ten zhang shook.
Qi against qi. Strength against strength.
And I won that brief clash.
Crack!
The Black Tiger flew backward as though it had become one with the spear and vanished beyond the dark forest. In the distance, dozens of towering trees snapped and swayed.
The mountain birds that had long since awakened and must have been watching us in silence took flight all at once, while countless leaves and branches poured down like a rain shower.
Tap. Rustle!
Now was the time to catch it.
But I had barely started after the Black Tiger when I had to stop.
Why can’t I sense it...?
I could not feel its presence. Not even a trace.
All it had left behind was wreckage that looked as though a bomb had gone off, and a spear lying on the ground with its blade shattered.
There were no footprints. No bloodstains.
It got beyond the range of my Qi Sense? That quickly?
As I searched the surroundings, the Beast Miao King arrived with White Tiger. Anger and shame mingled on his face.
“Where is it?”
“It seems to have run away. I can’t find it.”
“...Damn it. You saw me at my worst.”
“I understand. I mean that.”
Mungyeong and Jeok Cheongang had both been shaken for a moment by the Water God Dragon’s Fear.
The Beast Miao King was a formidable master, worthy of his place among the Ten Kings. But comparing him to those two, who had reached a realm beyond humanity, would hardly be fair.
If anything, he had shaken off the Fear faster than I expected.
Maybe growing up in Nanman, surrounded by strange venomous beasts and ferocious animals, had helped. I could not say.
What mattered right now was something else.
“It’s still alive. There’s no blood, so it doesn’t seem to have suffered any significant injury.”
The Beast Miao King nodded at my quiet words.

“I thought as much. When it knew it couldn’t dodge, it bit down on the spearhead at the last moment. A spearhead wreathed in Force, no less. I’ve lived in Nanman all my life, but I’ve never seen or heard of anything like it.”
“I don’t think that’s true.”
“What do you mean?”
“The last part.”
Before he could reply, I went on.
“You may never have seen one, but you’ve heard of one. I’m sure of it.”

“Could it be...?”
“You’re probably thinking of the right thing. Something similar happened in Hubei Province.”
“...You mean that imugi?”
The words came out like a groan. He continued, “The Murim Alliance mentioned it in a letter. But I thought the story sounded far-fetched.”
“Are you really the Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace? Your only son rides around on a White Tiger, and you couldn’t believe that?”
“He rides a White Tiger, not an imugi.”
Fair enough.
An imugi belonged in myth. Even coming from the Murim Alliance, the story would have been hard to believe.

“If that is the case, was that creature that just appeared also the work of the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—that witch?”
“I can’t be sure. But it’s likely.”
Too much about this felt wrong for me to rule it out.

What was it really?
Where were the two hundred warriors who should still have been here, aside from the people now sprawled around us as cold corpses? And where were the ferocious beasts they commanded?
I was slowly scanning the area with a heavy gaze when—
Grrr.
Having barely recovered from the Fear, White Tiger suddenly crouched low and raised its tail high.
The Beast Miao King and I understood what that meant and turned at once.
Far away, the darkness was rippling.
That’s...!
We had both overlooked something while we talked.
An animal’s sense of smell was dozens, even hundreds of times keener than a human’s. A tiger, which usually hunted at night, had a nose to match.
Which meant...
White Tiger can smell farther than my Qi Sense can reach.
The moment it clicked, the Beast Miao King and I kicked off the ground together.
As we chased it, I learned exactly why people called tigers mountain lords.
Ah. Look at that fucking bastard.
I swallowed the curse and glared at the black shape racing far ahead.
No matter how far we ran along the winding ridges, no matter how many cloud- and mist-covered peaks we crossed, we could not catch it.
Its strength, inexhaustible Stamina, and elusive movements kept it ahead of the Beast Miao King and me. Even White Tiger—a spiritual creature with white fur to boast of—could not catch up.
If anything, White Tiger was growing more anxious by the moment.
No wonder. That’s no ordinary tiger.
A mountain lord was not just the king of a mountain. The term could also refer to a mountain spirit. But that creature was no spirit of Ailao Mountain.
It was its wraith. Perhaps something still more ominous: an evil spirit.
What we saw as we pursued the Black Tiger only strengthened that thought.
“That damned beast...!”
The Beast Miao King’s voice seemed to boil like lava. His furious gaze had fallen on bodies with their limbs hanging limp.
Deep valleys. The edges of cliffs. Ravines that must once have run clear but had now been stained black by poison...
The corpses of Nanman warriors lay along our route like signposts. The wind carried a sickening mix of blood and foul odors.
“How dare they? How dare they do something like this!”
A savage wave of qi poured from the Beast Miao King as the horrific sights flashed past us.
He was angrier than ever, and his movements grew rougher with it.
“You bastard!”
Tap-tap—shreeeek!
