But his opponent was a creature called Ailao Mountain’s Wraith. A head-on fight might be another matter; in natural physique and speed, the Beast Miao King could not match it.
Papat!
Just as I expected.
The Black Tiger, far beyond an ordinary spiritual creature, pulled farther ahead instead of being caught. Soon it vanished into a deep, dark valley.
It gave us a look that seemed to say, Come and get me if you dare.
What?
Only then did I slow down and look around.
Ancient trees and vines filled every direction, while the hot, humid air mixed with mist carried the distinctive stench of poison.
I did not know exactly where we were, but after running mindlessly in pursuit of the creature, I could at least guess that we had reached the heart of Ailao Mountain.
This...
I had a bad feeling. A very bad feeling.
But while I slowed, the Beast Miao King charged straight into the valley without a hint of hesitation.
“Great Hero Yayul, wait—!”
Crack!
There was no time to stop him. Even if there had been, he would not have listened.
A little anger could wake a dulled mind. Too much could put it to sleep.
“Damn it.”
I muttered under my breath and looked at White Tiger, which had gone quiet.
It was pacing anxiously at the valley entrance where the Beast Miao King had disappeared, as though it had already sensed the danger. When it met my eyes, it shook its head like a person.
“Was that supposed to mean it’s dangerous?”
Grrr.
“This guy’s pretty smart. We agreed for the first time. But there’s nothing we can do this time.”
Grrr...
“You don’t have to come. Go back from here, and if you run into your master or anyone else, tell them we’re here.”
White Tiger was clever enough to count as a spiritual creature. I trusted it had understood me.
As Yayul Mok had done, I gently stroked it between the eyes, then stepped toward the valley.
Without a trace of fear.
With my head held high.

chapters.title: Chapter 636
paragraphs: The valley was narrow and dark. Trees too old for me to guess their age grew thick enough to block the moonlight, and strange plants and creatures I had never seen before filled the space around me.
Some of them were aggressive, too.
Hiss!
I was moving with my movement technique when I reached out. Something shot from the grass like lightning and writhed in my grip.
Chrit. Chrit!
What is this? A snake?
A closer look told me I was half right.
It was a snake, but no ordinary one. Horns grew from either side of its triangular head.
Wait. Haven’t I seen this somewhere before?
I stared at it and muttered, “Mimi... No, a Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake?”
Chrit.
Why was one here? Wasn’t the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake supposed to be rare even across the whole world?
Now that I look again, it does seem a little different.
Maybe it was because this place was basically China. Knockoffs everywhere.
Compared to Mimi, its body was larger, but its sheen and horns were less impressive.

I stared at the snake in disbelief, then threw it into the distance and picked up speed. Whether it was a Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake or not, I had been right about one thing: this valley was not safe.
Is it a trap after all?

I had spent a little time before entering, and the Black Tiger and the Beast Miao King were already far ahead. At least the Beast Miao King had left tracks here and there. The Black Tiger had left none, as though it really were a wraith.
Swish, swish, swish!
After running for about half a gak, I spotted a vast swamp drawing closer in the distance. A familiar figure stood at its center.
“Great Hero Yayul! Stop! Stop charging in headfirst!”
“...I’ve already stopped.”
He had. The Beast Miao King still looked furious, but he stood perfectly still amid the bodies of venomous beasts and ferocious animals.
“What happened here?”
“They came at me from every direction like mad things. I lost sight of it because of them.”
Humans and beasts alike knew better than to attack someone stronger without good reason. If anything, beasts were more cautious because their instincts were sharper.
Yet these creatures had blocked the Beast Miao King’s path.
“Were they doing it for the Black Tiger?”
“I don’t know. But whatever their reason, it isn’t strange. This land has always been like this. It was probably the same a hundred years ago. Two hundred, too.”
That was an odd answer. He sounded as though he had known about this place all along.
When I gave him a questioning look, he continued, his expression hard.
“In the past, unlike the other tribes, the Five Poisons Sect focused on raising venomous beasts rather than ferocious animals.”

Poison was scorned everywhere, but it was an efficient weapon. Especially for the Five Poisons Sect. They had made enemies of everyone else in Nanman and faced opponents who outnumbered them dozens of times over.

“The place they created was called the Poisonblood Grounds. The most savage and vicious beasts and venomous creatures in all Nanman—perhaps in the entire world—ran rampant there. It was the deadliest and most secret legacy the Five Poisons Sect left behind.”
“Are you saying this is...”
The Beast Miao King nodded.
“The Poisonblood Grounds.”
“Huh. No wonder there wasn’t a path. But it doesn’t seem as dangerous as you made it sound. I can still breathe.”
Granted, I had met a knockoff Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake on the way, and poisonous air seeped into me like carbonation with every breath. So far, though, I was doing all right.
Then the Beast Miao King spoke again.
“Of course. We’re on the outskirts of the Poisonblood Grounds. This is only the entrance.”
“The entrance?”

“According to the records, a little over a hundred years ago, each tribe in Nanman selected only its finest warriors to enter the Poisonblood Grounds. They carried hundreds of jars filled with lamp oil and held poison-warding pearls in their mouths. What do you think happened?”
“I’m guessing they didn’t all come home safely and live happily ever after.”
“Not one returned. The whole undertaking came to nothing. It is the chief reason Ailao Mountain remains forbidden to this day.”
I followed his pointing finger to a huge swamp that stretched for hundreds of zhang. Mist hung over it.
“By the way,” I asked cautiously, “is the fog around here usually green?”
“Of course not. Fog is usually white.”
“That fog is green.”
“Ah. That is because it’s Poison Mist.”
He said it as casually as a mother announcing that dinner was soybean-paste stew. I took a moment to collect myself.
“...Where exactly have you brought me?”
“The Poisonblood Grounds.”
For fuck’s sake. He calls that an answer?
The Beast Miao King smacked his lips at my stare.
“I didn’t know until we came in. Even the records didn’t give the Poisonblood Grounds’ exact location.”
This was a goddamn mess. Wondering whether White Tiger could lead the others this far, I asked, “Then what’s deeper inside?”
“How would I know? Everyone died.”
“That’s incredibly reassuring.”
“Baeksang’s grandfather died there, too. He was Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace at the time. I’ve heard he was the strongest warrior in the history of the Bai people.”

The Palace Lord’s position did not pass down through a single family. Yayul Mok was only the nominal Young Palace Lord. If the position became vacant, the Tribal Grand Council would convene, and one of the great chieftains of the four most powerful tribes would be elected Palace Lord.
“Stronger than you, Great Hero Yayul?”
“I cannot say. The measure of strength changes with the times. But had he lived in my era, I would not be surprised if we had a Beast Bai King instead of a Beast Miao King.”

For the Beast Miao King to speak of him like that, Baeksang’s grandfather must have been at least a Supreme Peak master by Central Plains standards—someone who had opened the Middle Dantian, or gone beyond it.
And a master like that died in the Poisonblood Grounds alongside Nanman’s finest warriors.
And the even bigger problem is that I have to go in there now.
Still...
“We’ve come this far. We can’t turn back now. Let’s go.”
The Beast Miao King looked surprised by how calmly I said it.
“That is unexpected. I thought you would suggest turning back.”
“Someone once said that if a man draws his sword, he should cut through even the Poisonblood Grounds.”
“...Who said that?”
“I did.”
He gave me a dubious look, then grinned.
“Elder Jeok raised his Disciple well.”
“Well, technically, there was a lot of violence and oppression involved... But why get into every little detail? You won’t listen to me no matter what I say, Great Hero Yayul.”
“Did that even need saying?”
Crack.
Bones ground in his tightly clenched fist. His voice turned cold.
“I am the great chieftain of the Miao people, but I am also Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace. I must make someone pay for their blood.”
Perhaps that was why he had become Palace Lord.
I was looking at him in a new light when he spoke again.
“Thank you. For helping me.”
“What else could I do? People died. I couldn’t leave you here alone and go back.”
“Even if Dark Heaven isn’t in there?”
“I’m not that much of a coward.”
A faint smile touched his lips.
“I hear the Central Plains calls men like you chivalrous heroes.”
“People who dislike me usually call me a fucking bastard. I get called a lunatic a lot, too.”
It was true, so I wasn’t offended. Besides, most of the people who had called me those things had died by my hand. People really ought to watch what they say.
A chivalrous hero.
I still didn’t know if I was one. I had done one thing, then another, and somehow ended up here with people calling me that.

A chivalrous hero in the Central Plains. A hero in the modern world. What did it matter? Whatever anyone called me, I had always done what I wanted. Dark Heaven just happened to be something I particularly couldn’t stand.
Fine. Let’s take on whatever’s in there.
Alone, I might have had reason to worry. With the Beast Miao King beside me, we had a chance even if the Southern Heaven Demon Empress was waiting inside.
Step.
I had just finished my thoughts and followed the Beast Miao King into the swamp shrouded in deep green poisonous mist when—
Ding. Ding. Ding.

System Quest condition: Investigate Ailao Mountain Within the Time Limit has been completed! Unexpected Quest: Unknown Omen has been successfully completed! - Quest completion rewards have been granted! - A small amount of EXP and Fame has been acquired! High-Grade Antidote ×20 acquired!
The System notifications came without warning. And they did not stop there.
Ding.

System You have entered the hidden location Poisonblood Grounds! Poisonblood Grounds is the most secret location created by the former Five Poisons Sect. Here, they raised countless venomous beasts and produced deadly poisons that could not be cured. - You have achieved the extremely rare Achievement How’d You Find This? You have acquired a High-Grade Poison-Warding Pearl as an Achievement reward! - A Chain Quest has been created! - Would you like to accept the Quest My Good Sir, Do Not Cross That Swamp?
For fuck’s sake. Look at that quest title.
The longer I stared at the holographic window, the less I wanted to answer. In the end, I nodded.
System Quest My Good Sir, Do Not Cross That Swamp has been accepted!
Then I instinctively sighed in the deep green Poison Mist, and realized—
Beep.
System The penalty effect of Poison Mist has activated!
Something had gone seriously wrong.
Beep! Beep! Beep-beep-beep!

System Poison permeating the air is entering your body through your respiratory tract and skin! - Due to your traits, Myriad-Poison Immunity and Scorching Yang Qi, the penalty from Poisoned has been reduced! - You have been afflicted with the Mildly Poisoned status abnormality! - All stats have decreased by 10! - If Mildly Poisoned persists for a certain length of time, the penalty effect will increase and may even result in death!
One sigh was enough to poison me?
If the poison entered through my skin, holding my breath wouldn’t help, either.
What the fuck kind of bullshit is this?
It was absurd, but I held back. As it happened, I had just the thing for a situation like this.
Open Inventory. Summon.

I took out a ring set with a black jewel that gleamed in the light. It was the Myriad-Poison Ring, a divine artifact of the Sichuan Tang Clan. As soon as I slipped it onto my finger, a System notification told me the status abnormality had been removed. The heaviness that had briefly settled over my body lifted.
Just as I thought.
I smiled contentedly and stroked the Myriad-Poison Ring. Then I noticed someone silently glaring at me and flinched.
“Oh. You startled me. What is it?”
“...Hngh. Poison. Hngh. Don’t talk to me. Hngh.”
Oh, right. He was here too.
I gave the Beast Miao King a flat, chilled stare and tossed him the High-Grade Poison-Warding Pearl I had received as the Achievement completion reward.

At least the Beast Miao King had left tracks here and there.
The Black Tiger had left none, as though it really were a wraith.
Swish, swish, swish!
After running for about half a gak, I spotted a vast swamp drawing closer in the distance.
A familiar figure stood at its center.
“Great Hero Yayul!
Stop!
Stop charging in headfirst!”
“...I’ve already stopped.”
He had.
The Beast Miao King still looked furious, but he stood perfectly still amid the bodies of venomous beasts and ferocious animals.
“What happened here?”
“They came at me from every direction like mad things.
I lost sight of it because of them.”
Humans and beasts alike knew better than to attack someone stronger without good reason.
If anything, beasts were more cautious because their instincts were sharper.
Yet these creatures had blocked the Beast Miao King’s path.
“Were they doing it for the Black Tiger?”
“I don’t know.
But whatever their reason, it isn’t strange.
This land has always been like this.
It was probably the same a hundred years ago.
Two hundred, too.”
That was an odd answer.
He sounded as though he had known about this place all along.
When I gave him a questioning look, he continued, his expression hard.
“In the past, unlike the other tribes, the Five Poisons Sect focused on raising venomous beasts rather than ferocious animals.”
Poison was scorned everywhere, but it was an efficient weapon.
Especially for the Five Poisons Sect.
They had made enemies of everyone else in Nanman and faced opponents who outnumbered them dozens of times over.
“The place they created was called the Poisonblood Grounds.
The most savage and vicious beasts and venomous creatures in all Nanman—perhaps in the entire world—ran rampant there.
It was the deadliest and most secret legacy the Five Poisons Sect left behind.”
“Are you saying this is...”
The Beast Miao King nodded.
“The Poisonblood Grounds.”
“Huh.
No wonder there wasn’t a path.
But it doesn’t seem as dangerous as you made it sound.
I can still breathe.”
Granted, I had met a knockoff Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake on the way, and poisonous air seeped into me like carbonation with every breath.
So far, though, I was doing all right.
Then the Beast Miao King spoke again.
“Of course.
We’re on the outskirts of the Poisonblood Grounds.
This is only the entrance.”
“The entrance?”
“According to the records, a little over a hundred years ago, each tribe in Nanman selected only its finest warriors to enter the Poisonblood Grounds.
They carried hundreds of jars filled with lamp oil and held poison-warding pearls in their mouths.
What do you think happened?”
“I’m guessing they didn’t all come home safely and live happily ever after.”
“Not one returned.
The whole undertaking came to nothing.
It is the chief reason Ailao Mountain remains forbidden to this day.”
I followed his pointing finger to a huge swamp that stretched for hundreds of zhang.
Mist hung over it.
“By the way,” I asked cautiously, “is the fog around here usually green?”
“Of course not.
Fog is usually white.”
“That fog is green.”
“Ah.
That is because it’s Poison Mist.”
He said it as casually as a mother announcing that dinner was soybean-paste stew.
I took a moment to collect myself.
“...Where exactly have you brought me?”
“The Poisonblood Grounds.”
For fuck’s sake.
He calls that an answer?
The Beast Miao King smacked his lips at my stare.
“I didn’t know until we came in.
Even the records didn’t give the Poisonblood Grounds’ exact location.”
This was a goddamn mess.
Wondering whether White Tiger could lead the others this far, I asked, “Then what’s deeper inside?”
“How would I know?
Everyone died.”
“That’s incredibly reassuring.”
“Baeksang’s grandfather died there, too.
He was Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace at the time.
I’ve heard he was the strongest warrior in the history of the Bai people.”
The Palace Lord’s position did not pass down through a single family.
Yayul Mok was only the nominal Young Palace Lord.
If the position became vacant, the Tribal Grand Council would convene, and one of the great chieftains of the four most powerful tribes would be elected Palace Lord.
“Stronger than you, Great Hero Yayul?”
“I cannot say.
The measure of strength changes with the times.
But had he lived in my era, I would not be surprised if we had a Beast Bai King instead of a Beast Miao King.”

For the Beast Miao King to speak of him like that, Baeksang’s grandfather must have been at least a Supreme Peak master by Central Plains standards—someone who had opened the Middle Dantian, or gone beyond it.
And a master like that died in the Poisonblood Grounds alongside Nanman’s finest warriors.
And the even bigger problem is that I have to go in there now.
Still...
“We’ve come this far.
We can’t turn back now.
Let’s go.”
The Beast Miao King looked surprised by how calmly I said it.
“That is unexpected.
I thought you would suggest turning back.”
“Someone once said that if a man draws his sword, he should cut through even the Poisonblood Grounds.”
“...Who said that?”
“I did.”
He gave me a dubious look, then grinned.
“Elder Jeok raised his Disciple well.”
“Well, technically, there was a lot of violence and oppression involved...
But why get into every little detail?
You won’t listen to me no matter what I say, Great Hero Yayul.”
“Did that even need saying?”
Crack.
Bones ground in his tightly clenched fist.
His voice turned cold.
“I am the great chieftain of the Miao people, but I am also Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace.
I must make someone pay for their blood.”
Perhaps that was why he had become Palace Lord.
I was looking at him in a new light when he spoke again.
“Thank you.
For helping me.”
“What else could I do?
People died.
I couldn’t leave you here alone and go back.”
“Even if Dark Heaven isn’t in there?”
“I’m not that much of a coward.”
A faint smile touched his lips.
“I hear the Central Plains calls men like you chivalrous heroes.”
“People who dislike me usually call me a fucking bastard.
I get called a lunatic a lot, too.”
It was true, so I wasn’t offended.
Besides, most of the people who had called me those things had died by my hand.
People really ought to watch what they say.
A chivalrous hero.
I still didn’t know if I was one.
I had done one thing, then another, and somehow ended up here with people calling me that.
A chivalrous hero in the Central Plains.
A hero in the modern world.
What did it matter?
Whatever anyone called me, I had always done what I wanted.
Dark Heaven just happened to be something I particularly couldn’t stand.
Fine.
Let’s take on whatever’s in there.
Alone, I might have had reason to worry.
With the Beast Miao King beside me, we had a chance even if the Southern Heaven Demon Empress was waiting inside.
Step.
I had just finished my thoughts and followed the Beast Miao King into the swamp shrouded in deep green poisonous mist when—
Ding.
Ding.
Ding.
System Quest condition: Investigate Ailao Mountain Within the Time Limit has been completed!
Unexpected Quest: Unknown Omen has been successfully completed! - Quest completion rewards have been granted! - A small amount of EXP and Fame has been acquired!
High-Grade Antidote ×20 acquired!
The System notifications came without warning.
And they did not stop there.
Ding.
System You have entered the hidden location Poisonblood Grounds!
Poisonblood Grounds is the most secret location created by the former Five Poisons Sect.
Here, they raised countless venomous beasts and produced deadly poisons that could not be cured. - You have achieved the extremely rare Achievement How’d You Find This?
You have acquired a High-Grade Poison-Warding Pearl as an Achievement reward! - A Chain Quest has been created! - Would you like to accept the Quest My Good Sir, Do Not Cross That Swamp?
For fuck’s sake.
Look at that quest title.
The longer I stared at the holographic window, the less I wanted to answer.
In the end, I nodded.
System Quest My Good Sir, Do Not Cross That Swamp has been accepted!
Then I instinctively sighed in the deep green Poison Mist, and realized—
Beep.
System The penalty effect of Poison Mist has activated!
Something had gone seriously wrong.
Beep!
Beep!
Beep-beep-beep!

System Poison permeating the air is entering your body through your respiratory tract and skin! - Due to your traits, Myriad-Poison Immunity and Scorching Yang Qi, the penalty from Poisoned has been reduced! - You have been afflicted with the Mildly Poisoned status abnormality! - All stats have decreased by 10! - If Mildly Poisoned persists for a certain length of time, the penalty effect will increase and may even result in death!
One sigh was enough to poison me?
If the poison entered through my skin, holding my breath wouldn’t help, either.
What the fuck kind of bullshit is this?
It was absurd, but I held back.
As it happened, I had just the thing for a situation like this.
Open Inventory.
Summon.
I took out a ring set with a black jewel that gleamed in the light.
It was the Myriad-Poison Ring, a divine artifact of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
As soon as I slipped it onto my finger, a System notification told me the status abnormality had been removed.
The heaviness that had briefly settled over my body lifted.
Just as I thought.
I smiled contentedly and stroked the Myriad-Poison Ring.
Then I noticed someone silently glaring at me and flinched.
“Oh.
You startled me.
What is it?”
“...Hngh.
Poison.
Hngh.
Don’t talk to me.
Hngh.”
Oh, right.
He was here too.
I gave the Beast Miao King a flat, chilled stare and tossed him the High-Grade Poison-Warding Pearl I had received as the Achievement completion reward.

chapters.title: Chapter 637
paragraphs: This was a first.
The first time I had crossed a swamp this long and wide.
The first time I had fought things that weren’t human while breathing Poison Mist like ordinary air.
Splash!
A sudden sound came from behind me. I pivoted smoothly and brought down my straightened hand like a blade.
Slash!
From what I could see, the thing was easily more than three zhang long.
But neither its sharp teeth nor its armor-thick hide could stop the qi in my knife-hand.
The enormous crocodile looked like something from a documentary about the Amazon. It split in half and fell onto the blackened water.
Splash!
The fishy smell of blood and an even fouler stench rose from it, but I only felt sick for a moment. I was holding up much better than I’d expected.
Then again, I’d been covered for some time in slime and blood that smelled worse than sewage.
This isn’t exactly fighting fire with fire.
Nanman Life Pro Tip: If you’re worried about a bad smell, get used to an even worse one.
“...Fuck.”
I had a brief moment of clarity, but the Poisonblood Grounds—shittier than working two shifts loading and unloading trucks—wouldn’t even allow me that much.
Swish!
A snake hidden in the swamp shot toward my neck like an arrow.
The moment it bared its black, razor-sharp fangs and opened its jaws wide toward my thigh—
Whack!
Fingers as thick as the branches of a great tree blew its triangular head away.
No question it was dead. The Beast Miao King caught its limp tail, slammed it into the swamp, and spoke with a grave expression.
“Dohn’ led yer gar’ down.”
“Don’t let my what?”
“Be gareful.”
“...Ah. Right.”
Roughly translated: Don’t let your guard down. Be careful. Something like that.
Nanman’s greatest warrior, now over eighty years old, was speaking less clearly than an eight-year-old because his mouth was stuffed with the poison-warding pearl.
“Almos’ dere.”
That pronunciation sounded awfully familiar.
I wanted to ask if he was from somewhere around Gyeongsang-do, but I held back. This was hardly the time, and just as the Beast Miao King had said, the swamp really was coming to an end.
That didn’t mean things had gotten any better.
Open Quest Window.
Ding.

System Quest My Good Sir, Do Not Cross That Swamp You have entered the Poisonblood Grounds. Deep within Ailao Mountain, once the headquarters of the Five Poisons Sect, lies this most secluded and secret place. It is home to life-forms unknown and undiscovered. A cursed land filled with poison-laden mist and the spirits of countless dead. No one can tell you what awaits beyond it. You have no choice but to see for yourself. Grade: Supreme Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: ??? Reward: ??? Failure: Death
No matter how many times I looked at it, this was ridiculous.
It had been a while since I’d seen a Quest window this short. The mission and reward were a mystery, but one thing was clear: fail and you die.
Then again, it had always worked like that. In the modern world’s Gates and here in Murim alike.
Win and live. Lose and die.
Simple, brutal logic.
Hunters and Murim practitioners alike were people who always lived with one foot in the Sanzu River.
And just as I had every other time, I had no intention of dying now.
Splash.

When the swamp ended, relatively soft ground appeared. Every time the foul-smelling slime fell to the ground in the wake of my and the Beast Miao King’s footsteps, I could see the already blackish earth around us becoming even darker.
“Vile.”
The Beast Miao King spat out the poison-warding pearl and continued as he looked around.
“This is only the second time in my life I’ve seen a place this horrible.”
“What was the first?”
“The Great Faction War. Everywhere we went, there was a hellscape.”
He was comparing the Poisonblood Grounds to a war in which hundreds of thousands had slaughtered one another. That said enough about this place.
Fwoooosh.
Poison Mist rolled toward us over the blackened earth. The Beast Miao King swallowed a groan at the grim sight.
“Damn it. If I’d known this would happen, I’d have trained in poison arts when I was young.”
“You didn’t know. Isn’t that why you never learned them?”
The Beast Miao King nodded regretfully.
“Yes. I thought my own martial arts were enough. It’s why I never learned the beast-taming techniques everyone else studied, either.”
“That makes sense. Why learn something you don’t need?”
I suddenly felt a strange sense of kinship.
In the modern world, people gave up on math or English. In Nanman, they gave up on poison arts or beast taming. For the record, I’d given up on every subject when I took the college entrance exam.
“Come to think of it, I thought everyone in Nanman learned poison arts.”
“If they did, wouldn’t this be the Nanman Poison Palace instead of the Nanman Beast Palace?”

“That is a prejudice held by people from the Central Plains. It is true that the nature of Nanman’s land means we encounter poison easily, but most tribes primarily deal with ferocious beasts. After the Five Poisons Sect rose to power, we rejected poison even more strongly. You can tell just by looking at the divine artifact passed down through our Palace for generations.”
“Oh, I see... Wait.”
What did he just say?
I stopped for a moment and stared at the Beast Miao King. He frowned and looked back at me.
“What?”
“What you just said.”
“That we came to reject poison arts? After the harm this Palace suffered, it was only natural.”
“Not that. The divine artifact. You said there was a divine artifact.”
“Ah. That. I thought you meant something else.”
The Beast Miao King answered as if it were nothing, but from my perspective, it wasn’t something I could simply brush off with an Oh, I see.
“The Nanman Beast Palace had a divine artifact?”
“Any faction with a long history is bound to have one. From what I have seen, that is even truer in the Central Plains.”
He wasn’t wrong. Mid-sized sects and even neighborhood martial arts schools would hang an old iron sword on the wall, call it a divine artifact, and hope it made them look important.
But some objects truly deserved the name.
The Green Jade Buddha Staff was one: the divine artifact of Shaolin Temple, the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim, whose lineage stretched back a thousand years.
And for some reason, Dark Heaven was targeting those very divine artifacts.
They had even caused the major incident known as the Shaolin Bloodshed to do so.
And the Nanman Beast Palace had one too?
As far as I knew, the Palace was more than three hundred years old.
An Outer Lands power formed by an alliance of dozens of tribes, it had arisen in the struggle against the Five Poisons Sect and, after a long war, become the dominant force in Nanman.
It wouldn’t be strange for it to have a divine artifact. What mattered was that this was the first I’d heard of it.
“I’ve never heard that the Nanman Beast Palace had a divine artifact.”
I did my best to sound calm. The Beast Miao King nodded.
“Of course not. It disappeared not long after the Palace was founded.”
“What?”
“Then again, it may never have existed. The Beast King Stone has been passed down from Palace Lord to Palace Lord as a legend. No one can even say for certain it was real.”
“The Beast King Stone...”
Its name alone was extraordinary. The Beast Miao King nodded at my quiet murmur and continued.

“As I said, it is a legend. A divine artifact carried by the first Palace Lord, said to make every ferocious beast under heaven obey him. It supposedly vanished after he and the founding Sect Leader of the Five Poisons Sect grievously wounded each other in battle.”
A stone with the miraculous power to command every ferocious beast under heaven. That was a legend if I’d ever heard one.
And one passed down by word of mouth for hundreds of years, at that.
If I started working on it right now, then in a few hundred years, I could insist that I had been born from an egg.
Still, I should keep the Beast King Stone in mind...
For now, though, it was far more plausible that the Southern Heaven Demon Empress meant to create a “rift” in Nanman than that she was after a legendary stone no one could even prove existed.
“By the way...”
“Yes?”
The Beast Miao King glanced between me and the Poison Mist, then hesitated.
“That. Do you have another one?”
By that, he meant the Myriad-Poison Ring.
I gave him a firm answer.
“No.”
“Then let me borrow it for a moment—”
“Hey, Mr. Yayul. Cut the nonsense and put the poison-warding pearl back in your mouth.”
“...What did you just say?”
“Ah. My tongue slipped for a moment. If you don’t want to get poisoned, keep the poison-warding pearl in your mouth.”
The Beast Miao King shot me a displeased look, but then put the large poison-warding pearl in his mouth without another word.
He might have held the lowest seat among the Ten Kings, but he was still a master worthy of belonging to them.
With martial prowess that had reached such a lofty realm and a vast reserve of internal energy, poison was unlikely to overcome him easily. Even so, a little precaution never hurt.
A High-Grade Poison-Warding Pearl should keep most ordinary poisons from penetrating.
And I had the Myriad-Poison Ring, a divine artifact of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
The Beast Miao King looked at me enviously before stepping into the Poison Mist.
Step.
His footfall sounded unusually loud.
Deep green mist covered everything, so thick I could barely see in front of me. The silence was just as strange.
As if something is watching its prey.
I could feel something watching us through the dense Poison Mist. Why, then, was it quieter here than in the swamp?
I wasn’t the only one who noticed.
—A small patch of grass ten or so zhang away. Northwest. Do you sense it?
A Sound Transmission reached my ear. I gave a small nod.
—The grass beside the rock?
—Yes. Something is there. Could it be...
I thought of Ailao Mountain’s Wraith. The ghostlike presence I had felt from it, and its ray-like movements.
—It isn’t the wraith. Even if it were, we couldn’t catch it from this distance.
—That depends on how we go about it.
The Beast Miao King thrust out a palm like lightning.
Boom!
Compressed air burst outward, scattering the thick mist for an instant.
Through the brief opening, I saw his powerful palm force sweep over the grass like a storm.
And then...
“Guh!”
There was a scream. Not the cry of a beast, but unmistakably the scream of a human.
The Beast Miao King and I stared at each other, eyes wide, then shot toward the source of the cry like lightning.
Whoooosh!
Countless thoughts flashed through my mind as I cut through the mist.
But the first two words that came to me were Dark Heaven.
It’s them.
Who else would be in Ailao Mountain, Nanman’s forbidden land—let alone here in the Poisonblood Grounds?
A jolt ran through my entire body. My heart pounding, I closed the distance of ten or so zhang in an instant.
Then I saw who had been flung out of the grass, and the words escaped me.
“What the hell...?”
Dark red blood stained the corner of his mouth. His eyes were wide open.
There was no doubt that he was a human corpse, but he was wearing clothing that was painfully familiar to both me and someone else.
“...Why is a Bai warrior here?”
The confusion in the Beast Miao King’s hollow voice matched my own. The man who had been alive only moments ago was a Bai warrior.
His body, dressed in white garments like a burial shroud, was tightly wrapped in something sticky and tough.
Rope. No, thread?
The Beast Miao King and I stared, unable to make sense of it.
That was when—
Rustle. Rustle-rustle.
When had they gotten there? Where had they been hiding?
Along with the countless presences approaching from every direction, I suddenly felt darkness settle over my head. I looked up.
At last, I saw them.
Hissss!
Some beings descended like ghosts from a tree so enormous that it was impossible to guess its age.
They had black bodies, countless legs, and stiff hair covering them. The Beast Miao King discovered them and muttered like he was groaning.
“...Thousand-Year Spider.”
The monster of the Poisonblood Grounds had appeared.

I gave him a firm answer.
“No.”
“Then let me borrow it for a moment—”
“Hey, Mr.
Yayul.
Cut the nonsense and put the poison-warding pearl back in your mouth.”
“...What did you just say?”
“Ah.
My tongue slipped for a moment.
If you don’t want to get poisoned, keep the poison-warding pearl in your mouth.”
The Beast Miao King shot me a displeased look, but then put the large poison-warding pearl in his mouth without another word.
He might have held the lowest seat among the Ten Kings, but he was still a master worthy of belonging to them.
With martial prowess that had reached such a lofty realm and a vast reserve of internal energy, poison was unlikely to overcome him easily.
Even so, a little precaution never hurt.
A High-Grade Poison-Warding Pearl should keep most ordinary poisons from penetrating.
And I had the Myriad-Poison Ring, a divine artifact of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
The Beast Miao King looked at me enviously before stepping into the Poison Mist.
Step.
His footfall sounded unusually loud.
Deep green mist covered everything, so thick I could barely see in front of me.
The silence was just as strange.
As if something is watching its prey.
I could feel something watching us through the dense Poison Mist.
Why, then, was it quieter here than in the swamp?
I wasn’t the only one who noticed.
—A small patch of grass ten or so zhang away.
Northwest.
Do you sense it?
A Sound Transmission reached my ear.
I gave a small nod.
—The grass beside the rock?
—Yes.
Something is there.
Could it be...
I thought of Ailao Mountain’s Wraith.
The ghostlike presence I had felt from it, and its ray-like movements.
—It isn’t the wraith.
Even if it were, we couldn’t catch it from this distance.
—That depends on how we go about it.
The Beast Miao King thrust out a palm like lightning.
Boom!
Compressed air burst outward, scattering the thick mist for an instant.
Through the brief opening, I saw his powerful palm force sweep over the grass like a storm.
And then...
“Guh!”
There was a scream.
Not the cry of a beast, but unmistakably the scream of a human.
The Beast Miao King and I stared at each other, eyes wide, then shot toward the source of the cry like lightning.
Whoooosh!
Countless thoughts flashed through my mind as I cut through the mist.
But the first two words that came to me were Dark Heaven.
It’s them.
Who else would be in Ailao Mountain, Nanman’s forbidden land—let alone here in the Poisonblood Grounds?
A jolt ran through my entire body.
My heart pounding, I closed the distance of ten or so zhang in an instant.
Then I saw who had been flung out of the grass, and the words escaped me.
“What the hell...?”
Dark red blood stained the corner of his mouth.
His eyes were wide open.
There was no doubt that he was a human corpse, but he was wearing clothing that was painfully familiar to both me and someone else.
“...Why is a Bai warrior here?”
The confusion in the Beast Miao King’s hollow voice matched my own.
The man who had been alive only moments ago was a Bai warrior.
His body, dressed in white garments like a burial shroud, was tightly wrapped in something sticky and tough.
Rope.
No, thread?
The Beast Miao King and I stared, unable to make sense of it.
That was when—
Rustle.
Rustle-rustle.
When had they gotten there?
Where had they been hiding?
Along with the countless presences approaching from every direction, I suddenly felt darkness settle over my head.
I looked up.
At last, I saw them.
Hissss!
Some beings descended like ghosts from a tree so enormous that it was impossible to guess its age.
They had black bodies, countless legs, and stiff hair covering them.
The Beast Miao King discovered them and muttered like he was groaning.
“...Thousand-Year Spider.”
The monster of the Poisonblood Grounds had appeared.

chapters.title: Chapter 638
paragraphs: Spiders?
I’d seen more than enough of them in my life. Hope Goshiwon had survived the war-torn Great Cataclysm, and all kinds of bugs had infested the place. Spiders were among its most regular guests.
Jinho hyung once said, “Could the landlord of this building be Fabre, by any chance?”
There were enough insects in that building to make you believe an entomologist who’d been dead for nearly two hundred years had come back to life.
But someone once said humans were creatures of adaptation.
At first, I couldn’t stand the spiders appearing at all hours. Before a year had passed, I’d grown used to them. A few years later, I could even tell one species from another.
“Hyung, say hello. This one’s a ghost spider. The one next to it is a Joro spider.”
“Forget saying hello. I get it, so move them away from me.”
“And this one’s a Brazilian wandering spider.”
“I said move it—wait, why the hell is a Brazilian wandering spider wandering around Hope Goshiwon? How does that make any sense?”
“Why wouldn’t it? I fought a goblin yesterday.”
“Ah.”
“And this one’s a tarantula. Must be new here.”
“Is this a nightmare? Why on earth is there a tarantula...?”
What a mysterious goshiwon ecosystem. I’d spent the flower of my youth there among countless spiders. Eventually, we’d been practically neighbors.
But I could say one thing for certain: I’d never seen a spider as hideous or enormous as the one that had just appeared before me.
“...Thousand-Year Spider?”
I’d never heard the name the Beast Miao King had just uttered. And the creature itself was on another level from a tarantula or a Brazilian wandering spider.
What the hell is that...?
If someone asked whether I’d ever seen a spider bigger than a bear, I’d nod without hesitation.
I was looking at one with my own two eyes.
Five of them, in fact.
Skritch, skritch!
Their movements were ghostlike. Every time their eight stiff, hair-covered legs moved, their enormous bodies slid along the trunks of the great trees.
The moment our rapidly approaching figures appeared in the monsters’ eyes, large and small, the Beast Miao King shouted like a thunderclap.
“They’re coming!”
And then—
Shhhhhaaa!
Pale, viscous slime poured down from above, covering a radius of ten or so zhang.
Thanks to the Beast Miao King’s warning, I barely escaped the attack’s range. I stared at the sight before me, eyes wide.
Hissss!
The ground, the rocks, the grass—even the unidentified Bai warrior’s corpse we’d had to leave behind.
Everything the slime touched was melting with a foul stench, as though someone had poured acid over it.
Acid?
If I hadn’t dodged without knowing what it was, or if even a little had touched me, the slime might have melted part of my body on the spot.
Just looking at it sent a chill down my spine. But I couldn’t afford to stand there in shock.
Skritch, skritch!
Among the thick grass. Beyond the dense mist. On the great tree that blotted out the sky.
Five venomous spiders, each bigger than a bear and hideous beyond description, were closing in from every direction.
“...Are they surrounding us?”
The Beast Miao King raised his internal energy as he answered my incredulous mutter.

“Among the countless venomous beasts of Nanman, the Thousand-Year Spider is called a king. More than being ferocious, it is a cunning creature. There is even a record of a thousand warriors once trying to exterminate one, only for it to kill half of them over ten days and nights before vanishing.”
“All that, from a spider? No, wait. If they’ve been around for a thousand years, I guess that makes sense.”
“They are called Thousand-Year Spiders because they can live that long. No one knows how old these particular creatures are. This may be the first time several have appeared at once, too.”
Nanman was home to countless venomous beasts, and five of the monsters called kings had appeared at once.
I looked at the slime that was still melting everything around us and muttered inwardly.
Damn it. We walked right into this.
I thought I understood why we hadn’t found the rest of the Nanman warriors’ bodies—or any sign of the beasts they’d commanded.
After filling their bellies to some degree through hunting, they must have carried the corpses deeper into the Poisonblood Grounds to stockpile food.
Wrapped tight in webs, like that Bai warrior.
They were certainly planning to hunt us the same way.
But...
That’s what you think.
As the creatures closed in with a skin-crawling rustle, I stretched my empty hand into the air.
Open Inventory. Summon.
Ding.
At my command, the boundless warehouse opened its doors. Of all the weapons I’d collected for emergencies, one spear radiating pure white light settled into my hand.
“Did I just see something wrong...?”
“You did. It’s a three-section folding spear, so I usually keep it in my sleeve.”
Leaving the Beast Miao King staring in disbelief, I sent internal energy into White Flame’s lowered spearhead.
Fwoooosh.
Flames of tangible qi bloomed over its edge, which radiated a chilling sharpness.

As the blue flames kindled by Scorching Yang Qi flickered, the dense Poison Mist surrounding us and the five Thousand-Year Spiders that had marked out positions around us and were slowly tightening their noose both flinched as though they had been burned.
Hissss.
Their cries and movements had turned wary. Their beetle-black eyes, some large and some small, darted in every direction.
But it was too late to retreat.
For them. For us.
The die had been cast. One side would live, and the other would die.
And today, we wouldn’t be the ones getting hunted.
“What are you waiting for?” I leveled the blue-flamed spearhead at them. “Get over here already.”
That was the signal.
Shhhhhaaa!
Pale slime came pouring at us from the front, the back, both sides, and overhead. The Beast Miao King and I shot forward to meet it.
Whoooosh!
Wind rushed over my body. The poison that had seeped in through my skin and airways ebbed away, while the flames surging around the silver spearhead burned higher.
Now.
Fwoosh! Kwoooong!
One swing.
I swept the spear around me in a single horizontal strike, and the slime pouring in from every direction evaporated as it met the flames.
And before that, the Beast Miao King’s fist had already shot through the air.
Boom! Hissss!
The slime burst outward with a tremendous explosion, raining acid over several dozen zhang.
But neither of us had lost so much as a hair. We pressed on, leaving everything that was melting behind us.
Whoooosh!
The Beast Miao King went for the Thousand-Year Spider blocking the way ahead. I went for another clinging to the great tree above.
We hadn’t made a plan, but one glance in passing was enough to tell us what the other intended.
Grab.
Just as I kicked off into the air, a large palm caught the tip of my foot.
Muscles that belied the Beast Miao King’s eighty-plus years rippled through his arm. With a thunderous shout, he drove my foot upward with the force of a shot put.
“Go!”
Whoooosh!
Weightlessness swept through me.
I hurtled upward, faster and harder than I could have managed with ordinary Stepping on Empty Air. In an instant, I was right in front of the eight-legged monster’s face.
A multitude of emotions could be read in its many eyes, both large and small.
The Thousand-Year Spider looked almost human in its shock as I brought the spearhead down.
Swish! Slash!
A streak of flame cut through the air. Sticky blood sprayed.
The spider sacrificed three of its eight legs, each harder than steel, to survive the blow. It hastily spat slime at me.
Splatter! Hissss!
My quick movements and the Scorching Yang Qi that countered its poison helped me avoid the spray, but I’d been too close. Even what brushed my skin and clothes brought a searing pain.
Rather than groan, I drove my spear into its enormous body as it tried to escape.
Crack! Thrust!
Unlike insects, spiders are arthropods with thin exoskeletons. Their bodies aren’t especially hard.
Even a Thousand-Year Spider, king of the venomous beasts, couldn’t withstand Force.
“Fuck, you think I’ve only killed one or two spiders? If you’d lived in Hope Goshiwon, your whole extended family—in-laws and eighth cousins included—would’ve died by my hand.”
—Kiiiiiieet!
Its enormous body writhed as it shrieked.
I dodged another blast of slime, then caught the leg sweeping toward my side and tore it off with my bare hand.
Crack!
—Kieeeet!
Once, maybe. I wasn’t getting caught by the same move twice.
The Thousand-Year Spider was convulsing now, not merely struggling. I drove the spearhead into its head.
Thrust!
Its flailing legs went limp. Its enormous body stiffened.
A notification sounded, confirming what I’d suspected.
Ding.

System Defeated Lv. 117 Thousand-Year Spider! - Gained a substantial amount of EXP and Fame! - The Thousand-Year Spider is a special existence among the countless venomous beasts. An additional Reward will be granted! - Achieved the rare Achievement Indiscriminate Hunting Bug! - When facing insect-form enemies in the future, you will gain additional stats!
The System notifications poured in as though they’d been waiting. But I had no time to read every line of the holographic window.
Below the great tree I stood on, the Beast Miao King was fighting for his life against several spiders at once.
Hissss!
“You bastards! Even tearing you to pieces wouldn’t be enough! How dare you do this to my hair!”
His hair. He was worried about his hair at a time like this.
Half his clothes had melted away, exposing patches of skin, and the slime had eaten through almost all of his once-thick hair.
Even so, true to his title as one of the Ten Kings, he had already killed one and was fighting three at once.
Wham!
Correction. Two.
The moment the Beast Miao King’s fist, thrown with a savage aura, smashed one of the Thousand-Year Spiders apart, I kicked off the great tree and plunged toward the ground like a bolt of lightning.
Whooosh! Crack!
My spearhead sank into a Thousand-Year Spider’s body as though it were tofu. Then the powerful Scorching Yang Qi I’d drawn from my dantian surged inside it.
Fwoosh. Boom!
Its enormous body exploded into pieces. A torrent of bodily fluid sprayed out and evaporated. Only a new System notification remained above the unrecognizable corpse.
Ding.
System Defeated Lv. 109 Thousand-Year Spider! - Gained a substantial amount of EXP and Fame! - You have gained bonus EXP for defeating another extremely rare creature! Level Up!
Fwoooosh.
Invisible healing light swept through me.

The skin melted by the slime and the internal energy I had expended were restored, while the flames on the spearhead, which had been slowly dying down, suddenly blazed as fiercely as though they had never weakened.
Fwoosh.
—Sssssss...
The last Thousand-Year Spider stared fearfully at the blue flames in the darkness. Then it fled.
Pat-pat-pat!
All eight legs kicked off the ground at once. Its huge body leaped into the air, stepped on something invisible, and settled lightly onto it.
That was when I caught sight of something glinting beyond the flames lighting up the darkness.
A spiderweb?
The thought flashed through my mind as the Beast Miao King and I raced after the fleeing spider.

chapters.title: Chapter 639
paragraphs: When I thought about it, it made sense.

No matter how extraordinary a venomous beast a Thousand-Year Spider was, it was still a spider. Webs covered the Poisonblood Grounds, which might as well have been its home. The last survivor of the five Thousand-Year Spider siblings had lost all will to fight and was fleeing along them.
What I hadn’t expected was...
Thump! Shhhhk!
...how fast that enormous spider could run.
...What the hell? How is it that fast?

Maybe it was moving so quickly because it was fleeing for its life. Or maybe it had laid webs everywhere for just such an emergency. Either way, we could barely close the distance. It raced between the great trees and the open air dozens of zhang above us, with no obvious way for us to catch it.
No wonder Spider-Man’s so fast...
I was using my movement technique when an inexplicable chill swept through me. I ducked on instinct.
Slice!
With a sharp cutting sound, a handful of hair drifted through the air. A web had narrowly missed my head. Tough and elastic as steel wire, it had become razor-sharp at that speed.
“Great Hero Yayul!”
I shouted a warning as soon as I realized what had happened, but the Beast Miao King was bigger than me and moved more roughly. He reacted a little too late.
Slice!
What was that, a razor commercial?
The top of his head had been shaved clean instead of his flesh and bone. He answered me with a look of utter misery.
“...Why did you call me?”
“...No reason. Just felt like it.”

The thick hair that had streamed behind him like a lion’s mane was gone. Between the Thousand-Year Spiders’ barrages of acid-laden phlegm and this web, the crown of his head had been stripped bare. It gleamed like an octopus that had just come ashore.
Is this a battle between Doctor Octopus and Spider-Man?
The good and evil sides seemed to be reversed, but still. Watching a superhero movie play out right in front of me made my heart swell.
The Octopus Miao King, whose hair was looking considerably less impressive, was not enjoying himself. His fury reached the heavens.
“You bastard! How dare you!”

His hair wasn’t the only reason, of course. The warriors might have belonged to different tribes, but hundreds of them—people who were practically his own—had died overnight. Savage energy spilled from his bloodshot eyes.
Kra-boom!
The Beast Miao King stamped his foot. The ground, sodden with poison and moisture, caved in beneath him like a sinkhole. Using the tremendous force of the rebound, he leaped high and threw a punch.
Whoooom! Bang!
Compressed air burst outward. The wind rippled.
Fist Energy tore through the air, severing webs hidden in the darkness as it shot toward the Thousand-Year Spider.
Shreeeek! Shhk!
But the blow missed. The spider narrowly escaped death and let out a chilling cry.
—Ssssssissss!
It was no ordinary cry. The strange noise burrowed into my ears like Sound Transmission and spread through the air. My sharpened senses picked up movement everywhere.
This is...
Rustle.

Amid the Poison Mist that had turned the Poisonblood Grounds into a land of death, the blackened grass stirred. Things emerged from between ancient trees, and I remembered a phrase I had briefly forgotten.
King of the venomous beasts.
It described the Thousand-Year Spider perfectly.
Venomous beasts had been crouching throughout the Poisonblood Grounds, waiting for orders. Now they answered their king’s call, gathering in a vast army that blocked our way.
Slither. Ssssss!
Snakes and centipedes as long and enormous as whips. Spiders and toads the size of human heads. Hundreds of bees pouring out from somewhere among the leaves of the great trees.
Hideous venomous beasts of kinds I couldn’t identify—and didn’t want to—converged. In the blink of an eye, dozens became hundreds, and hundreds became thousands. Together, they formed a wall.
Kraaaaa!
They blocked the only path through the Poisonblood Grounds, then surged toward us in a massive triangular wave.
Above them, the Thousand-Year Spider stood on a web much lower than before and looked down at us. It had stopped running. Now it gazed down like a king.
“Fucking bastard,” I muttered. “Now you want to look cool?”
This must have been its plan from the start.
Nanman really was a goddamn place. Why were its beasts and spiders so cunning?

I had entered the Poisonblood Grounds following the Black Tiger known as Ailao Mountain’s Wraith. The Thousand-Year Spider we encountered there had finally summoned all its guards once it reached a battlefield favorable to itself.
Judging by everything I had seen firsthand, its intelligence was in no way inferior to an ordinary human’s.
Compared to a certain glutton, it’s Einstein.
Taishan came to mind. I turned to the Beast Miao King.
Even he, after a lifetime in Nanman, seemed never to have seen anything like this. He let out a low groan. When our eyes met, his expression hardened.
“There’s no need to be afraid. Neither of us will die here.”
Afraid?
I gave a quiet laugh instead of answering. I couldn’t think of a word that was at once so close to me and so far away.
I’d always thought of myself as a coward, yet I’d never once backed down when faced with death.
At first, I became a Hunter because I wasn’t afraid. Later, I learned martial arts because I was.
Strange. I fought with everything I had because I was afraid of dying, but I kept walking into battlefields where I could die at any moment.
Still... today, at least, I didn’t think I would die.
Kraaaaaaaaa!
I watched the wave of venomous beasts roll closer, then spoke.
“When those things are gone, kill it immediately. No—just hurt it enough to leave it barely breathing.”
“What?”
“Remember, you can’t hesitate. We have to get it now, while it’s let its guard down and come lower.”
“What are you—”
Now.
Instead of answering, I stepped lightly against the ground. Internal energy was already surging from my dantian toward my toes.
Slither. Boom!
Compression. Then explosion.

The internal energy that burst from a single point—the tip of my toe—gave my entire body the speed of a beam of light. At the same time, a fierce gale wrapped around me and scattered the deep green Poison Mist.
Beyond it waited a colossal wall of thousands of venomous beasts.
Kraaaaaa!
A thick shadow fell over my head. The already dark Poisonblood Grounds plunged into complete darkness.
Then brilliant light burst from the blade of White Flame, the spear in my hand.
Vooooom.
With a hum like a swarm of bees, flames bluer than the sky took hold. Three jiazi’s worth of powerful Scorching Yang Qi drew together, linked and coalesced into a still greater hellfire.
And at the end of it all—
One Annihilation.
Ruuuumble!
A flash tore through the darkness. A roar shook earth and sky.
Since childhood, Beast Miao King Yayul Cheok had thought of himself as a wild man.
He was rough and unrefined, with no use for etiquette or elegant manners. But perhaps it was true that a position shaped the person.

As the years went by, he found himself responsible for leading others. People began following him, though he couldn’t see what there was in him worth following. Eventually he became Great Chieftain of the Bai people. Then one day he looked around and found himself Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace.
How did that happen?
He had no idea. All he’d done his entire life was train in martial arts.
But the water had been spilled long ago. There was no turning back and no gathering it up again, so he did his best to fulfill his duties as Palace Lord.
He stopped beating people up. He even cut back on the swearing that had once come as naturally as breathing.

Slapping a tribal chieftain who couldn’t understand a damn thing he was told might bring him peace of mind. But if he slapped the man hard enough to deafen him permanently, that chieftain would rebel against the Nanman Beast Palace.
Years as Palace Lord had made the Beast Miao King much tamer. Even so, at the sight before him, his lips began moving of their own accord.
“Uh... what the fuck is that? Uh...”
Ruuuumble!
Everything broke apart and melted.
The wave of thousands of venomous beasts was shattering before his eyes.

The two-headed horn snakes that hunted bears whenever they grew bored. The black frogs whose poison could kill a hundred bulls with a single drop. The golden bees said to strip a tiger to its bones in half a gak.
Fwoosh! Kraaaaaa!
Thousands of venomous beasts, every bit as powerful as they were hideous, turned to ash in the blue flames and the thunderous roar that lit the darkness.
...This is insane.
Not since the Great Faction War, more than fifty years ago, had he seen anything so astonishing.

Even the final ultimate technique unleashed by the Demonic Cult’s Sword Demon just before his death could not compare with the sight before him. And even Fire King Jeok Cheongang, who had easily dodged the Sword Demon’s final strike and methodically trampled him until he was on the verge of death, had never displayed this level of destructive power.
Nor, of course, had the man thinking it. Not even Beast Miao King Yayul Cheok himself.
How is this possible?
Unable to hide his shock and confusion, the Beast Miao King stared at the back of the young man standing tall before the blazing hellfire.
Then a single sentence suddenly flashed through his mind.
When those things are gone, kill it immediately. No—just hurt it enough to leave it barely breathing.
At first, he had wondered what kind of nonsense the young man was spouting. Now that nonsense had become reality.
The Beast Miao King knew what he had to do.
Boom!
He shot toward the sky with a thunderous roar. He was half a beat late, but so was the Thousand-Year Spider, caught in a situation it could never have predicted.
—S-Siss?
Its many eyes, large and small, darted in different directions. The moment they found the Beast Miao King, they froze.
His few remaining hairs streamed behind him as he flew upward. A cold smile touched his lips.
“I’ve finally caught you. You piece of shit. I’ll tear you apart.”
The Thousand-Year Spider had made two fatal mistakes.
First, it had underestimated the young human’s strength.
Second, it had killed the old human’s tribespeople and shaved off the thick hair he had always been proud of.
Splaaash!
Its last desperate spray of slime cut through empty air. The Beast Miao King caught one of its legs.
Crack!
—Siiiiiiit!
The leg tore free. Screaming in pain, the Thousand-Year Spider plummeted toward the ground.

Slice!

Slice!

chapters.title: Chapter 640
paragraphs: One Annihilation was a technique that didn’t merely destroy its target. It erased it.
It drew out all my power in an instant, producing several times my usual strength. The greater my martial attainment, the more powerful One Annihilation became.
But it had one fatal drawback...
Beep. Beep. Beep-beep-beep!

System You have exhausted all your power! - Warning! Warning! The effects of overusing your abilities will rebound on you in full! - Status abnormality Internal Injury applied! - Status abnormality Exhaustion applied! - Status abnormality Anemia applied! - Status abnormality Paralyzed applied! - Due to the stacked status abnormalities, all stats temporarily decrease by 100!
As One Annihilation grew more powerful, its aftereffects grew more severe.
...Ah. Damn it.
My entire body trembled as though I’d been electrocuted. My once-clear vision blurred like a screen full of static.
Turning thousands of venomous beasts to ash had come at a steep price.
Still, I thought I’d at least level up once.
The higher my Level rose, the less EXP I gained.

Back when I had been a low-level nobody who could barely stand up to a single Peak Master, leveling up could cover for that weakness to some extent. But now that my vessel had grown larger, I needed far more EXP to fill it, and even leveling up had become difficult.
Internal Injury and Exhaustion weren’t enough. I had Anemia and paralysis, too. It was a miracle I hadn’t passed out.
I staggered, my vision swimming, and barely managed to drive White Flame into the ground.
Thud!
Leaning on my spear in this sorry state, I wished Jeok Cheongang had taught me the Dance of the Fire God and Demon. Not that there was any point begging him. I knew what he’d say.
The Dance of the Fire God and Demon? Is dying young your life’s ambition?
He said it was too dangerous, but really, the difference would be no greater than the one between a pistol and an automatic rifle.
To be honest, at this rate, I felt like I might die far from home using One Annihilation before then.
Not that I had the slightest intention of dying in a horrible place like this.
That’s why I took out insurance.
Just as I thought that, the insurance agent noticed his client’s accident and dropped out of the sky.
Whoooosh. Boom!
The heavily built old man landed on the Thousand-Year Spider, using its enormous, barely living, convulsing body as a cushion.
The Beast Miao King, his face flushed, spread both arms toward me.
“Uh, that’s really crossing the line—”
Grab! Crack!
“What an incredible bastard!”
“Argh! Aaaagh!”
“How did you do that? Was it the Fire Gate Clan’s unique martial art? Or the final ultimate technique Old Man Jeok learned?”
Whap! Whap!
“Uuuugh!”
“What a monster! I couldn’t believe it even while watching!”
“Aaaaaagh! You crazy bastard!”
“What? Crazy bastard? Yes! That’s exactly what you are—a madman born of the Central Plains!”
I nearly died far from home. I wasn’t joking.
When the madman born of Nanman finally let go of me, a mournful notification sounded in my ear.
Beep.
System Status abnormality Mild Ligament Tear applied! Strength decreases by 20 until recovery! Agility decreases by 20 until recovery!
This was why Doctor Octopus was a villain.
I didn’t have the strength to say anything else. Gasping through the pain, I glared at the Beast Miao King and barely managed to speak.
“Spider. Spider.”
“Spider? Oh, the Thousand-Year Spider?”
“Quick. Hurry.”
At my pitiful gestures, the Beast Miao King nodded in admiration.
“I wondered if that was what you meant, but are you planning to use the Thousand-Year Spider to figure out the Poisonblood Grounds? You really are something.”
“Ah, please.”
“Ha, all right. Just as you asked, I brought it here alive and unharmed—”
Before he could spout any more nonsense, I squeezed out what little strength I had left.
“Gnnngh!”
I wrenched White Flame free and drove it straight into the Thousand-Year Spider’s head, like a patient collecting a random insurance payout.
Thud!
—Ssssit! Kieeeek!
The monster gave a brief death cry. Then heavenly bells rang from somewhere.
Ding. Ding. Ding.

System You defeated Level 119 Thousand-Year Spider! - Additional EXP has been awarded for defeating a rare entity! - Level Up! - The damaged body has been substantially restored! - All status abnormalities have been removed! - Warning! Your physical condition is not yet perfect! A little treatment and rest are required!
Ah, this was why I took out insurance.
If the EXP from one venomous beast was an ant’s tear, the Thousand-Year Spider was a downpour from heaven.
Add its EXP to what I’d earned killing thousands of venomous beasts at once, and life immediately surged back into my dying body.
“Buuuurp.”
Last hit. Sweet.
As the ancient sages said, one Level Up made the five loaves and two fish look like nothing.
I couldn’t tell you which sage said it, but someone did. It was true, too.
Whew. I almost died.
Having barely made it back from the nursing home’s doorstep, I rubbed my stomach, feeling a satisfying fullness spread through my body.
Then I looked up and met the eyes of someone staring at me with a distinctly unimpressed expression.
“Why?”
“What is it?”
After a moment, the Beast Miao King spoke, his expression gone cold.
“Why did you tell me to keep it alive if you were going to do that?”
Why else? To get the EXP, obviously.
But years of working for a shitty small Guild had given me something I had never possessed before: social awareness and people skills.
I answered with a mournful, rigid expression.
“I wanted to take revenge with my own hands.”
“What?”
“For the Nanman warriors who died at the hands... no, the slime and webs of those bastards. Tearing them apart wouldn’t have been enough.”
The Beast Miao King’s eyes widened, emotion stirring in them. He stared at me, his gaze trembling, then spoke in a choked voice.
“I... don’t know what to say.”
“Shh. Don’t say anything. I already know.”
“You... you little bastard!”
What a romantic moment... Like hell. Fuck off. I was going to gag.
But one thing was certain: the Beast Miao King couldn’t hide how moved he was.
Well, the result’s good. That’s what matters, right?
I didn’t need to feel guilty. I genuinely mourned the Nanman warriors, and I genuinely needed the EXP to recover.
More importantly, my quick excuse had made things better.
If word of this gets around Nanman, maybe the odds of the Nanman Beast Palace joining the Murim Alliance will go up ten percent.
Even so, a weight remained in my chest.
I felt guilty because I hadn’t been able to prevent hundreds of people from being massacred less than two shichen away.
...Damn it.
A bitter taste filled my mouth.
Even now, countless people were probably dying across both the modern world and Murim. Some in traffic accidents. Some at the hands of monsters.
A martial artist might get into a quarrel at an inn, draw a sword, and die on the spot. Somewhere, a nameless hero might lose their life fighting an evildoer.
I knew I couldn’t save them all.
But I was human, and I hated seeing other people die.
And I felt regret, too. Regret that if I had been there, perhaps I could have saved innocent people.
Great power comes with great responsibility.
At some point, that line from a superhero movie had become a boulder weighing on my body and mind.
It weighed on me even while I circulated my qi, when I needed to give it my full concentration.
Maybe this is a Heart Demon, too.
I sighed softly, shook my head, and started walking again, leaving the Thousand-Year Spider’s corpse behind.
We headed deeper into the hidden reaches of the Poisonblood Grounds.
Splash. Splash.

The Beast Miao King and I watched our steps more carefully now. Killing five Thousand-Year Spiders and an enormous number of venomous beasts had left the area quiet, but it was too soon to let our guard down.
That bastard is the biggest problem of all.
Ailao Mountain’s Wraith.
The Black Tiger fit the name the System had given it perfectly. It was the one thing we had to watch for above all else.
Its enormous body moved like the wind. The powerful, eerie qi I’d sensed from it, however briefly, proved it was far beyond any ordinary spiritual creature or venomous beast.
—Where do you think it is now?
It was useful having someone beside me who was thinking the same thing. I moved my lips in answer to the Beast Miao King’s Sound Transmission.
—Who knows? But I’m sure it’s still in the Poisonblood Grounds.
—That’s what I don’t understand. Why lure us all this way and then fail to appear? Fifteen minutes ago, we would have been at a clear disadvantage.
He was right.

Despite their reputation, the five Thousand-Year Spiders had been easier to handle than I’d expected, and so had the thousands of venomous beasts. But if Ailao Mountain’s Wraith had joined them, things would have been different.
If it had joined the fight from the beginning, we could probably have put up a decent fight. But if it had appeared right after I used One Annihilation...
Even if we’d done everything right, it would have been a brutal fight.
Its teeth could withstand Force. It was unbelievably fast, and, true to its name, its presence was as impossible to sense as a wraith’s.
One of us might have died. Or left a limb behind.
At worst, we’d both be dead.
But why? Why didn’t it appear even under those circumstances?
I didn’t know. Only two remotely plausible explanations came to mind.
First, a classic island-nation plot twist:
Heh heh. The Thousand-Year Spider is merely the weakest of our Four Great Venomous Beasts.
And second:
Ailao Mountain’s Wraith has no intention of hurting us.
I took a few cautious steps and discarded the second theory. However I looked at it, it seemed too unlikely.
Before I could think any further, the Beast Miao King, who had been following behind and watching our flanks and rear, put his broad hand on my shoulder.
Tap.
Oh, shit.
That scared the hell out of me. My heart nearly fell out of my chest.
I steadied myself and turned to look where his finger was pointing.
Beyond the Poison Mist, growing thicker with every step, and the dark jungle crowding in on all sides, a faint, unfamiliar light shone through.
Could it be?
We didn’t need to say anything. My instincts had reached the answer before my thoughts had.
Rustle. Crackle.
We pushed through grass that carried a faint trace of poison and came to the source of the light.
At last, we saw what lay before us. Both of us stopped, mouths hanging open.
“This is...!”
A vast swamp lay under the faint moonlight.
Waiting there were countless shapes hanging, each bound tight in transparent spiderwebs—and white eggs.
